It is a [[Beppyo shrine]], or a shrine that is particularly notable in a certain way with a significant history to it.{{Cite web|title=Learn about Oyama Afuri Shrine - Oyama Afuri Shrine|url=https://www.afuri.or.jp/en/about/|access-date=2024-03-29|language=en-US}}{{Cite web|date=2023-12-28|title=Oyama Afuri Shrine|url=https://www.afuri.or.jp/en/|access-date=2024-03-29|language=en-US}}{{Cite web|date=2013-04-07|title=Afuri Shrine on Mt. Oyama - Kanagawa|url=https://en.japantravel.com/kanagawa/afuri-shrine-on-mt-oyama/4043|access-date=2024-03-29|website=JapanTravel|language=en}} '''{{ill|Oyama Afuri Shrine|ja|大山阿夫利神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}''' (Oyama Afuri Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} located in {{ill|Isehara City|ja|伊勢原市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Kanagawa Prefecture|ja|神奈川県|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, situated on {{ill|Oyama|ja|大山|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (also known as '''Amefuri-yama'''〈{{ill|Amefuri-yama|ja|雨降山|qq=draft|qq=draft}}〉). It is recorded in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|qq=draft|qq=draft}} from the {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式|qq=draft|qq=draft}} period (Enchō 5, {{ill|927|ja|927th year|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) as one of the thirteen shrines (small shrines) of the {{ill|Engishiki-shiki Naishinsha Jūsansha|ja|延喜式内社十三社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in {{ill|Sagami Province|ja|相模国|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Under the [[Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines]], it was classified as a prefectural shrine (Ken-sha) and is currently designated as a [[Beppyo Shrine|Beppyo shrine]] by the {{ill|Jinja Honchō|ja|神社本庁|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. The shrine is composed of two parts: the main shrine (honsha), which includes the inner shrine (okusha) and the front shrine (zensha) located at the summit of Oyama, and the lower shrine (gesha) located on the mid-slope.[http://www.afuri.or.jp/about/map/]{{ill|About Oyama Afuri Shrine|ja|大山阿夫利神社について：境内のご案内|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Official site of Oyama Afuri Shrine). The lower shrine is accessible via the {{ill|Oyama Cable Car|ja|大山ケーブルカー|qq=draft|qq=draft}} operated by {{ill|Oyama Kankō Dentetsu|ja|大山観光電鉄|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. == History == [[File:Pilgrims at the Roben waterfall, Oyama.jpg|thumb|left|245px|“Ōyama Sekison Raben-taki no Zu” by {{ill|Utagawa Kuniyoshi|ja|歌川国芳|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Art name: Ichiyūsai), painted circa 1819–1820 (Bunsei 2–3). Men praying at the waterfall of Ōyama Sekison (current Oyama Afuri Shrine).]] {{ill|Oyama|ja|大山|qq=draft|qq=draft}} has long been revered as an object of mountain worship. Excavations at its summit have uncovered {{ill|Jomon pottery|ja|縄文土器|qq=draft|qq=draft}} used in rituals.[http://www.afuri.or.jp/about/]{{ill|About Oyama Afuri Shrine|ja|大山阿夫利神社について|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Official site of Oyama Afuri Shrine) It is also known as “{{ill|Amefuri-yama|ja|雨降山|qq=draft|qq=draft}}” because clouds and mist frequently gather at the summit, which are believed to bring rain, and it was revered as a rain-making deity. In addition, worship of a giant stone ({{ill|Iwa-za|ja|磐座|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) at the summit and of the twin waterfalls on the mountainside as sacred water sources is also observed.[[宝賀寿男]], “Section 3: The Early Branches of Clans in Kinai and Tōkoku – Part 2: Musashi no Kuni no Kunizukuri and the Provincial Clans of Tōkoku”, in “Studies on Ancient Clans, No. 16: The Rise and Fall of the Izumo Kingdom” (青垣出版, 2020), pp.263–264. According to tradition, Ōyama Afuri Shrine was founded during the reign of {{ill|Sujin-tennō|ja|崇神天皇|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (around the 3rd century BC, though this is considered legendary rather than historical). The {{ill|Engishiki-shiki Shinnamōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, compiled during the Engishiki period, records the shrine as “Afuri Shrine” in its 5th year ({{ill|927|ja|927th year|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) and classifies it as a minor shrine among the thirteen shrines of the {{ill|Engishiki-shiki Naishinsha Jūsansha|ja|延喜式内社十三社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in {{ill|Sagami Province|ja|相模国|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. [[simple:user:immanuelle/Oyama Afuri Shrine]] == Enshrined Deities == * The primary deity enshrined at the lower shrine is {{ill|Ōyamatsumi|ja|大山祇神|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Ōyamatsumi-no-kami). * The main shrine enshrines {{ill|Ōyamatsumi|ja|大山祇神|qq=draft|qq=draft}} as its principal deity (prior to the Shinto-Buddhism separation, he was revered as {{ill|Sekison Daigongen|ja|石尊大権現|qq=draft|qq=draft}}). * The subsidiary shrine (oku-sha) enshrines {{ill|Raijin|ja|大雷神|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Ōi-katsuchi-no-kami; known as {{ill|Ōtengu|ja|大天狗|qq=draft|qq=draft}} during the syncretic period). * The subsidiary shrine (zen-sha) enshrines {{ill|Takaokami|ja|高龗神|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Takaokami; known as {{ill|Kotenko|ja|小天狗|qq=draft|qq=draft}} during the syncretic period). This arrangement—enshrining Ōyamatsumi along with the subsidiary deities Raijin and Takaokami—is identical to that of the shrine in {{ill|Ehime Prefecture|ja|愛媛県|qq=draft|qq=draft}} known as {{ill|Ōyamatsumi Shrine|ja|大山祇神社|1=Ōyamazumi Shrine|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, although these deities were enshrined only after the separation of Shinto and Buddhism in the Meiji period. During the Edo period, when Shinto and Buddhism were syncretized, the main shrine originally enshrined {{ill|Sekison Daigongen|ja|石尊大権現|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, as the sacred stone ({{ill|Reisekki|ja|霊石|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) at the summit served as his manifestation. In the subsidiary shrines, {{ill|Ōtengu|ja|大天狗|qq=draft|qq=draft}} was enshrined in the oku-sha and {{ill|Kotenko|ja|小天狗|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in the zen-sha. == Cultural Importance == === Oyama Pilgrimage === During the Edo period the Oyama Pilgrimage was a tradition where worshippers formed groups ("{{ill|Kō (lecture)|lt=Kō|en|qq=draft|qq=draft}}") to visit the shrine. This pilgrimage, coupled with the "Oyama Kaido" pathway played a role in shaping culture by inspiring rakugo stories and ukiyo e artworks. In 2008 this pilgrimage was designated as a Heritage Site due to its cultural significance. === Osamedachi Tradition === A tradition stemming from a tale about Minamoto no Yoritomo offering a sword to the shrine the Osamedachi custom involves presenting swords that can reach lengths of up to 6 meters. === Kagura Dance === Imported from Kasuga Taisha Shrine during the Meiji era the Kagura dance performed at Oyama Afuri Shrine includes dances by boys (Yamato Mai) and girls (Miko dance) spanning age groups, from elementary school students to adults. The Sendoshi Ryokan originally built to host worshippers has transformed into an inn that provides lodging and dining services. It stands as one of the temple accommodations, in Japan. As for the Oyama Noh tradition it reflects the shrines commitment to peace and harmony tracing its origins back, to the Genroku era. This tradition signifies the bond established among the leaders of Mt. Oyama through their embrace of Noh performances. == Access == === To the Lower Shrine === ; Public Transportation * From the north exit of the {{ill|Odakyu Odawara Line|ja|小田急小田原線|qq=draft|qq=draft}} at {{ill|Isehara Station|ja|伊勢原駅|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, take Bus Route 10 operated by {{ill|Kanagawa Chūō Kōtsū|ja|神奈川中央交通西|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, alight at the final stop ("Ōyama Cable" bound), which takes approximately 25 minutes. *** Then walk about 15 minutes (approximately 600 meters) from the Ōyama Cable Car Station. ; By Car * Accessible via the {{ill|Shin-Tōmei Expressway|ja|新東名高速道路|qq=draft|qq=draft}} at the {{ill|Isehara Ōyama Interchange|ja|伊勢原大山インターチェンジ|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, then via {{ill|Kanagawa Prefectural Road 611|ja|神奈川県道611号大山板戸線|qq=draft|qq=draft}}; municipal parking is available (about a 15-minute walk from the parking lot to the Ōyama Cable Car Station). === To the Main Shrine === * Ascend the mountain It is a [[Beppyo shrine]], or a shrine that is particularly notable in a certain way with a significant history to it.{{Cite web|title=Learn about Oyama Afuri Shrine - Oyama Afuri Shrine|url=https://www.afuri.or.jp/en/about/|access-date=2024-03-29|language=en-US}}{{Cite web|date=2023-12-28|title=Oyama Afuri Shrine|url=https://www.afuri.or.jp/en/|access-date=2024-03-29|language=en-US}}{{Cite web|date=2013-04-07|title=Afuri Shrine on Mt. Oyama - Kanagawa|url=https://en.japantravel.com/kanagawa/afuri-shrine-on-mt-oyama/4043|access-date=2024-03-29|website=JapanTravel|language=en}} '''{{ill|Oyama Afuri Shrine|ja|大山阿夫利神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}''' (Oyama Afuri Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} located in {{ill|Isehara City|ja|伊勢原市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Kanagawa Prefecture|ja|神奈川県|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, situated on {{ill|Oyama|ja|大山|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (also known as '''Amefuri-yama'''〈{{ill|Amefuri-yama|ja|雨降山|qq=draft|qq=draft}}〉). It is recorded in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|qq=draft|qq=draft}} from the {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式|qq=draft|qq=draft}} period (Enchō 5, {{ill|927|ja|927th year|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) as one of the thirteen shrines (small shrines) of the {{ill|Engishiki-shiki Naishinsha Jūsansha|ja|延喜式内社十三社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in {{ill|Sagami Province|ja|相模国|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Under the [[Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines]], it was classified as a prefectural shrine (Ken-sha) and is currently designated as a [[Beppyo Shrine|Beppyo shrine]] by the {{ill|Jinja Honchō|ja|神社本庁|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. The shrine is composed of two parts: the main shrine (honsha), which includes the inner shrine (okusha) and the front shrine (zensha) located at the summit of Oyama, and the lower shrine (gesha) located on the mid-slope.[http://www.afuri.or.jp/about/map/]{{ill|About Oyama Afuri Shrine|ja|大山阿夫利神社について：境内のご案内|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Official site of Oyama Afuri Shrine). The lower shrine is accessible via the {{ill|Oyama Cable Car|ja|大山ケーブルカー|qq=draft|qq=draft}} operated by {{ill|Oyama Kankō Dentetsu|ja|大山観光電鉄|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. == History == [[File:Pilgrims at the Roben waterfall, Oyama.jpg|thumb|left|245px|“Ōyama Sekison Raben-taki no Zu” by {{ill|Utagawa Kuniyoshi|ja|歌川国芳|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Art name: Ichiyūsai), painted circa 1819–1820 (Bunsei 2–3). Men praying at the waterfall of Ōyama Sekison (current Oyama Afuri Shrine).]] {{ill|Oyama|ja|大山|qq=draft|qq=draft}} has long been revered as an object of mountain worship. Excavations at its summit have uncovered {{ill|Jomon pottery|ja|縄文土器|qq=draft|qq=draft}} used in rituals.[http://www.afuri.or.jp/about/]{{ill|About Oyama Afuri Shrine|ja|大山阿夫利神社について|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Official site of Oyama Afuri Shrine) It is also known as “{{ill|Amefuri-yama|ja|雨降山|qq=draft|qq=draft}}” because clouds and mist frequently gather at the summit, which are believed to bring rain, and it was revered as a rain-making deity. In addition, worship of a giant stone ({{ill|Iwa-za|ja|磐座|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) at the summit and of the twin waterfalls on the mountainside as sacred water sources is also observed.[[宝賀寿男]], “Section 3: The Early Branches of Clans in Kinai and Tōkoku – Part 2: Musashi no Kuni no Kunizukuri and the Provincial Clans of Tōkoku”, in “Studies on Ancient Clans, No. 16: The Rise and Fall of the Izumo Kingdom” (青垣出版, 2020), pp.263–264. According to tradition, Ōyama Afuri Shrine was founded during the reign of {{ill|Sujin-tennō|ja|崇神天皇|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (around the 3rd century BC, though this is considered legendary rather than historical). The {{ill|Engishiki-shiki Shinnamōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, compiled during the Engishiki period, records the shrine as “Afuri Shrine” in its 5th year ({{ill|927|ja|927th year|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) and classifies it as a minor shrine among the thirteen shrines of the {{ill|Engishiki-shiki Naishinsha Jūsansha|ja|延喜式内社十三社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in {{ill|Sagami Province|ja|相模国|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. [[simple:user:immanuelle/Oyama Afuri Shrine]] == Enshrined Deities == * The primary deity enshrined at the lower shrine is {{ill|Ōyamatsumi|ja|大山祇神|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Ōyamatsumi-no-kami). * The main shrine enshrines {{ill|Ōyamatsumi|ja|大山祇神|qq=draft|qq=draft}} as its principal deity (prior to the Shinto-Buddhism separation, he was revered as {{ill|Sekison Daigongen|ja|石尊大権現|qq=draft|qq=draft}}). * The subsidiary shrine (oku-sha) enshrines {{ill|Raijin|ja|大雷神|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Ōi-katsuchi-no-kami; known as {{ill|Ōtengu|ja|大天狗|qq=draft|qq=draft}} during the syncretic period). * The subsidiary shrine (zen-sha) enshrines {{ill|Takaokami|ja|高龗神|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Takaokami; known as {{ill|Kotenko|ja|小天狗|qq=draft|qq=draft}} during the syncretic period). This arrangement—enshrining Ōyamatsumi along with the subsidiary deities Raijin and Takaokami—is identical to that of the shrine in {{ill|Ehime Prefecture|ja|愛媛県|qq=draft|qq=draft}} known as {{ill|Ōyamatsumi Shrine|ja|大山祇神社|1=Ōyamazumi Shrine|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, although these deities were enshrined only after the separation of Shinto and Buddhism in the Meiji period. During the Edo period, when Shinto and Buddhism were syncretized, the main shrine originally enshrined {{ill|Sekison Daigongen|ja|石尊大権現|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, as the sacred stone ({{ill|Reisekki|ja|霊石|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) at the summit served as his manifestation. In the subsidiary shrines, {{ill|Ōtengu|ja|大天狗|qq=draft|qq=draft}} was enshrined in the oku-sha and {{ill|Kotenko|ja|小天狗|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in the zen-sha. == Cultural Importance == === Oyama Pilgrimage === During the Edo period the Oyama Pilgrimage was a tradition where worshippers formed groups ("{{ill|Kō (lecture)|lt=Kō|en|qq=draft|qq=draft}}") to visit the shrine. This pilgrimage, coupled with the "Oyama Kaido" pathway played a role in shaping culture by inspiring rakugo stories and ukiyo e artworks. In 2008 this pilgrimage was designated as a Heritage Site due to its cultural significance. === Osamedachi Tradition === A tradition stemming from a tale about Minamoto no Yoritomo offering a sword to the shrine the Osamedachi custom involves presenting swords that can reach lengths of up to 6 meters. === Kagura Dance === Imported from Kasuga Taisha Shrine during the Meiji era the Kagura dance performed at Oyama Afuri Shrine includes dances by boys (Yamato Mai) and girls (Miko dance) spanning age groups, from elementary school students to adults. The Sendoshi Ryokan originally built to host worshippers has transformed into an inn that provides lodging and dining services. It stands as one of the temple accommodations, in Japan. As for the Oyama Noh tradition it reflects the shrines commitment to peace and harmony tracing its origins back, to the Genroku era. This tradition signifies the bond established among the leaders of Mt. Oyama through their embrace of Noh performances. == Access == === To the Lower Shrine === ; Public Transportation * From the north exit of the {{ill|Odakyu Odawara Line|ja|小田急小田原線|qq=draft|qq=draft}} at {{ill|Isehara Station|ja|伊勢原駅|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, take Bus Route 10 operated by {{ill|Kanagawa Chūō Kōtsū|ja|神奈川中央交通西|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, alight at the final stop ("Ōyama Cable" bound), which takes approximately 25 minutes. *** Then walk about 15 minutes (approximately 600 meters) from the Ōyama Cable Car Station. ; By Car * Accessible via the {{ill|Shin-Tōmei Expressway|ja|新東名高速道路|qq=draft|qq=draft}} at the {{ill|Isehara Ōyama Interchange|ja|伊勢原大山インターチェンジ|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, then via {{ill|Kanagawa Prefectural Road 611|ja|神奈川県道611号大山板戸線|qq=draft|qq=draft}}; municipal parking is available (about a 15-minute walk from the parking lot to the Ōyama Cable Car Station). === To the Main Shrine === * Ascend the mountain Oyama - Kanagawa|url=https://en.japantravel.com/kanagawa/afuri-shrine-on-mt-oyama/4043|access-date=2024-03-29|website=JapanTravel|language=en}} '''{{ill|Oyama Afuri Shrine|ja|大山阿夫利神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}''' (Oyama Afuri Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} located in {{ill|Isehara City|ja|伊勢原市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Kanagawa Prefecture|ja|神奈川県|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, situated on {{ill|Oyama|ja|大山|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (also known as '''Amefuri-yama'''〈{{ill|Amefuri-yama|ja|雨降山|qq=draft|qq=draft}}〉). It is recorded in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|qq=draft|qq=draft}} from the {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式|qq=draft|qq=draft}} period (Enchō 5, {{ill|927|ja|927th year|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) as one of the thirteen shrines (small shrines) of the {{ill|Engishiki-shiki Naishinsha Jūsansha|ja|延喜式内社十三社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in {{ill|Sagami Province|ja|相模国|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Under the [[Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines]], it was classified as a prefectural shrine (Ken-sha) and is currently designated as a [[Beppyo Shrine|Beppyo shrine]] by the {{ill|Jinja Honchō|ja|神社本庁|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. The shrine is composed of two parts: the main shrine (honsha), which includes the inner shrine (okusha) and the front shrine (zensha) located at the summit of Oyama, and the lower shrine (gesha) located on the mid-slope.[http://www.afuri.or.jp/about/map/]{{ill|About Oyama Afuri Shrine|ja|大山阿夫利神社について：境内のご案内|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Official site of Oyama Afuri Shrine). The lower shrine is accessible via the {{ill|Oyama Cable Car|ja|大山ケーブルカー|qq=draft|qq=draft}} operated by {{ill|Oyama Kankō Dentetsu|ja|大山観光電鉄|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. == History == [[File:Pilgrims at the Roben waterfall, Oyama.jpg|thumb|left|245px|“Ōyama Sekison Raben-taki no Zu” by {{ill|Utagawa Kuniyoshi|ja|歌川国芳|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Art name: Ichiyūsai), painted circa 1819–1820 (Bunsei 2–3). Men praying at the waterfall of Ōyama Sekison (current Oyama Afuri Shrine).]] {{ill|Oyama|ja|大山|qq=draft|qq=draft}} has long been revered as an object of mountain worship. Excavations at its summit have uncovered {{ill|Jomon pottery|ja|縄文土器|qq=draft|qq=draft}} used in rituals.[http://www.afuri.or.jp/about/]{{ill|About Oyama Afuri Shrine|ja|大山阿夫利神社について|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Official site of Oyama Afuri Shrine) It is also known as “{{ill|Amefuri-yama|ja|雨降山|qq=draft|qq=draft}}” because clouds and mist frequently gather at the summit, which are believed to bring rain, and it was revered as a rain-making deity. In addition, worship of a giant stone ({{ill|Iwa-za|ja|磐座|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) at the summit and of the twin waterfalls on the mountainside as sacred water sources is also observed.[[宝賀寿男]], “Section 3: The Early Branches of Clans in Kinai and Tōkoku – Part 2: Musashi no Kuni no Kunizukuri and the Provincial Clans of Tōkoku”, in “Studies on Ancient Clans, No. 16: The Rise and Fall of the Izumo Kingdom” (青垣出版, 2020), pp.263–264. According to tradition, Ōyama Afuri Shrine was founded during the reign of {{ill|Sujin-tennō|ja|崇神天皇|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (around the 3rd century BC, though this is considered legendary rather than historical). The {{ill|Engishiki-shiki Shinnamōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, compiled during the Engishiki period, records the shrine as “Afuri Shrine” in its 5th year ({{ill|927|ja|927th year|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) and classifies it as a minor shrine among the thirteen shrines of the {{ill|Engishiki-shiki Naishinsha Jūsansha|ja|延喜式内社十三社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in {{ill|Sagami Province|ja|相模国|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. [[simple:user:immanuelle/Oyama Afuri Shrine]] == Enshrined Deities == * The primary deity enshrined at the lower shrine is {{ill|Ōyamatsumi|ja|大山祇神|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Ōyamatsumi-no-kami). * The main shrine enshrines {{ill|Ōyamatsumi|ja|大山祇神|qq=draft|qq=draft}} as its principal deity (prior to the Shinto-Buddhism separation, he was revered as {{ill|Sekison Daigongen|ja|石尊大権現|qq=draft|qq=draft}}). * The subsidiary shrine (oku-sha) enshrines {{ill|Raijin|ja|大雷神|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Ōi-katsuchi-no-kami; known as {{ill|Ōtengu|ja|大天狗|qq=draft|qq=draft}} during the syncretic period). * The subsidiary shrine (zen-sha) enshrines {{ill|Takaokami|ja|高龗神|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Takaokami; known as {{ill|Kotenko|ja|小天狗|qq=draft|qq=draft}} during the syncretic period). This arrangement—enshrining Ōyamatsumi along with the subsidiary deities Raijin and Takaokami—is identical to that of the shrine in {{ill|Ehime Prefecture|ja|愛媛県|qq=draft|qq=draft}} known as {{ill|Ōyamatsumi Shrine|ja|大山祇神社|1=Ōyamazumi Shrine|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, although these deities were enshrined only after the separation of Shinto and Buddhism in the Meiji period. During the Edo period, when Shinto and Buddhism were syncretized, the main shrine originally enshrined {{ill|Sekison Daigongen|ja|石尊大権現|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, as the sacred stone ({{ill|Reisekki|ja|霊石|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) at the summit served as his manifestation. In the subsidiary shrines, {{ill|Ōtengu|ja|大天狗|qq=draft|qq=draft}} was enshrined in the oku-sha and {{ill|Kotenko|ja|小天狗|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in the zen-sha. == Cultural Importance == === Oyama Pilgrimage === During the Edo period the Oyama Pilgrimage was a tradition where worshippers formed groups ("{{ill|Kō (lecture)|lt=Kō|en|qq=draft|qq=draft}}") to visit the shrine. This pilgrimage, coupled with the "Oyama Kaido" pathway played a role in shaping culture by inspiring rakugo stories and ukiyo e artworks. In 2008 this pilgrimage was designated as a Heritage Site due to its cultural significance. === Osamedachi Tradition === A tradition stemming from a tale about Minamoto no Yoritomo offering a sword to the shrine the Osamedachi custom involves presenting swords that can reach lengths of up to 6 meters. === Kagura Dance === Imported from Kasuga Taisha Shrine during the Meiji era the Kagura dance performed at Oyama Afuri Shrine includes dances by boys (Yamato Mai) and girls (Miko dance) spanning age groups, from elementary school students to adults. The Sendoshi Ryokan originally built to host worshippers has transformed into an inn that provides lodging and dining services. It stands as one of the temple accommodations, in Japan. As for the Oyama Noh tradition it reflects the shrines commitment to peace and harmony tracing its origins back, to the Genroku era. This tradition signifies the bond established among the leaders of Mt. Oyama through their embrace of Noh performances. == Access == === To the Lower Shrine === ; Public Transportation * From the north exit of the {{ill|Odakyu Odawara Line|ja|小田急小田原線|qq=draft|qq=draft}} at {{ill|Isehara Station|ja|伊勢原駅|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, take Bus Route 10 operated by {{ill|Kanagawa Chūō Kōtsū|ja|神奈川中央交通西|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, alight at the final stop ("Ōyama Cable" bound), which takes approximately 25 minutes. *** Then walk about 15 minutes (approximately 600 meters) from the Ōyama Cable Car Station. ; By Car * Accessible via the {{ill|Shin-Tōmei Expressway|ja|新東名高速道路|qq=draft|qq=draft}} at the {{ill|Isehara Ōyama Interchange|ja|伊勢原大山インターチェンジ|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, then via {{ill|Kanagawa Prefectural Road 611|ja|神奈川県道611号大山板戸線|qq=draft|qq=draft}}; municipal parking is available (about a 15-minute walk from the parking lot to the Ōyama Cable Car Station). === To the Main Shrine === * Ascend the mountain Oyama - Kanagawa|url=https://en.japantravel.com/kanagawa/afuri-shrine-on-mt-oyama/4043|access-date=2024-03-29|website=JapanTravel|language=en}} '''{{ill|Oyama Afuri Shrine|ja|大山阿夫利神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}''' (Oyama Afuri Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} located in {{ill|Isehara City|ja|伊勢原市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Kanagawa Prefecture|ja|神奈川県|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, situated on {{ill|Oyama|ja|大山|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (also known as '''Amefuri-yama'''〈{{ill|Amefuri-yama|ja|雨降山|qq=draft|qq=draft}}〉). It is recorded in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|qq=draft|qq=draft}} from the {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式|qq=draft|qq=draft}} period (Enchō 5, {{ill|927|ja|927th year|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) as one of the thirteen shrines (small shrines) of the {{ill|Engishiki-shiki Naishinsha Jūsansha|ja|延喜式内社十三社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in {{ill|Sagami Province|ja|相模国|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Under the [[Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines]], it was classified as a prefectural shrine (Ken-sha) and is currently designated as a [[Beppyo Shrine|Beppyo shrine]] by the {{ill|Jinja Honchō|ja|神社本庁|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. The shrine is composed of two parts: the main shrine (honsha), which includes the inner shrine (okusha) and the front shrine (zensha) located at the summit of Oyama, and the lower shrine (gesha) located on the mid-slope.[http://www.afuri.or.jp/about/map/]{{ill|About Oyama Afuri Shrine|ja|大山阿夫利神社について：境内のご案内|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Official site of Oyama Afuri Shrine). The lower shrine is accessible via the {{ill|Oyama Cable Car|ja|大山ケーブルカー|qq=draft|qq=draft}} operated by {{ill|Oyama Kankō Dentetsu|ja|大山観光電鉄|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. == History == [[File:Pilgrims at the Roben waterfall, Oyama.jpg|thumb|left|245px|“Ōyama Sekison Raben-taki no Zu” by {{ill|Utagawa Kuniyoshi|ja|歌川国芳|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Art name: Ichiyūsai), painted circa 1819–1820 (Bunsei 2–3). Men praying at the waterfall of Ōyama Sekison (current Oyama Afuri Shrine).]] {{ill|Oyama|ja|大山|qq=draft|qq=draft}} has long been revered as an object of mountain worship. Excavations at its summit have uncovered {{ill|Jomon pottery|ja|縄文土器|qq=draft|qq=draft}} used in rituals.[http://www.afuri.or.jp/about/]{{ill|About Oyama Afuri Shrine|ja|大山阿夫利神社について|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Official site of Oyama Afuri Shrine) It is also known as “{{ill|Amefuri-yama|ja|雨降山|qq=draft|qq=draft}}” because clouds and mist frequently gather at the summit, which are believed to bring rain, and it was revered as a rain-making deity. In addition, worship of a giant stone ({{ill|Iwa-za|ja|磐座|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) at the summit and of the twin waterfalls on the mountainside as sacred water sources is also observed.[[宝賀寿男]], “Section 3: The Early Branches of Clans in Kinai and Tōkoku – Part 2: Musashi no Kuni no Kunizukuri and the Provincial Clans of Tōkoku”, in “Studies on Ancient Clans, No. 16: The Rise and Fall of the Izumo Kingdom” (青垣出版, 2020), pp.263–264. According to tradition, Ōyama Afuri Shrine was founded during the reign of {{ill|Sujin-tennō|ja|崇神天皇|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (around the 3rd century BC, though this is considered legendary rather than historical). The {{ill|Engishiki-shiki Shinnamōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, compiled during the Engishiki period, records the shrine as “Afuri Shrine” in its 5th year ({{ill|927|ja|927th year|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) and classifies it as a minor shrine among the thirteen shrines of the {{ill|Engishiki-shiki Naishinsha Jūsansha|ja|延喜式内社十三社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in {{ill|Sagami Province|ja|相模国|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. [[simple:user:immanuelle/Oyama Afuri Shrine]] == Enshrined Deities == * The primary deity enshrined at the lower shrine is {{ill|Ōyamatsumi|ja|大山祇神|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Ōyamatsumi-no-kami). * The main shrine enshrines {{ill|Ōyamatsumi|ja|大山祇神|qq=draft|qq=draft}} as its principal deity (prior to the Shinto-Buddhism separation, he was revered as {{ill|Sekison Daigongen|ja|石尊大権現|qq=draft|qq=draft}}). * The subsidiary shrine (oku-sha) enshrines {{ill|Raijin|ja|大雷神|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Ōi-katsuchi-no-kami; known as {{ill|Ōtengu|ja|大天狗|qq=draft|qq=draft}} during the syncretic period). * The subsidiary shrine (zen-sha) enshrines {{ill|Takaokami|ja|高龗神|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Takaokami; known as {{ill|Kotenko|ja|小天狗|qq=draft|qq=draft}} during the syncretic period). This arrangement—enshrining Ōyamatsumi along with the subsidiary deities Raijin and Takaokami—is identical to that of the shrine in {{ill|Ehime Prefecture|ja|愛媛県|qq=draft|qq=draft}} known as {{ill|Ōyamatsumi Shrine|ja|大山祇神社|1=Ōyamazumi Shrine|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, although these deities were enshrined only after the separation of Shinto and Buddhism in the Meiji period. During the Edo period, when Shinto and Buddhism were syncretized, the main shrine originally enshrined {{ill|Sekison Daigongen|ja|石尊大権現|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, as the sacred stone ({{ill|Reisekki|ja|霊石|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) at the summit served as his manifestation. In the subsidiary shrines, {{ill|Ōtengu|ja|大天狗|qq=draft|qq=draft}} was enshrined in the oku-sha and {{ill|Kotenko|ja|小天狗|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in the zen-sha. == Cultural Importance == === Oyama Pilgrimage === During the Edo period the Oyama Pilgrimage was a tradition where worshippers formed groups ("{{ill|Kō (lecture)|lt=Kō|en|qq=draft|qq=draft}}") to visit the shrine. This pilgrimage, coupled with the "Oyama Kaido" pathway played a role in shaping culture by inspiring rakugo stories and ukiyo e artworks. In 2008 this pilgrimage was designated as a Heritage Site due to its cultural significance. === Osamedachi Tradition === A tradition stemming from a tale about Minamoto no Yoritomo offering a sword to the shrine the Osamedachi custom involves presenting swords that can reach lengths of up to 6 meters. === Kagura Dance === Imported from Kasuga Taisha Shrine during the Meiji era the Kagura dance performed at Oyama Afuri Shrine includes dances by boys (Yamato Mai) and girls (Miko dance) spanning age groups, from elementary school students to adults. The Sendoshi Ryokan originally built to host worshippers has transformed into an inn that provides lodging and dining services. It stands as one of the temple accommodations, in Japan. As for the Oyama Noh tradition it reflects the shrines commitment to peace and harmony tracing its origins back, to the Genroku era. This tradition signifies the bond established among the leaders of Mt. Oyama through their embrace of Noh performances. == Access == === To the Lower Shrine === ; Public Transportation * From the north exit of the {{ill|Odakyu Odawara Line|ja|小田急小田原線|qq=draft|qq=draft}} at {{ill|Isehara Station|ja|伊勢原駅|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, take Bus Route 10 operated by {{ill|Kanagawa Chūō Kōtsū|ja|神奈川中央交通西|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, alight at the final stop ("Ōyama Cable" bound), which takes approximately 25 minutes. *** Then walk about 15 minutes (approximately 600 meters) from the Ōyama Cable Car Station. ; By Car * Accessible via the {{ill|Shin-Tōmei Expressway|ja|新東名高速道路|qq=draft|qq=draft}} at the {{ill|Isehara Ōyama Interchange|ja|伊勢原大山インターチェンジ|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, then via {{ill|Kanagawa Prefectural Road 611|ja|神奈川県道611号大山板戸線|qq=draft|qq=draft}}; municipal parking is available (about a 15-minute walk from the parking lot to the Ōyama Cable Car Station). === To the Main Shrine === * Ascend the mountain }} {{osm box|w|161550990}} [[File:大山道.png|thumb|right|260px|大山道(主要8道)]] '''大山阿夫利神社'''（おおやまあふりじんじゃ）は、[[神奈川県]][[伊勢原市]]の[[大山 (神奈川県)|大山]]（別名: '''雨降山'''〈あふりやま〉）にある[[神社]]である。[[延長 (元号)|延長]]5年（[[927年]]）の『[[延喜式神名帳]]』に記載されている[[相模国]]の[[相模国の式内社一覧|延喜式内社十三社]]の内の一社（小社）で、[[近代社格制度|旧社格]]では[[県社]]に列している（現・[[神社本庁]]の[[別表神社]]）。 大山の山頂に鎮座する'''本社'''（奥社・前社含む）と中腹に鎮座する'''下社'''があり[http://www.afuri.or.jp/about/map/ 大山阿夫利神社について：境内のご案内]（大山阿夫利神社公式サイト）、下社までは[[大山観光電鉄大山鋼索線|大山ケーブルカー]]でアクセス可能である（[[#交通アクセス]]も参照）。 == 祭神 == 下社主祭神は、[[オオヤマツミ|大山祇神]]（おおやまつみのかみ）。 本社主祭神に、[[オオヤマツミ|大山祇神]]（おおやまつみのかみ、神仏分離前は[[石尊大権現]]）。 摂社の奥社祭神に、[[雷神|大雷神]]（おおいかつちのかみ、神仏分離前は[[大天狗]]）。 摂社の前社祭神に、[[淤加美神|高龗神]]（たかおかみ、神仏分離前は[[烏天狗|小天狗]]）。 主祭神の大山祇神に摂社として雷神と高龗神の2神を配するのは愛媛県の[[大山祇神社]]と同じ構成であるが、これらは[[明治]]になってから[[神仏分離]]の際に祀られるようになったものであり、[[江戸時代|江戸期]]以前の[[神仏習合]]時代には、本社には本来の[[祭神]]である[[石尊大権現]]（せきそんだいごんげん、山頂で[[霊石]]が祀られていたことからこう呼ばれた）が祀られていた。また摂社では、奥社に[[大天狗]]、前社に[[烏天狗|小天狗]]が祀られていた。 == 歴史 == [[File:Pilgrims at the Roben waterfall, Oyama.jpg|thumb|left|245px|「大山石尊良辧瀧之図」 [[歌川国芳]]（[[号 (称号)|画号]]: 一勇斎）筆、1819-20年（[[文政]]2-3年）。大山石尊（現・大山阿夫利神社）の滝に参拝する男達。]] [[大山 (神奈川県)|大山]]は古くから[[山岳信仰]]の対象として知られ、山頂からは祭祀に使われたとされる[[縄文土器]]が発掘されるなどしている[http://www.afuri.or.jp/about/ 大山阿夫利神社について]（大山阿夫利神社公式サイト）。大山は山上によく雲や霧が生じて雨を降らすことが多いとされたことから、「'''あめふり（あふり）山'''」とも呼ばれ、[[雨乞い]]の対象としても知られていた。また、山頂の自然石を[[神体]]とする巨石崇拝（[[磐座]]）と山腹の二重滝を崇拝する[[湧水]]地信仰も見られる[[宝賀寿男]]「第三部 畿内・東国に展開した初期分岐の支族　二 武蔵国造と東国の諸国造族」『古代氏族の研究⑯　出雲氏・土師氏 原出雲王国の盛衰』青垣出版、2020年、263、264頁。。 大山阿夫利神社は、社伝によると[[崇神天皇]]の御代崇神天皇の御代は西暦の[[3世紀]]ごろに相当すると考えられている。もっとも、社伝と史実は多分に別儀である事をここに特記しておく。に創建されたとされる。[[延長 (元号)|延長]]5年（[[927年]]）の『[[延喜式神名帳]]』では「'''阿夫利神社'''」と記載され、小社に列している。 [[天平勝宝]]4年（西暦[[752年]]）、[[良弁]]により[[神宮寺]]として雨降山[[大山寺 (伊勢原市)|大山寺]]が建立され、本尊として[[不動明王]]が祀られた。以後、[[神仏習合]]が続く。 [[中世]]以降は大山寺を拠点とする[[修験道]]（大山修験）が盛んになり、[[源頼朝]]を始め、[[北条氏]]・[[徳川氏]]など、武家の崇敬を受けた。 [[江戸時代]]には当社に参詣する[[講]]（大山講）が関東各地に組織され、多くの庶民が参詣した。大山詣は6月27日から7月17日まで期間に行われる[[女人禁制]]の参詣で、特に[[鳶職|鳶]]や[[職人]]の間で人気があった。大山に2つある瀧・良辧瀧と大瀧で[[水垢離]]し、頂上の石尊大権現に登り、持ってきた木太刀を神前に納め、改めて授けられた木太刀を[[護符]]として持ち帰った。また、大山祇大神は、[[富士山]]に鎮まるとされる木花咲耶姫の父であるため、大山と富士山の「両詣り」も盛んとなり、「富士に登らば大山に登るべし、大山に登らば富士に登るべし」といわれた。なお、一部の地域には、大山に登ると一人前として認められるという伝承があり、大山の神霊が立身出世の神とされていたことがうかがえる。 [[明治時代]]になると[[神仏分離令]]慶応4年・明治元年([[1868年]])3月の[[太政官布告]]。を機に巻き起こった[[廃仏毀釈]]の大波に、強い勢力を保持していた大山寺も一呑みにされた。この時期に「'''石尊大権現・大山寺'''」の名称は使われなくなり、旧来の「'''阿夫利神社'''」に再び改称された。その後、大山寺はかつての女坂途中に場所を移して再建され、現在に至る。[[明治]]6年（[[1873年]]）には国学者の[[権田直助]]を祠官に迎え県社兼郷社に列格している。 戦後、[[神社本庁]]には属さず、[[昭和]]27年（[[1952年]]）8月より阿夫利神社本庁として単独で運営されてきたが、近年{{いつ|date=2022年12月}}、神社本庁の傘下に入った（阿夫利神社本庁も存続）。 == 祭事 == *筒粥神事 - 天候を占う。 *引目祭 - 厄を祓う。 *山開き *火祭薪能 *大山能 *巫女舞 *倭舞 == 探訪（ギャラリー） == File:Ooyama It is a [[Beppyo shrine]], or a shrine that is particularly notable in a certain way with a significant history to it.{{Cite web|title=Learn about Oyama Afuri Shrine - Oyama Afuri Shrine|url=https://www.afuri.or.jp/en/about/|access-date=2024-03-29|language=en-US}}{{Cite web|date=2023-12-28|title=Oyama Afuri Shrine|url=https://www.afuri.or.jp/en/|access-date=2024-03-29|language=en-US}}{{Cite web|date=2013-04-07|title=Afuri Shrine on Mt. Oyama - Kanagawa|url=https://en.japantravel.com/kanagawa/afuri-shrine-on-mt-oyama/4043|access-date=2024-03-29|website=JapanTravel|language=en}} '''{{ill|Oyama Afuri Shrine|ja|大山阿夫利神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}''' (Oyama Afuri Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} located in {{ill|Isehara City|ja|伊勢原市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Kanagawa Prefecture|ja|神奈川県|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, situated on {{ill|Oyama|ja|大山|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (also known as '''Amefuri-yama'''〈{{ill|Amefuri-yama|ja|雨降山|qq=draft|qq=draft}}〉). It is recorded in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|qq=draft|qq=draft}} from the {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式|qq=draft|qq=draft}} period (Enchō 5, {{ill|927|ja|927th year|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) as one of the thirteen shrines (small shrines) of the {{ill|Engishiki-shiki Naishinsha Jūsansha|ja|延喜式内社十三社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in {{ill|Sagami Province|ja|相模国|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Under the [[Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines]], it was classified as a prefectural shrine (Ken-sha) and is currently designated as a [[Beppyo Shrine|Beppyo shrine]] by the {{ill|Jinja Honchō|ja|神社本庁|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. The shrine is composed of two parts: the main shrine (honsha), which includes the inner shrine (okusha) and the front shrine (zensha) located at the summit of Oyama, and the lower shrine (gesha) located on the mid-slope.[http://www.afuri.or.jp/about/map/]{{ill|About Oyama Afuri Shrine|ja|大山阿夫利神社について：境内のご案内|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Official site of Oyama Afuri Shrine). The lower shrine is accessible via the {{ill|Oyama Cable Car|ja|大山ケーブルカー|qq=draft|qq=draft}} operated by {{ill|Oyama Kankō Dentetsu|ja|大山観光電鉄|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. == History == [[File:Pilgrims at the Roben waterfall, Oyama.jpg|thumb|left|245px|“Ōyama Sekison Raben-taki no Zu” by {{ill|Utagawa Kuniyoshi|ja|歌川国芳|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Art name: Ichiyūsai), painted circa 1819–1820 (Bunsei 2–3). Men praying at the waterfall of Ōyama Sekison (current Oyama Afuri Shrine).]] {{ill|Oyama|ja|大山|qq=draft|qq=draft}} has long been revered as an object of mountain worship. Excavations at its summit have uncovered {{ill|Jomon pottery|ja|縄文土器|qq=draft|qq=draft}} used in rituals.[http://www.afuri.or.jp/about/]{{ill|About Oyama Afuri Shrine|ja|大山阿夫利神社について|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Official site of Oyama Afuri Shrine) It is also known as “{{ill|Amefuri-yama|ja|雨降山|qq=draft|qq=draft}}” because clouds and mist frequently gather at the summit, which are believed to bring rain, and it was revered as a rain-making deity. In addition, worship of a giant stone ({{ill|Iwa-za|ja|磐座|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) at the summit and of the twin waterfalls on the mountainside as sacred water sources is also observed.[[宝賀寿男]], “Section 3: The Early Branches of Clans in Kinai and Tōkoku – Part 2: Musashi no Kuni no Kunizukuri and the Provincial Clans of Tōkoku”, in “Studies on Ancient Clans, No. 16: The Rise and Fall of the Izumo Kingdom” (青垣出版, 2020), pp.263–264. According to tradition, Ōyama Afuri Shrine was founded during the reign of {{ill|Sujin-tennō|ja|崇神天皇|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (around the 3rd century BC, though this is considered legendary rather than historical). The {{ill|Engishiki-shiki Shinnamōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, compiled during the Engishiki period, records the shrine as “Afuri Shrine” in its 5th year ({{ill|927|ja|927th year|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) and classifies it as a minor shrine among the thirteen shrines of the {{ill|Engishiki-shiki Naishinsha Jūsansha|ja|延喜式内社十三社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in {{ill|Sagami Province|ja|相模国|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. [[simple:user:immanuelle/Oyama Afuri Shrine]] == Enshrined Deities == * The primary deity enshrined at the lower shrine is {{ill|Ōyamatsumi|ja|大山祇神|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Ōyamatsumi-no-kami). * The main shrine enshrines {{ill|Ōyamatsumi|ja|大山祇神|qq=draft|qq=draft}} as its principal deity (prior to the Shinto-Buddhism separation, he was revered as {{ill|Sekison Daigongen|ja|石尊大権現|qq=draft|qq=draft}}). * The subsidiary shrine (oku-sha) enshrines {{ill|Raijin|ja|大雷神|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Ōi-katsuchi-no-kami; known as {{ill|Ōtengu|ja|大天狗|qq=draft|qq=draft}} during the syncretic period). * The subsidiary shrine (zen-sha) enshrines {{ill|Takaokami|ja|高龗神|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Takaokami; known as {{ill|Kotenko|ja|小天狗|qq=draft|qq=draft}} during the syncretic period). This arrangement—enshrining Ōyamatsumi along with the subsidiary deities Raijin and Takaokami—is identical to that of the shrine in {{ill|Ehime Prefecture|ja|愛媛県|qq=draft|qq=draft}} known as {{ill|Ōyamatsumi Shrine|ja|大山祇神社|1=Ōyamazumi Shrine|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, although these deities were enshrined only after the separation of Shinto and Buddhism in the Meiji period. During the Edo period, when Shinto and Buddhism were syncretized, the main shrine originally enshrined {{ill|Sekison Daigongen|ja|石尊大権現|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, as the sacred stone ({{ill|Reisekki|ja|霊石|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) at the summit served as his manifestation. In the subsidiary shrines, {{ill|Ōtengu|ja|大天狗|qq=draft|qq=draft}} was enshrined in the oku-sha and {{ill|Kotenko|ja|小天狗|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in the zen-sha. == Cultural Importance == === Oyama Pilgrimage === During the Edo period the Oyama Pilgrimage was a tradition where worshippers formed groups ("{{ill|Kō (lecture)|lt=Kō|en|qq=draft|qq=draft}}") to visit the shrine. This pilgrimage, coupled with the "Oyama Kaido" pathway played a role in shaping culture by inspiring rakugo stories and ukiyo e artworks. In 2008 this pilgrimage was designated as a Heritage Site due to its cultural significance. === Osamedachi Tradition === A tradition stemming from a tale about Minamoto no Yoritomo offering a sword to the shrine the Osamedachi custom involves presenting swords that can reach lengths of up to 6 meters. === Kagura Dance === Imported from Kasuga Taisha Shrine during the Meiji era the Kagura dance performed at Oyama Afuri Shrine includes dances by boys (Yamato Mai) and girls (Miko dance) spanning age groups, from elementary school students to adults. The Sendoshi Ryokan originally built to host worshippers has transformed into an inn that provides lodging and dining services. It stands as one of the temple accommodations, in Japan. As for the Oyama Noh tradition it reflects the shrines commitment to peace and harmony tracing its origins back, to the Genroku era. This tradition signifies the bond established among the leaders of Mt. Oyama through their embrace of Noh performances. == Access == === To the Lower Shrine === ; Public Transportation * From the north exit of the {{ill|Odakyu Odawara Line|ja|小田急小田原線|qq=draft|qq=draft}} at {{ill|Isehara Station|ja|伊勢原駅|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, take Bus Route 10 operated by {{ill|Kanagawa Chūō Kōtsū|ja|神奈川中央交通西|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, alight at the final stop ("Ōyama Cable" bound), which takes approximately 25 minutes. *** Then walk about 15 minutes (approximately 600 meters) from the Ōyama Cable Car Station. ; By Car * Accessible via the {{ill|Shin-Tōmei Expressway|ja|新東名高速道路|qq=draft|qq=draft}} at the {{ill|Isehara Ōyama Interchange|ja|伊勢原大山インターチェンジ|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, then via {{ill|Kanagawa Prefectural Road 611|ja|神奈川県道611号大山板戸線|qq=draft|qq=draft}}; municipal parking is available (about a 15-minute walk from the parking lot to the Ōyama Cable Car Station). === To the Main Shrine === * Ascend the mountain It is a [[Beppyo shrine]], or a shrine that is particularly notable in a certain way with a significant history to it.{{Cite web|title=Learn about Oyama Afuri Shrine - Oyama Afuri Shrine|url=https://www.afuri.or.jp/en/about/|access-date=2024-03-29|language=en-US}}{{Cite web|date=2023-12-28|title=Oyama Afuri Shrine|url=https://www.afuri.or.jp/en/|access-date=2024-03-29|language=en-US}}{{Cite web|date=2013-04-07|title=Afuri Shrine on Mt. Oyama - Kanagawa|url=https://en.japantravel.com/kanagawa/afuri-shrine-on-mt-oyama/4043|access-date=2024-03-29|website=JapanTravel|language=en}} '''{{ill|Oyama Afuri Shrine|ja|大山阿夫利神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}''' (Oyama Afuri Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} located in {{ill|Isehara City|ja|伊勢原市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Kanagawa Prefecture|ja|神奈川県|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, situated on {{ill|Oyama|ja|大山|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (also known as '''Amefuri-yama'''〈{{ill|Amefuri-yama|ja|雨降山|qq=draft|qq=draft}}〉). It is recorded in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|qq=draft|qq=draft}} from the {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式|qq=draft|qq=draft}} period (Enchō 5, {{ill|927|ja|927th year|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) as one of the thirteen shrines (small shrines) of the {{ill|Engishiki-shiki Naishinsha Jūsansha|ja|延喜式内社十三社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in {{ill|Sagami Province|ja|相模国|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Under the [[Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines]], it was classified as a prefectural shrine (Ken-sha) and is currently designated as a [[Beppyo Shrine|Beppyo shrine]] by the {{ill|Jinja Honchō|ja|神社本庁|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. The shrine is composed of two parts: the main shrine (honsha), which includes the inner shrine (okusha) and the front shrine (zensha) located at the summit of Oyama, and the lower shrine (gesha) located on the mid-slope.[http://www.afuri.or.jp/about/map/]{{ill|About Oyama Afuri Shrine|ja|大山阿夫利神社について：境内のご案内|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Official site of Oyama Afuri Shrine). The lower shrine is accessible via the {{ill|Oyama Cable Car|ja|大山ケーブルカー|qq=draft|qq=draft}} operated by {{ill|Oyama Kankō Dentetsu|ja|大山観光電鉄|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. == History == [[File:Pilgrims at the Roben waterfall, Oyama.jpg|thumb|left|245px|“Ōyama Sekison Raben-taki no Zu” by {{ill|Utagawa Kuniyoshi|ja|歌川国芳|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Art name: Ichiyūsai), painted circa 1819–1820 (Bunsei 2–3). Men praying at the waterfall of Ōyama Sekison (current Oyama Afuri Shrine).]] {{ill|Oyama|ja|大山|qq=draft|qq=draft}} has long been revered as an object of mountain worship. Excavations at its summit have uncovered {{ill|Jomon pottery|ja|縄文土器|qq=draft|qq=draft}} used in rituals.[http://www.afuri.or.jp/about/]{{ill|About Oyama Afuri Shrine|ja|大山阿夫利神社について|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Official site of Oyama Afuri Shrine) It is also known as “{{ill|Amefuri-yama|ja|雨降山|qq=draft|qq=draft}}” because clouds and mist frequently gather at the summit, which are believed to bring rain, and it was revered as a rain-making deity. In addition, worship of a giant stone ({{ill|Iwa-za|ja|磐座|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) at the summit and of the twin waterfalls on the mountainside as sacred water sources is also observed.[[宝賀寿男]], “Section 3: The Early Branches of Clans in Kinai and Tōkoku – Part 2: Musashi no Kuni no Kunizukuri and the Provincial Clans of Tōkoku”, in “Studies on Ancient Clans, No. 16: The Rise and Fall of the Izumo Kingdom” (青垣出版, 2020), pp.263–264. According to tradition, Ōyama Afuri Shrine was founded during the reign of {{ill|Sujin-tennō|ja|崇神天皇|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (around the 3rd century BC, though this is considered legendary rather than historical). The {{ill|Engishiki-shiki Shinnamōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, compiled during the Engishiki period, records the shrine as “Afuri Shrine” in its 5th year ({{ill|927|ja|927th year|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) and classifies it as a minor shrine among the thirteen shrines of the {{ill|Engishiki-shiki Naishinsha Jūsansha|ja|延喜式内社十三社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in {{ill|Sagami Province|ja|相模国|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. [[simple:user:immanuelle/Oyama Afuri Shrine]] == Enshrined Deities == * The primary deity enshrined at the lower shrine is {{ill|Ōyamatsumi|ja|大山祇神|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Ōyamatsumi-no-kami). * The main shrine enshrines {{ill|Ōyamatsumi|ja|大山祇神|qq=draft|qq=draft}} as its principal deity (prior to the Shinto-Buddhism separation, he was revered as {{ill|Sekison Daigongen|ja|石尊大権現|qq=draft|qq=draft}}). * The subsidiary shrine (oku-sha) enshrines {{ill|Raijin|ja|大雷神|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Ōi-katsuchi-no-kami; known as {{ill|Ōtengu|ja|大天狗|qq=draft|qq=draft}} during the syncretic period). * The subsidiary shrine (zen-sha) enshrines {{ill|Takaokami|ja|高龗神|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Takaokami; known as {{ill|Kotenko|ja|小天狗|qq=draft|qq=draft}} during the syncretic period). This arrangement—enshrining Ōyamatsumi along with the subsidiary deities Raijin and Takaokami—is identical to that of the shrine in {{ill|Ehime Prefecture|ja|愛媛県|qq=draft|qq=draft}} known as {{ill|Ōyamatsumi Shrine|ja|大山祇神社|1=Ōyamazumi Shrine|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, although these deities were enshrined only after the separation of Shinto and Buddhism in the Meiji period. During the Edo period, when Shinto and Buddhism were syncretized, the main shrine originally enshrined {{ill|Sekison Daigongen|ja|石尊大権現|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, as the sacred stone ({{ill|Reisekki|ja|霊石|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) at the summit served as his manifestation. In the subsidiary shrines, {{ill|Ōtengu|ja|大天狗|qq=draft|qq=draft}} was enshrined in the oku-sha and {{ill|Kotenko|ja|小天狗|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in the zen-sha. == Cultural Importance == === Oyama Pilgrimage === During the Edo period the Oyama Pilgrimage was a tradition where worshippers formed groups ("{{ill|Kō (lecture)|lt=Kō|en|qq=draft|qq=draft}}") to visit the shrine. This pilgrimage, coupled with the "Oyama Kaido" pathway played a role in shaping culture by inspiring rakugo stories and ukiyo e artworks. In 2008 this pilgrimage was designated as a Heritage Site due to its cultural significance. === Osamedachi Tradition === A tradition stemming from a tale about Minamoto no Yoritomo offering a sword to the shrine the Osamedachi custom involves presenting swords that can reach lengths of up to 6 meters. === Kagura Dance === Imported from Kasuga Taisha Shrine during the Meiji era the Kagura dance performed at Oyama Afuri Shrine includes dances by boys (Yamato Mai) and girls (Miko dance) spanning age groups, from elementary school students to adults. The Sendoshi Ryokan originally built to host worshippers has transformed into an inn that provides lodging and dining services. It stands as one of the temple accommodations, in Japan. As for the Oyama Noh tradition it reflects the shrines commitment to peace and harmony tracing its origins back, to the Genroku era. This tradition signifies the bond established among the leaders of Mt. Oyama through their embrace of Noh performances. == Access == === To the Lower Shrine === ; Public Transportation * From the north exit of the {{ill|Odakyu Odawara Line|ja|小田急小田原線|qq=draft|qq=draft}} at {{ill|Isehara Station|ja|伊勢原駅|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, take Bus Route 10 operated by {{ill|Kanagawa Chūō Kōtsū|ja|神奈川中央交通西|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, alight at the final stop ("Ōyama Cable" bound), which takes approximately 25 minutes. *** Then walk about 15 minutes (approximately 600 meters) from the Ōyama Cable Car Station. ; By Car * Accessible via the {{ill|Shin-Tōmei Expressway|ja|新東名高速道路|qq=draft|qq=draft}} at the {{ill|Isehara Ōyama Interchange|ja|伊勢原大山インターチェンジ|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, then via {{ill|Kanagawa Prefectural Road 611|ja|神奈川県道611号大山板戸線|qq=draft|qq=draft}}; municipal parking is available (about a 15-minute walk from the parking lot to the Ōyama Cable Car Station). === To the Main Shrine === * Ascend the mountain {{ill|Betsuhyō Shrine|ja|別表神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} |創建 = Tradition: During the reign of {{ill|Sujin-tennō|ja|崇神天皇|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (circa BC 97–BC 30) |例祭 = July 27 |地図 = {{Location map+|Japan Kanagawa|width=210|float=center|caption=|places= {{Location map~|Japan Kanagawa|lat_deg=35|lat_min=26|lat_sec=26|lon_deg=139|lon_min=13|lon_sec=51.8|position=top|label={{ill|Main Shrine|ja|本社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20}} {{Location map~|Japan Kanagawa|lat_deg=35|lat_min=25|lat_sec=54.7|lon_deg=139|lon_min=14|lon_sec=16.6|position=right|label={{ill|Lower Shrine|ja|下社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20}}|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| image=大山阿夫利神社 下社拝殿.jpg}} {{OSM Location map|coord={{coord|35.436187|N|139.234166|E}}|fullscreen-option=1|zoom=14|float=center|width=200|caption=|title=|mark-coord1={{coord|35|26|26|N|139|13|51.8|E}}|label1={{ill|Main Shrine|ja|本社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}|label-pos1=right|mark-size1=8|mark-coord2={{coord|35|25|54.7|N|139|14|16.6|E}}|label2={{ill|Lower Shrine|ja|下社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}|label-pos2=top|mark-size2=8}} }} {{osm box|w|161550990}} [[File:大山道.png|thumb|right|260px|{{ill|Oyama-dō|ja|大山道|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Main 8 Routes)]] {{ill|Oyama Afuri Shrine|ja|%E5%A4%A7%E5%B1%B1%E9%98%BF%E5%A4%AB%E5%88%A9%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (大山阿夫利神社) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in Isehara City, Kanagawa Prefecture, [[Japan]]. It is a [[Beppyo shrine]], or a shrine that is particularly notable in a certain way with a significant history to it.{{Cite web|title=Learn about Oyama Afuri Shrine - Oyama Afuri Shrine|url=https://www.afuri.or.jp/en/about/|access-date=2024-03-29|language=en-US}}{{Cite web|date=2023-12-28|title=Oyama Afuri Shrine|url=https://www.afuri.or.jp/en/|access-date=2024-03-29|language=en-US}}{{Cite web|date=2013-04-07|title=Afuri Shrine on Mt. Oyama - Kanagawa|url=https://en.japantravel.com/kanagawa/afuri-shrine-on-mt-oyama/4043|access-date=2024-03-29|website=JapanTravel|language=en}} '''{{ill|Oyama Afuri Shrine|ja|大山阿夫利神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}''' (Oyama Afuri Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} located in {{ill|Isehara City|ja|伊勢原市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Kanagawa Prefecture|ja|神奈川県|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, situated on {{ill|Oyama|ja|大山|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (also known as '''Amefuri-yama'''〈{{ill|Amefuri-yama|ja|雨降山|qq=draft|qq=draft}}〉). It is recorded in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|qq=draft|qq=draft}} from the {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式|qq=draft|qq=draft}} period (Enchō 5, {{ill|927|ja|927th year|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) as one of the thirteen shrines (small shrines) of the {{ill|Engishiki-shiki Naishinsha Jūsansha|ja|延喜式内社十三社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in {{ill|Sagami Province|ja|相模国|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Under the [[Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines]], it was classified as a prefectural shrine (Ken-sha) and is currently designated as a [[Beppyo Shrine|Beppyo shrine]] by the {{ill|Jinja Honchō|ja|神社本庁|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. The shrine is composed of two parts: the main shrine (honsha), which includes the inner shrine (okusha) and the front shrine (zensha) located at the summit of Oyama, and the lower shrine (gesha) located on the mid-slope.[http://www.afuri.or.jp/about/map/]{{ill|About Oyama Afuri Shrine|ja|大山阿夫利神社について：境内のご案内|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Official site of Oyama Afuri Shrine). The lower shrine is accessible via the {{ill|Oyama Cable Car|ja|大山ケーブルカー|qq=draft|qq=draft}} operated by {{ill|Oyama Kankō Dentetsu|ja|大山観光電鉄|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. == History == [[File:Pilgrims at the Roben waterfall, Oyama.jpg|thumb|left|245px|“Ōyama Sekison Raben-taki no Zu” by {{ill|Utagawa Kuniyoshi|ja|歌川国芳|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Art name: Ichiyūsai), painted circa 1819–1820 (Bunsei 2–3). Men praying at the waterfall of Ōyama Sekison (current Oyama Afuri Shrine).]] {{ill|Oyama|ja|大山|qq=draft|qq=draft}} has long been revered as an object of mountain worship. Excavations at its summit have uncovered {{ill|Jomon pottery|ja|縄文土器|qq=draft|qq=draft}} used in rituals.[http://www.afuri.or.jp/about/]{{ill|About Oyama Afuri Shrine|ja|大山阿夫利神社について|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Official site of Oyama Afuri Shrine) It is also known as “{{ill|Amefuri-yama|ja|雨降山|qq=draft|qq=draft}}” because clouds and mist frequently gather at the summit, which are believed to bring rain, and it was revered as a rain-making deity. In addition, worship of a giant stone ({{ill|Iwa-za|ja|磐座|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) at the summit and of the twin waterfalls on the mountainside as sacred water sources is also observed.[[宝賀寿男]], “Section 3: The Early Branches of Clans in Kinai and Tōkoku – Part 2: Musashi no Kuni no Kunizukuri and the Provincial Clans of Tōkoku”, in “Studies on Ancient Clans, No. 16: The Rise and Fall of the Izumo Kingdom” (青垣出版, 2020), pp.263–264. According to tradition, Ōyama Afuri Shrine was founded during the reign of {{ill|Sujin-tennō|ja|崇神天皇|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (around the 3rd century BC, though this is considered legendary rather than historical). The {{ill|Engishiki-shiki Shinnamōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, compiled during the Engishiki period, records the shrine as “Afuri Shrine” in its 5th year ({{ill|927|ja|927th year|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) and classifies it as a minor shrine among the thirteen shrines of the {{ill|Engishiki-shiki Naishinsha Jūsansha|ja|延喜式内社十三社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in {{ill|Sagami Province|ja|相模国|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. [[simple:user:immanuelle/Oyama Afuri Shrine]] == Enshrined Deities == * The primary deity enshrined at the lower shrine is {{ill|Ōyamatsumi|ja|大山祇神|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Ōyamatsumi-no-kami). * The main shrine enshrines {{ill|Ōyamatsumi|ja|大山祇神|qq=draft|qq=draft}} as its principal deity (prior to the Shinto-Buddhism separation, he was revered as {{ill|Sekison Daigongen|ja|石尊大権現|qq=draft|qq=draft}}). * The subsidiary shrine (oku-sha) enshrines {{ill|Raijin|ja|大雷神|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Ōi-katsuchi-no-kami; known as {{ill|Ōtengu|ja|大天狗|qq=draft|qq=draft}} during the syncretic period). * The subsidiary shrine (zen-sha) enshrines {{ill|Takaokami|ja|高龗神|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Takaokami; known as {{ill|Kotenko|ja|小天狗|qq=draft|qq=draft}} during the syncretic period). This arrangement—enshrining Ōyamatsumi along with the subsidiary deities Raijin and Takaokami—is identical to that of the shrine in {{ill|Ehime Prefecture|ja|愛媛県|qq=draft|qq=draft}} known as {{ill|Ōyamatsumi Shrine|ja|大山祇神社|1=Ōyamazumi Shrine|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, although these deities were enshrined only after the separation of Shinto and Buddhism in the Meiji period. During the Edo period, when Shinto and Buddhism were syncretized, the main shrine originally enshrined {{ill|Sekison Daigongen|ja|石尊大権現|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, as the sacred stone ({{ill|Reisekki|ja|霊石|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) at the summit served as his manifestation. In the subsidiary shrines, {{ill|Ōtengu|ja|大天狗|qq=draft|qq=draft}} was enshrined in the oku-sha and {{ill|Kotenko|ja|小天狗|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in the zen-sha. == Cultural Importance == === Oyama Pilgrimage === During the Edo period the Oyama Pilgrimage was a tradition where worshippers formed groups ("{{ill|Kō (lecture)|lt=Kō|en|qq=draft|qq=draft}}") to visit the shrine. This pilgrimage, coupled with the "Oyama Kaido" pathway played a role in shaping culture by inspiring rakugo stories and ukiyo e artworks. In 2008 this pilgrimage was designated as a Heritage Site due to its cultural significance. === Osamedachi Tradition === A tradition stemming from a tale about Minamoto no Yoritomo offering a sword to the shrine the Osamedachi custom involves presenting swords that can reach lengths of up to 6 meters. === Kagura Dance === Imported from Kasuga Taisha Shrine during the Meiji era the Kagura dance performed at Oyama Afuri Shrine includes dances by boys (Yamato Mai) and girls (Miko dance) spanning age groups, from elementary school students to adults. The Sendoshi Ryokan originally built to host worshippers has transformed into an inn that provides lodging and dining services. It stands as one of the temple accommodations, in Japan. As for the Oyama Noh tradition it reflects the shrines commitment to peace and harmony tracing its origins back, to the Genroku era. This tradition signifies the bond established among the leaders of Mt. Oyama through their embrace of Noh performances. == Access == === To the Lower Shrine === ; Public Transportation * From the north exit of the {{ill|Odakyu Odawara Line|ja|小田急小田原線|qq=draft|qq=draft}} at {{ill|Isehara Station|ja|伊勢原駅|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, take Bus Route 10 operated by {{ill|Kanagawa Chūō Kōtsū|ja|神奈川中央交通西|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, alight at the final stop ("Ōyama Cable" bound), which takes approximately 25 minutes. *** Then walk about 15 minutes (approximately 600 meters) from the Ōyama Cable Car Station. ; By Car * Accessible via the {{ill|Shin-Tōmei Expressway|ja|新東名高速道路|qq=draft|qq=draft}} at the {{ill|Isehara Ōyama Interchange|ja|伊勢原大山インターチェンジ|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, then via {{ill|Kanagawa Prefectural Road 611|ja|神奈川県道611号大山板戸線|qq=draft|qq=draft}}; municipal parking is available (about a 15-minute walk from the parking lot to the Ōyama Cable Car Station). === To the Main Shrine === * Ascend the mountain }} {{osm box|w|161550990}} [[File:大山道.png|thumb|right|260px|大山道(主要8道)]] '''大山阿夫利神社'''（おおやまあふりじんじゃ）は、[[神奈川県]][[伊勢原市]]の[[大山 (神奈川県)|大山]]（別名: '''雨降山'''〈あふりやま〉）にある[[神社]]である。[[延長 (元号)|延長]]5年（[[927年]]）の『[[延喜式神名帳]]』に記載されている[[相模国]]の[[相模国の式内社一覧|延喜式内社十三社]]の内の一社（小社）で、[[近代社格制度|旧社格]]では[[県社]]に列している（現・[[神社本庁]]の[[別表神社]]）。 大山の山頂に鎮座する'''本社'''（奥社・前社含む）と中腹に鎮座する'''下社'''があり[http://www.afuri.or.jp/about/map/ 大山阿夫利神社について：境内のご案内]（大山阿夫利神社公式サイト）、下社までは[[大山観光電鉄大山鋼索線|大山ケーブルカー]]でアクセス可能である（[[#交通アクセス]]も参照）。 == 祭神 == 下社主祭神は、[[オオヤマツミ|大山祇神]]（おおやまつみのかみ）。 本社主祭神に、[[オオヤマツミ|大山祇神]]（おおやまつみのかみ、神仏分離前は[[石尊大権現]]）。 摂社の奥社祭神に、[[雷神|大雷神]]（おおいかつちのかみ、神仏分離前は[[大天狗]]）。 摂社の前社祭神に、[[淤加美神|高龗神]]（たかおかみ、神仏分離前は[[烏天狗|小天狗]]）。 主祭神の大山祇神に摂社として雷神と高龗神の2神を配するのは愛媛県の[[大山祇神社]]と同じ構成であるが、これらは[[明治]]になってから[[神仏分離]]の際に祀られるようになったものであり、[[江戸時代|江戸期]]以前の[[神仏習合]]時代には、本社には本来の[[祭神]]である[[石尊大権現]]（せきそんだいごんげん、山頂で[[霊石]]が祀られていたことからこう呼ばれた）が祀られていた。また摂社では、奥社に[[大天狗]]、前社に[[烏天狗|小天狗]]が祀られていた。 == 歴史 == [[File:Pilgrims at the Roben waterfall, Oyama.jpg|thumb|left|245px|「大山石尊良辧瀧之図」 [[歌川国芳]]（[[号 (称号)|画号]]: 一勇斎）筆、1819-20年（[[文政]]2-3年）。大山石尊（現・大山阿夫利神社）の滝に参拝する男達。]] [[大山 (神奈川県)|大山]]は古くから[[山岳信仰]]の対象として知られ、山頂からは祭祀に使われたとされる[[縄文土器]]が発掘されるなどしている[http://www.afuri.or.jp/about/ 大山阿夫利神社について]（大山阿夫利神社公式サイト）。大山は山上によく雲や霧が生じて雨を降らすことが多いとされたことから、「'''あめふり（あふり）山'''」とも呼ばれ、[[雨乞い]]の対象としても知られていた。また、山頂の自然石を[[神体]]とする巨石崇拝（[[磐座]]）と山腹の二重滝を崇拝する[[湧水]]地信仰も見られる[[宝賀寿男]]「第三部 畿内・東国に展開した初期分岐の支族　二 武蔵国造と東国の諸国造族」『古代氏族の研究⑯　出雲氏・土師氏 原出雲王国の盛衰』青垣出版、2020年、263、264頁。。 大山阿夫利神社は、社伝によると[[崇神天皇]]の御代崇神天皇の御代は西暦の[[3世紀]]ごろに相当すると考えられている。もっとも、社伝と史実は多分に別儀である事をここに特記しておく。に創建されたとされる。[[延長 (元号)|延長]]5年（[[927年]]）の『[[延喜式神名帳]]』では「'''阿夫利神社'''」と記載され、小社に列している。 [[天平勝宝]]4年（西暦[[752年]]）、[[良弁]]により[[神宮寺]]として雨降山[[大山寺 (伊勢原市)|大山寺]]が建立され、本尊として[[不動明王]]が祀られた。以後、[[神仏習合]]が続く。 [[中世]]以降は大山寺を拠点とする[[修験道]]（大山修験）が盛んになり、[[源頼朝]]を始め、[[北条氏]]・[[徳川氏]]など、武家の崇敬を受けた。 [[江戸時代]]には当社に参詣する[[講]]（大山講）が関東各地に組織され、多くの庶民が参詣した。大山詣は6月27日から7月17日まで期間に行われる[[女人禁制]]の参詣で、特に[[鳶職|鳶]]や[[職人]]の間で人気があった。大山に2つある瀧・良辧瀧と大瀧で[[水垢離]]し、頂上の石尊大権現に登り、持ってきた木太刀を神前に納め、改めて授けられた木太刀を[[護符]]として持ち帰った。また、大山祇大神は、[[富士山]]に鎮まるとされる木花咲耶姫の父であるため、大山と富士山の「両詣り」も盛んとなり、「富士に登らば大山に登るべし、大山に登らば富士に登るべし」といわれた。なお、一部の地域には、大山に登ると一人前として認められるという伝承があり、大山の神霊が立身出世の神とされていたことがうかがえる。 [[明治時代]]になると[[神仏分離令]]慶応4年・明治元年([[1868年]])3月の[[太政官布告]]。を機に巻き起こった[[廃仏毀釈]]の大波に、強い勢力を保持していた大山寺も一呑みにされた。この時期に「'''石尊大権現・大山寺'''」の名称は使われなくなり、旧来の「'''阿夫利神社'''」に再び改称された。その後、大山寺はかつての女坂途中に場所を移して再建され、現在に至る。[[明治]]6年（[[1873年]]）には国学者の[[権田直助]]を祠官に迎え県社兼郷社に列格している。 戦後、[[神社本庁]]には属さず、[[昭和]]27年（[[1952年]]）8月より阿夫利神社本庁として単独で運営されてきたが、近年{{いつ|date=2022年12月}}、神社本庁の傘下に入った（阿夫利神社本庁も存続）。 == 祭事 == *筒粥神事 - 天候を占う。 *引目祭 - 厄を祓う。 *山開き *火祭薪能 *大山能 *巫女舞 *倭舞 == 探訪（ギャラリー） == File:Ooyama It is a [[Beppyo shrine]], or a shrine that is particularly notable in a certain way with a significant history to it.{{Cite web|title=Learn about Oyama Afuri Shrine - Oyama Afuri Shrine|url=https://www.afuri.or.jp/en/about/|access-date=2024-03-29|language=en-US}}{{Cite web|date=2023-12-28|title=Oyama Afuri Shrine|url=https://www.afuri.or.jp/en/|access-date=2024-03-29|language=en-US}}{{Cite web|date=2013-04-07|title=Afuri Shrine on Mt. Oyama - Kanagawa|url=https://en.japantravel.com/kanagawa/afuri-shrine-on-mt-oyama/4043|access-date=2024-03-29|website=JapanTravel|language=en}} '''{{ill|Oyama Afuri Shrine|ja|大山阿夫利神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}''' (Oyama Afuri Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} located in {{ill|Isehara City|ja|伊勢原市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Kanagawa Prefecture|ja|神奈川県|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, situated on {{ill|Oyama|ja|大山|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (also known as '''Amefuri-yama'''〈{{ill|Amefuri-yama|ja|雨降山|qq=draft|qq=draft}}〉). It is recorded in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|qq=draft|qq=draft}} from the {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式|qq=draft|qq=draft}} period (Enchō 5, {{ill|927|ja|927th year|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) as one of the thirteen shrines (small shrines) of the {{ill|Engishiki-shiki Naishinsha Jūsansha|ja|延喜式内社十三社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in {{ill|Sagami Province|ja|相模国|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Under the [[Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines]], it was classified as a prefectural shrine (Ken-sha) and is currently designated as a [[Beppyo Shrine|Beppyo shrine]] by the {{ill|Jinja Honchō|ja|神社本庁|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. The shrine is composed of two parts: the main shrine (honsha), which includes the inner shrine (okusha) and the front shrine (zensha) located at the summit of Oyama, and the lower shrine (gesha) located on the mid-slope.[http://www.afuri.or.jp/about/map/]{{ill|About Oyama Afuri Shrine|ja|大山阿夫利神社について：境内のご案内|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Official site of Oyama Afuri Shrine). The lower shrine is accessible via the {{ill|Oyama Cable Car|ja|大山ケーブルカー|qq=draft|qq=draft}} operated by {{ill|Oyama Kankō Dentetsu|ja|大山観光電鉄|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. == History == [[File:Pilgrims at the Roben waterfall, Oyama.jpg|thumb|left|245px|“Ōyama Sekison Raben-taki no Zu” by {{ill|Utagawa Kuniyoshi|ja|歌川国芳|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Art name: Ichiyūsai), painted circa 1819–1820 (Bunsei 2–3). Men praying at the waterfall of Ōyama Sekison (current Oyama Afuri Shrine).]] {{ill|Oyama|ja|大山|qq=draft|qq=draft}} has long been revered as an object of mountain worship. Excavations at its summit have uncovered {{ill|Jomon pottery|ja|縄文土器|qq=draft|qq=draft}} used in rituals.[http://www.afuri.or.jp/about/]{{ill|About Oyama Afuri Shrine|ja|大山阿夫利神社について|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Official site of Oyama Afuri Shrine) It is also known as “{{ill|Amefuri-yama|ja|雨降山|qq=draft|qq=draft}}” because clouds and mist frequently gather at the summit, which are believed to bring rain, and it was revered as a rain-making deity. In addition, worship of a giant stone ({{ill|Iwa-za|ja|磐座|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) at the summit and of the twin waterfalls on the mountainside as sacred water sources is also observed.[[宝賀寿男]], “Section 3: The Early Branches of Clans in Kinai and Tōkoku – Part 2: Musashi no Kuni no Kunizukuri and the Provincial Clans of Tōkoku”, in “Studies on Ancient Clans, No. 16: The Rise and Fall of the Izumo Kingdom” (青垣出版, 2020), pp.263–264. According to tradition, Ōyama Afuri Shrine was founded during the reign of {{ill|Sujin-tennō|ja|崇神天皇|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (around the 3rd century BC, though this is considered legendary rather than historical). The {{ill|Engishiki-shiki Shinnamōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, compiled during the Engishiki period, records the shrine as “Afuri Shrine” in its 5th year ({{ill|927|ja|927th year|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) and classifies it as a minor shrine among the thirteen shrines of the {{ill|Engishiki-shiki Naishinsha Jūsansha|ja|延喜式内社十三社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in {{ill|Sagami Province|ja|相模国|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. [[simple:user:immanuelle/Oyama Afuri Shrine]] == Enshrined Deities == * The primary deity enshrined at the lower shrine is {{ill|Ōyamatsumi|ja|大山祇神|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Ōyamatsumi-no-kami). * The main shrine enshrines {{ill|Ōyamatsumi|ja|大山祇神|qq=draft|qq=draft}} as its principal deity (prior to the Shinto-Buddhism separation, he was revered as {{ill|Sekison Daigongen|ja|石尊大権現|qq=draft|qq=draft}}). * The subsidiary shrine (oku-sha) enshrines {{ill|Raijin|ja|大雷神|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Ōi-katsuchi-no-kami; known as {{ill|Ōtengu|ja|大天狗|qq=draft|qq=draft}} during the syncretic period). * The subsidiary shrine (zen-sha) enshrines {{ill|Takaokami|ja|高龗神|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Takaokami; known as {{ill|Kotenko|ja|小天狗|qq=draft|qq=draft}} during the syncretic period). This arrangement—enshrining Ōyamatsumi along with the subsidiary deities Raijin and Takaokami—is identical to that of the shrine in {{ill|Ehime Prefecture|ja|愛媛県|qq=draft|qq=draft}} known as {{ill|Ōyamatsumi Shrine|ja|大山祇神社|1=Ōyamazumi Shrine|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, although these deities were enshrined only after the separation of Shinto and Buddhism in the Meiji period. During the Edo period, when Shinto and Buddhism were syncretized, the main shrine originally enshrined {{ill|Sekison Daigongen|ja|石尊大権現|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, as the sacred stone ({{ill|Reisekki|ja|霊石|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) at the summit served as his manifestation. In the subsidiary shrines, {{ill|Ōtengu|ja|大天狗|qq=draft|qq=draft}} was enshrined in the oku-sha and {{ill|Kotenko|ja|小天狗|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in the zen-sha. == Cultural Importance == === Oyama Pilgrimage === During the Edo period the Oyama Pilgrimage was a tradition where worshippers formed groups ("{{ill|Kō (lecture)|lt=Kō|en|qq=draft|qq=draft}}") to visit the shrine. This pilgrimage, coupled with the "Oyama Kaido" pathway played a role in shaping culture by inspiring rakugo stories and ukiyo e artworks. In 2008 this pilgrimage was designated as a Heritage Site due to its cultural significance. === Osamedachi Tradition === A tradition stemming from a tale about Minamoto no Yoritomo offering a sword to the shrine the Osamedachi custom involves presenting swords that can reach lengths of up to 6 meters. === Kagura Dance === Imported from Kasuga Taisha Shrine during the Meiji era the Kagura dance performed at Oyama Afuri Shrine includes dances by boys (Yamato Mai) and girls (Miko dance) spanning age groups, from elementary school students to adults. The Sendoshi Ryokan originally built to host worshippers has transformed into an inn that provides lodging and dining services. It stands as one of the temple accommodations, in Japan. As for the Oyama Noh tradition it reflects the shrines commitment to peace and harmony tracing its origins back, to the Genroku era. This tradition signifies the bond established among the leaders of Mt. Oyama through their embrace of Noh performances. == Access == === To the Lower Shrine === ; Public Transportation * From the north exit of the {{ill|Odakyu Odawara Line|ja|小田急小田原線|qq=draft|qq=draft}} at {{ill|Isehara Station|ja|伊勢原駅|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, take Bus Route 10 operated by {{ill|Kanagawa Chūō Kōtsū|ja|神奈川中央交通西|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, alight at the final stop ("Ōyama Cable" bound), which takes approximately 25 minutes. *** Then walk about 15 minutes (approximately 600 meters) from the Ōyama Cable Car Station. ; By Car * Accessible via the {{ill|Shin-Tōmei Expressway|ja|新東名高速道路|qq=draft|qq=draft}} at the {{ill|Isehara Ōyama Interchange|ja|伊勢原大山インターチェンジ|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, then via {{ill|Kanagawa Prefectural Road 611|ja|神奈川県道611号大山板戸線|qq=draft|qq=draft}}; municipal parking is available (about a 15-minute walk from the parking lot to the Ōyama Cable Car Station). === To the Main Shrine === * Ascend the mountain Oyama - Kanagawa|url=https://en.japantravel.com/kanagawa/afuri-shrine-on-mt-oyama/4043|access-date=2024-03-29|website=JapanTravel|language=en}} '''{{ill|Oyama Afuri Shrine|ja|大山阿夫利神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=draft}}''' (Oyama Afuri Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=draft}} located in {{ill|Isehara City|ja|伊勢原市|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Kanagawa Prefecture|ja|神奈川県|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=draft}}, situated on {{ill|Oyama|ja|大山|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=draft}} (also known as '''Amefuri-yama'''〈{{ill|Amefuri-yama|ja|雨降山|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=draft}}〉). It is recorded in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=draft}} from the {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=draft}} period (Enchō 5, {{ill|927|ja|927th year|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=draft}}) as one of the thirteen shrines (small shrines) of the {{ill|Engishiki-shiki Naishinsha Jūsansha|ja|延喜式内社十三社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=draft}} in {{ill|Sagami Province|ja|相模国|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=draft}}. Under the [[Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines]], it was classified as a prefectural shrine (Ken-sha) and is currently designated as a [[Beppyo Shrine|Beppyo shrine]] by the {{ill|Jinja Honchō|ja|神社本庁|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=draft}}. The shrine is composed of two parts: the main shrine (honsha), which includes the inner shrine (okusha) and the front shrine (zensha) located at the summit of Oyama, and the lower shrine (gesha) located on the mid-slope.[http://www.afuri.or.jp/about/map/]{{ill|About Oyama Afuri Shrine|ja|大山阿夫利神社について：境内のご案内|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=draft}} (Official site of Oyama Afuri Shrine). The lower shrine is accessible via the {{ill|Oyama Cable Car|ja|大山ケーブルカー|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=draft}} operated by {{ill|Oyama Kankō Dentetsu|ja|大山観光電鉄|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=draft}}. == History == [[File:Pilgrims at the Roben waterfall, Oyama.jpg|thumb|left|245px|“Ōyama Sekison Raben-taki no Zu” by {{ill|Utagawa Kuniyoshi|ja|歌川国芳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=draft}} (Art name: Ichiyūsai), painted circa 1819–1820 (Bunsei 2–3). Men praying at the waterfall of Ōyama Sekison (current Oyama Afuri Shrine).]] {{ill|Oyama|ja|大山|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=draft}} has long been revered as an object of mountain worship. Excavations at its summit have uncovered {{ill|Jomon pottery|ja|縄文土器|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=draft}} used in rituals.[http://www.afuri.or.jp/about/]{{ill|About Oyama Afuri Shrine|ja|大山阿夫利神社について|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=draft}} (Official site of Oyama Afuri Shrine) It is also known as “{{ill|Amefuri-yama|ja|雨降山|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=draft}}” because clouds and mist frequently gather at the summit, which are believed to bring rain, and it was revered as a rain-making deity. In addition, worship of a giant stone ({{ill|Iwa-za|ja|磐座|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=draft}}) at the summit and of the twin waterfalls on the mountainside as sacred water sources is also observed.[[宝賀寿男]], “Section 3: The Early Branches of Clans in Kinai and Tōkoku – Part 2: Musashi no Kuni no Kunizukuri and the Provincial Clans of Tōkoku”, in “Studies on Ancient Clans, No. 16: The Rise and Fall of the Izumo Kingdom” (青垣出版, 2020), pp.263–264. According to tradition, Ōyama Afuri Shrine was founded during the reign of {{ill|Sujin-tennō|ja|崇神天皇|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=draft}} (around the 3rd century BC, though this is considered legendary rather than historical). The {{ill|Engishiki-shiki Shinnamōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=draft}}, compiled during the Engishiki period, records the shrine as “Afuri Shrine” in its 5th year ({{ill|927|ja|927th year|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=draft}}) and classifies it as a minor shrine among the thirteen shrines of the {{ill|Engishiki-shiki Naishinsha Jūsansha|ja|延喜式内社十三社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=draft}} in {{ill|Sagami Province|ja|相模国|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=draft}}. [[simple:user:immanuelle/Oyama Afuri Shrine]] == Enshrined Deities == * The primary deity enshrined at the lower shrine is {{ill|Ōyamatsumi|ja|大山祇神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=draft}} (Ōyamatsumi-no-kami). * The main shrine enshrines {{ill|Ōyamatsumi|ja|大山祇神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=draft}} as its principal deity (prior to the Shinto-Buddhism separation, he was revered as {{ill|Sekison Daigongen|ja|石尊大権現|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=draft}}). * The subsidiary shrine (oku-sha) enshrines {{ill|Raijin|ja|大雷神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=draft}} (Ōi-katsuchi-no-kami; known as {{ill|Ōtengu|ja|大天狗|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=draft}} during the syncretic period). * The subsidiary shrine (zen-sha) enshrines {{ill|Takaokami|ja|高龗神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=draft}} (Takaokami; known as {{ill|Kotenko|ja|小天狗|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=draft}} during the syncretic period). This arrangement—enshrining Ōyamatsumi along with the subsidiary deities Raijin and Takaokami—is identical to that of the shrine in {{ill|Ehime Prefecture|ja|愛媛県|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=draft}} known as {{ill|Ōyamatsumi Shrine|ja|大山祇神社|1=Ōyamazumi Shrine|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=draft}}, although these deities were enshrined only after the separation of Shinto and Buddhism in the Meiji period. During the Edo period, when Shinto and Buddhism were syncretized, the main shrine originally enshrined {{ill|Sekison Daigongen|ja|石尊大権現|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=draft}}, as the sacred stone ({{ill|Reisekki|ja|霊石|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=draft}}) at the summit served as his manifestation. In the subsidiary shrines, {{ill|Ōtengu|ja|大天狗|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=draft}} was enshrined in the oku-sha and {{ill|Kotenko|ja|小天狗|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=draft}} in the zen-sha. == Cultural Importance == === Oyama Pilgrimage === During the Edo period the Oyama Pilgrimage was a tradition where worshippers formed groups ("{{ill|Kō (lecture)|lt=Kō|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=draft}}") to visit the shrine. This pilgrimage, coupled with the "Oyama Kaido" pathway played a role in shaping culture by inspiring rakugo stories and ukiyo e artworks. In 2008 this pilgrimage was designated as a Heritage Site due to its cultural significance. === Osamedachi Tradition === A tradition stemming from a tale about Minamoto no Yoritomo offering a sword to the shrine the Osamedachi custom involves presenting swords that can reach lengths of up to 6 meters. === Kagura Dance === Imported from Kasuga Taisha Shrine during the Meiji era the Kagura dance performed at Oyama Afuri Shrine includes dances by boys (Yamato Mai) and girls (Miko dance) spanning age groups, from elementary school students to adults. The Sendoshi Ryokan originally built to host worshippers has transformed into an inn that provides lodging and dining services. It stands as one of the temple accommodations, in Japan. As for the Oyama Noh tradition it reflects the shrines commitment to peace and harmony tracing its origins back, to the Genroku era. This tradition signifies the bond established among the leaders of Mt. Oyama through their embrace of Noh performances. == Access == === To the Lower Shrine === ; Public Transportation * From the north exit of the {{ill|Odakyu Odawara Ōyama Cable Car Station. ; By Car * Accessible via the {{ill|Shin-Tōmei Expressway|ja|新東名高速道路|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=draft}} at the {{ill|Isehara Ōyama Interchange|ja|伊勢原大山インターチェンジ|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=draft}}, then via {{ill|Kanagawa Prefectural Road 611|ja|神奈川県道611号大山板戸線|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=draft}}; municipal parking is available (about a
