Men praying at the waterfall of Ōyama Sekison (current Oyama Afuri Shrine).]] {{ill|Oyama|ja|大山|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=draft}} has long been revered as an object of mountain worship. Excavations at its summit have uncovered {{ill|Jomon pottery|ja|縄文土器|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=draft}} used in rituals.[http://www.afuri.or.jp/about/]{{ill|About Oyama Afuri Shrine|ja|大山阿夫利神社について|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=draft}} (Official site of Oyama Afuri Shrine) It is also known as “{{ill|Amefuri-yama|ja|雨降山|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=draft}}” because clouds and mist frequently gather at the summit, which are believed to bring rain, and it was revered as a rain-making deity. In addition, worship of a giant stone ({{ill|Iwa-za|ja|磐座|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=draft}}) at the summit and of the twin waterfalls on the mountainside as sacred water sources is also observed.[[宝賀寿男]], “Section 3: The Early Branches of Clans in Kinai and Tōkoku – Part 2: Musashi no Kuni no Kunizukuri and the Provincial Clans of Tōkoku”, in “Studies on Ancient Clans, No. 16: The Rise and Fall of the Izumo Kingdom” (青垣出版, 2020), pp.263–264. According to tradition, Ōyama Afuri Shrine was founded during the reign of {{ill|Sujin-tennō|ja|崇神天皇|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=draft}} (around the 3rd century BC, though this is considered legendary rather than historical). The {{ill|Engishiki-shiki Shinnamōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=draft}}, compiled during the Engishiki period, records the shrine as “Afuri Shrine” in its 5th year ({{ill|927|ja|927th year|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=draft}}) and classifies it as a minor shrine among the thirteen shrines of the {{ill|Engishiki-shiki Naishinsha Jūsansha|ja|延喜式内社十三社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=draft}} in {{ill|Sagami Province|ja|相模国|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=draft}}. == Enshrined Deities == * The primary deity enshrined at the lower shrine is {{ill|Ōyamatsumi|ja|大山祇神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=draft}} (Ōyamatsumi-no-kami). * The main shrine enshrines {{ill|Ōyamatsumi|ja|大山祇神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=draft}} as its principal deity (prior to the Shinto-Buddhism separation, he was revered as {{ill|Sekison Daigongen|ja|石尊大権現|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=draft}}). * The subsidiary shrine (oku-sha) enshrines {{ill|Raijin|ja|大雷神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=draft}} (Ōi-katsuchi-no-kami; known as {{ill|Ōtengu|ja|大天狗|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=draft}} during the syncretic period). * The subsidiary shrine (zen-sha) enshrines {{ill|Takaokami|ja|高龗神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=draft}} (Takaokami; known as {{ill|Kotenko|ja|小天狗|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=draft}} during the syncretic period). This arrangement—enshrining Ōyamatsumi along with the subsidiary deities Raijin and Takaokami—is identical to that of the shrine in {{ill|Ehime Prefecture|ja|愛媛県|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=draft}} known as {{ill|Ōyamatsumi Shrine|ja|大山祇神社|1=Ōyamazumi Shrine|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=draft}}, although these deities were enshrined only after the separation of Shinto and Buddhism in the Meiji period. During the Edo period, when Shinto and Buddhism were syncretized, the main shrine originally enshrined {{ill|Sekison Daigongen|ja|石尊大権現|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=draft}}, as the sacred stone ({{ill|Reisekki|ja|霊石|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=draft}}) at the summit served as his manifestation. In the subsidiary shrines, {{ill|Ōtengu|ja|大天狗|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=draft}} was enshrined in the oku-sha and {{ill|Kotenko|ja|小天狗|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=draft}} in the zen-sha. == Cultural Importance == === Oyama Pilgrimage === During the Edo period the Oyama Pilgrimage was a tradition where worshippers formed groups ("{{ill|Kō (lecture)|lt=Kō|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=draft}}") to visit the shrine. This pilgrimage, coupled with the "Oyama Kaido" pathway played a role in shaping culture by inspiring rakugo stories and ukiyo e artworks. In 2008 this pilgrimage was designated as a Heritage Site due to its cultural significance. === Osamedachi Tradition === A tradition stemming from a tale about Minamoto no Yoritomo offering a sword to the shrine the Osamedachi custom involves presenting swords that can reach lengths of up to 6 meters. === Kagura Dance === Imported from Kasuga Taisha Shrine during the Meiji era the Kagura dance performed at Oyama Afuri Shrine includes dances by boys (Yamato Mai) and girls (Miko dance) spanning age groups, from elementary school students to adults. The Sendoshi Ryokan originally built to host worshippers has transformed into an inn that provides lodging and dining services. It stands as one of the temple accommodations, in Japan. As for the Oyama Noh tradition it reflects the shrines commitment to peace and harmony tracing its origins back, to the Genroku era. This tradition signifies the bond established among the leaders of Mt. Oyama through their embrace of Noh performances. == Access == === To the Lower Shrine === ; Public Transportation * From the north exit of the {{ill|Odakyu Odawara Line|ja|小田急小田原線|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=draft}} at {{ill|Isehara Station|ja|伊勢原駅|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=draft}}, take Bus Route 10 operated by {{ill|Kanagawa Chūō Kōtsū|ja|神奈川中央交通西|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=draft}}, alight at the final stop ("Ōyama Cable" bound), which takes approximately 25 minutes. *** Then walk about 15 minutes (approximately 600 meters) from the Ōyama Cable Car Station. ; By Car * Accessible via the {{ill|Shin-Tōmei Expressway|ja|新東名高速道路|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=draft}} at the {{ill|Isehara Ōyama Interchange|ja|伊勢原大山インターチェンジ|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=draft}}, then via {{ill|Kanagawa Prefectural Road 611|ja|神奈川県道611号大山板戸線|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=draft}}; municipal parking is available (about a 15-minute walk from the parking lot to the Ōyama Cable Car Station). === To the Main Shrine === * Ascend the mountain from the lower shrine (approximately 90 minutes). ==Gallery== File:Ohyama Afuri jinja 2009.jpg|alt=大山阿夫利神社 2009|Ōyama Afuri Jinja in 2009 File:Ooyama afurijinjya.jpg|alt=大山阿夫利神社|Ooyama Afurijinjya File:Oyama Aburi Shrine 01.jpg|alt=大山阿夫利神社01|Oyama Aburi Shrine 01 File:Oyama Aburi Shrine 02.jpg|alt=大山阿夫利神社02|Oyama Aburi Shrine 02 File:Oyama afuri shrine gesha shishiyama.jpg|alt=大山阿夫利神社 月車獅子山|Oyama Afuri Shrine Gesha Shishiyama File:Oyama-Afuri jinja 201709a.jpg|alt=大山阿夫利神社 2017th year 9月|Oyama-Afuri Jinja, September 2017 File:Oyama-afuri-jinja, shimosha, haiden.jpg|alt=下社拝殿|Lower Shrine Haiden (Worship Hall) File:Oyama-afuri-jinja, shimosha, tozanguchi.jpg|alt=下社登山口|Lower Shrine Entrance (Tozanguchi) File:Ōyama Afuri Jinja - This arrangement—enshrining Ōyamatsumi along with the subsidiary deities Raijin and Takaokami—is identical to that of the shrine in {{ill|Ehime Prefecture|ja|愛媛県|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} known as {{ill|Ōyamatsumi Shrine|ja|大山祇神社|1=Ōyamazumi Shrine|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, although these deities were enshrined only after the separation of Shinto and Buddhism in the Meiji period. During the Edo period, when Shinto and Buddhism were syncretized, the main shrine originally enshrined {{ill|Sekison Daigongen|ja|石尊大権現|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, as the sacred stone ({{ill|Reisekki|ja|霊石|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) at the summit served as his manifestation. In the subsidiary shrines, {{ill|Ōtengu|ja|大天狗|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} was enshrined in the oku-sha and {{ill|Kotenko|ja|小天狗|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in the zen-sha. == Cultural Importance == === Oyama Pilgrimage === During the Edo period the Oyama Pilgrimage was a tradition where worshippers formed groups ("{{ill|Kō (lecture)|lt=Kō|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}") to visit the shrine. This pilgrimage, coupled with the "Oyama Kaido" pathway played a role in shaping culture by inspiring rakugo stories and ukiyo e artworks. In 2008 this pilgrimage was designated as a Heritage Site due to its cultural significance. === Osamedachi Tradition === A tradition stemming from a tale about Minamoto no Yoritomo offering a sword to the shrine the Osamedachi custom involves presenting swords that can reach lengths of up to 6 meters. === Kagura Dance === Imported from Kasuga Taisha Shrine during the Meiji era the Kagura dance performed at Oyama Afuri Shrine includes dances by boys (Yamato Mai) and girls (Miko dance) spanning age groups, from elementary school students to adults. The Sendoshi Ryokan originally built to host worshippers has transformed into an inn that provides lodging and dining services. It stands as one of the temple accommodations, in Japan. As for the Oyama Noh tradition it reflects the shrines commitment to peace and harmony tracing its origins back, to the Genroku era. This tradition signifies the bond established among the leaders of Mt. Oyama through their embrace of Noh performances. == Access == === To the Lower Shrine === ; Public Transportation * From the north exit of the {{ill|Odakyu Odawara Line|ja|小田急小田原線|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} at {{ill|Isehara Station|ja|伊勢原駅|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, take Bus Route 10 operated by {{ill|Kanagawa Chūō Kōtsū|ja|神奈川中央交通西|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, alight at the final stop ("Ōyama Cable" bound), which takes approximately 25 minutes. *** Then walk about 15 minutes (approximately 600 meters) from the Ōyama Cable Car Station. ; By Car * Accessible via the {{ill|Shin-Tōmei Expressway|ja|新東名高速道路|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} at the {{ill|Isehara Ōyama Interchange|ja|伊勢原大山インターチェンジ|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, then via {{ill|Kanagawa Prefectural Road 611|ja|神奈川県道611号大山板戸線|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}; municipal parking is available (about a 15-minute walk from the parking lot to the Ōyama Cable Car Station). === To the Main Shrine === * Ascend the mountain from the lower shrine (approximately 90 minutes). ==Gallery== File:Ohyama Afuri jinja 2009.jpg|alt=大山阿夫利神社 2009|Ōyama Afuri Jinja in 2009 File:Ooyama afurijinjya.jpg|alt=大山阿夫利神社|Ooyama Afurijinjya File:Oyama Aburi Shrine 01.jpg|alt=大山阿夫利神社01|Oyama Aburi Shrine 01 File:Oyama Aburi Shrine 02.jpg|alt=大山阿夫利神社02|Oyama Aburi Shrine 02 File:Oyama afuri shrine gesha shishiyama.jpg|alt=大山阿夫利神社 月車獅子山|Oyama Afuri Shrine Gesha Shishiyama File:Oyama-Afuri jinja 201709a.jpg|alt=大山阿夫利神社 2017th year 9月|Oyama-Afuri Jinja, September 2017 File:Oyama-afuri-jinja, shimosha, haiden.jpg|alt=下社拝殿|Lower Shrine Haiden (Worship Hall) File:Oyama-afuri-jinja, shimosha, tozanguchi.jpg|alt=下社登山口|Lower Shrine Entrance (Tozanguchi) File:Ōyama Afuri Jinja - Oyama - Kanagawa|url=https://en.japantravel.com/kanagawa/afuri-shrine-on-mt-oyama/4043|access-date=2024-03-29|website=JapanTravel|language=en}} '''{{ill|Oyama Afuri Shrine|ja|大山阿夫利神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}''' (Oyama Afuri Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} located in {{ill|Isehara City|ja|伊勢原市|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Kanagawa Prefecture|ja|神奈川県|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, situated on {{ill|Oyama|ja|大山|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (also known as '''Amefuri-yama'''〈{{ill|Amefuri-yama|ja|雨降山|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}〉). It is recorded in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} from the {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} period (Enchō 5, {{ill|927|ja|927th year|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) as one of the thirteen shrines (small shrines) of the {{ill|Engishiki-shiki Naishinsha Jūsansha|ja|延喜式内社十三社|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in {{ill|Sagami Province|ja|相模国|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Under the [[Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines]], it was classified as a prefectural shrine (Ken-sha) and is currently designated as a [[Beppyo Shrine|Beppyo shrine]] by the {{ill|Jinja Honchō|ja|神社本庁|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. The shrine is composed of two parts: the main shrine (honsha), which includes the inner shrine (okusha) and the front shrine (zensha) located at the summit of Oyama, and the lower shrine (gesha) located on the mid-slope.[http://www.afuri.or.jp/about/map/]{{ill|About Oyama Afuri Shrine|ja|大山阿夫利神社について：境内のご案内|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Official site of Oyama Afuri Shrine). The lower shrine is accessible via the {{ill|Oyama Cable Car|ja|大山ケーブルカー|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} operated by {{ill|Oyama Kankō Dentetsu|ja|大山観光電鉄|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. == History == [[File:Pilgrims at the Roben waterfall, Oyama.jpg|thumb|left|245px|“Ōyama Sekison Raben-taki no Zu” by {{ill|Utagawa Kuniyoshi|ja|歌川国芳|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Art name: Ichiyūsai), painted circa 1819–1820 (Bunsei 2–3). Men praying at the waterfall of Ōyama Sekison (current Oyama Afuri Shrine).]] {{ill|Oyama|ja|大山|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} has long been revered as an object of mountain worship. Excavations at its summit have uncovered {{ill|Jomon pottery|ja|縄文土器|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} used in rituals.[http://www.afuri.or.jp/about/]{{ill|About Oyama Afuri Shrine|ja|大山阿夫利神社について|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Official site of Oyama Afuri Shrine) It is also known as “{{ill|Amefuri-yama|ja|雨降山|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}” because clouds and mist frequently gather at the summit, which are believed to bring rain, and it was revered as a rain-making deity. Oyama through their embrace of Noh performances. == Access == === To the Lower Shrine === ; Public Transportation * From the north exit of the {{ill|Odakyu Odawara Line|ja|小田急小田原線|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} at {{ill|Isehara Station|ja|伊勢原駅|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, take Bus Route 10 operated by {{ill|Kanagawa Chūō Kōtsū|ja|神奈川中央交通西|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, alight at the final stop ("Ōyama Cable" bound), which takes approximately 25 minutes. *** Then walk about 15 minutes (approximately 600 meters) from the Ōyama Cable Car Station. ; By Car * Accessible via the {{ill|Shin-Tōmei Expressway|ja|新東名高速道路|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} at the {{ill|Isehara Ōyama Interchange|ja|伊勢原大山インターチェンジ|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, then via {{ill|Kanagawa Prefectural Road 611|ja|神奈川県道611号大山板戸線|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}; municipal parking is available (about a 15-minute walk from the parking lot to the Ōyama Cable Car Station). === To the Main Shrine === * Ascend the mountain from the lower shrine (approximately 90 minutes). ==Gallery== File:Ohyama Afuri jinja 2009.jpg|alt=大山阿夫利神社 2009|Ōyama Afuri Jinja in 2009 File:Ooyama afurijinjya.jpg|alt=大山阿夫利神社|Ooyama Afurijinjya File:Oyama Aburi Shrine 01.jpg|alt=大山阿夫利神社01|Oyama Aburi Shrine 01 File:Oyama Aburi Shrine 02.jpg|alt=大山阿夫利神社02|Oyama Aburi Shrine 02 File:Oyama afuri shrine gesha shishiyama.jpg|alt=大山阿夫利神社 月車獅子山|Oyama Afuri Shrine Gesha Shishiyama File:Oyama-Afuri jinja 201709a.jpg|alt=大山阿夫利神社 2017th year 9月|Oyama-Afuri Jinja, September 2017 File:Oyama-afuri-jinja, shimosha, haiden.jpg|alt=下社拝殿|Lower Shrine Haiden (Worship Hall) File:Oyama-afuri-jinja, shimosha, tozanguchi.jpg|alt=下社登山口|Lower Shrine Entrance (Tozanguchi) File:Ōyama Afuri Jinja - It is a [[Beppyo shrine]], or a shrine that is particularly notable in a certain way with a significant history to it.{{Cite web|title=Learn about Oyama Afuri Shrine - Oyama Afuri Shrine|url=https://www.afuri.or.jp/en/about/|access-date=2024-03-29|language=en-US}}{{Cite web|date=2023-12-28|title=Oyama Afuri Shrine|url=https://www.afuri.or.jp/en/|access-date=2024-03-29|language=en-US}}{{Cite web|date=2013-04-07|title=Afuri Shrine on Mt. Oyama - Kanagawa|url=https://en.japantravel.com/kanagawa/afuri-shrine-on-mt-oyama/4043|access-date=2024-03-29|website=JapanTravel|language=en}} '''{{ill|Oyama Afuri Shrine|ja|大山阿夫利神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}''' (Oyama Afuri Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} located in {{ill|Isehara City|ja|伊勢原市|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Kanagawa Prefecture|ja|神奈川県|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, situated on {{ill|Oyama|ja|大山|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (also known as '''Amefuri-yama'''〈{{ill|Amefuri-yama|ja|雨降山|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}〉). It is recorded in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} from the {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} period (Enchō 5, {{ill|927|ja|927th year|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) as one of the thirteen shrines (small shrines) of the {{ill|Engishiki-shiki Naishinsha Jūsansha|ja|延喜式内社十三社|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in {{ill|Sagami Province|ja|相模国|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Under the [[Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines]], it was classified as a prefectural shrine (Ken-sha) and is currently designated as a [[Beppyo Shrine|Beppyo shrine]] by the {{ill|Jinja Honchō|ja|神社本庁|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. The shrine is composed of two parts: the main shrine (honsha), which includes the inner shrine (okusha) and the front shrine (zensha) located at the summit of Oyama, and the lower shrine (gesha) located on the mid-slope.[http://www.afuri.or.jp/about/map/]{{ill|About Oyama Afuri Shrine|ja|大山阿夫利神社について：境内のご案内|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Official site of Oyama Afuri Shrine). The lower shrine is accessible via the {{ill|Oyama Cable Car|ja|大山ケーブルカー|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} operated by {{ill|Oyama Kankō Dentetsu|ja|大山観光電鉄|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. == History == [[File:Pilgrims at the Roben waterfall, Oyama.jpg|thumb|left|245px|“Ōyama Sekison Raben-taki no Zu” by {{ill|Utagawa Kuniyoshi|ja|歌川国芳|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Art name: Ichiyūsai), painted circa 1819–1820 (Bunsei 2–3). Men praying at the waterfall of Ōyama Sekison (current Oyama Afuri Shrine).]] {{ill|Oyama|ja|大山|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} has long been revered as an object of mountain worship. Excavations at its summit have uncovered {{ill|Jomon pottery|ja|縄文土器|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} used in rituals.[http://www.afuri.or.jp/about/]{{ill|About Oyama Afuri Shrine|ja|大山阿夫利神社について|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Official site of Oyama Afuri Shrine) It is also known as “{{ill|Amefuri-yama|ja|雨降山|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}” because clouds and mist frequently gather at the summit, which are believed to bring rain, and it was revered as a rain-making deity. In addition, worship of a giant stone ({{ill|Iwa-za|ja|磐座|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) at the summit and of the twin waterfalls on the mountainside as sacred water sources is also observed.[[宝賀寿男]], “Section 3: The Early Branches of Clans in Kinai and Tōkoku – Part 2: Musashi no Kuni no Kunizukuri and the Provincial Clans of Tōkoku”, in “Studies on Ancient Clans, No. 16: The Rise and Fall of the Izumo Kingdom” (青垣出版, 2020), pp.263–264. According to tradition, Ōyama Afuri Shrine was founded during the reign of {{ill|Sujin-tennō|ja|崇神天皇|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (around the 3rd century BC, though this is considered legendary rather than historical). The {{ill|Engishiki-shiki Shinnamōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, compiled during the Engishiki period, records the shrine as “Afuri Shrine” in its 5th year ({{ill|927|ja|927th year|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) and classifies it as a minor shrine among the thirteen shrines of the {{ill|Engishiki-shiki Naishinsha Jūsansha|ja|延喜式内社十三社|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in {{ill|Sagami Province|ja|相模国|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. == Enshrined Deities == * The primary deity enshrined at the lower shrine is {{ill|Ōyamatsumi|ja|大山祇神|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Ōyamatsumi-no-kami). * The main shrine enshrines {{ill|Ōyamatsumi|ja|大山祇神|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} as its principal deity (prior to the Shinto-Buddhism separation, he was revered as {{ill|Sekison Daigongen|ja|石尊大権現|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}). * The subsidiary shrine (oku-sha) enshrines {{ill|Raijin|ja|大雷神|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Ōi-katsuchi-no-kami; known as {{ill|Ōtengu|ja|大天狗|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} during the syncretic period). * The subsidiary shrine (zen-sha) enshrines {{ill|Takaokami|ja|高龗神|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Takaokami; known as {{ill|Kotenko|ja|小天狗|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} during the syncretic period). This arrangement—enshrining Ōyamatsumi along with the subsidiary deities Raijin and Takaokami—is identical to that of the shrine in {{ill|Ehime Prefecture|ja|愛媛県|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} known as {{ill|Ōyamatsumi Shrine|ja|大山祇神社|1=Ōyamazumi Shrine|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, although these deities were enshrined only after the separation of Shinto and Buddhism in the Meiji period. During the Edo period, when Shinto and Buddhism were syncretized, the main shrine originally enshrined {{ill|Sekison Daigongen|ja|石尊大権現|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, as the sacred stone ({{ill|Reisekki|ja|霊石|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) at the summit served as his manifestation. In the subsidiary shrines, {{ill|Ōtengu|ja|大天狗|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} was enshrined in the oku-sha and {{ill|Kotenko|ja|小天狗|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in the zen-sha. == Cultural Importance == === Oyama Pilgrimage === During the Edo period the Oyama Pilgrimage was a tradition where worshippers formed groups ("{{ill|Kō (lecture)|lt=Kō|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}") to visit the shrine. This pilgrimage, coupled with the "Oyama Kaido" pathway played a role in shaping culture by inspiring rakugo stories and ukiyo e artworks. In 2008 this pilgrimage was designated as a Heritage Site due to its cultural significance. === Osamedachi Tradition === A tradition stemming from a tale about Minamoto no Yoritomo offering a sword to the shrine the Osamedachi custom involves presenting swords that can reach lengths of up to 6 meters. === Kagura Dance === Imported from Kasuga Taisha Shrine during the Meiji era the Kagura dance performed at Oyama Afuri Shrine includes dances by boys (Yamato Mai) and girls (Miko dance) spanning age groups, from elementary school students to adults. The Sendoshi Ryokan originally built to host worshippers has transformed into an inn that provides lodging and dining services. It stands as one of the temple accommodations, in Japan. As for the Oyama Noh tradition it reflects the shrines commitment to peace and harmony tracing its origins back, to the Genroku era. This tradition signifies the bond established among the leaders of Mt. Oyama through their embrace of Noh performances. == Access == === To the Lower Shrine === ; Public Transportation * From the north exit of the {{ill|Odakyu Odawara Line|ja|小田急小田原線|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} at {{ill|Isehara Station|ja|伊勢原駅|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, take Bus Route 10 operated by {{ill|Kanagawa Chūō Kōtsū|ja|神奈川中央交通西|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, alight at the final stop ("Ōyama Cable" bound), which takes approximately 25 minutes. *** Then walk about 15 minutes (approximately 600 meters) from the Ōyama Cable Car Station. ; By Car * Accessible via the {{ill|Shin-Tōmei Expressway|ja|新東名高速道路|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} at the {{ill|Isehara Ōyama Interchange|ja|伊勢原大山インターチェンジ|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, then via {{ill|Kanagawa Prefectural Road 611|ja|神奈川県道611号大山板戸線|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}; municipal parking is available (about a 15-minute walk from the parking lot to the Ōyama Cable Car Station). === To the Main Shrine === * Ascend the mountain from the lower shrine (approximately 90 minutes). ==Gallery== File:Ohyama Afuri jinja 2009.jpg|alt=大山阿夫利神社 2009|Ōyama Afuri Jinja in 2009 File:Ooyama afurijinjya.jpg|alt=大山阿夫利神社|Ooyama Afurijinjya File:Oyama Aburi Shrine 01.jpg|alt=大山阿夫利神社01|Oyama Aburi Shrine 01 File:Oyama Aburi Shrine 02.jpg|alt=大山阿夫利神社02|Oyama Aburi Shrine 02 File:Oyama afuri shrine gesha shishiyama.jpg|alt=大山阿夫利神社 月車獅子山|Oyama Afuri Shrine Gesha Shishiyama File:Oyama-Afuri jinja 201709a.jpg|alt=大山阿夫利神社 2017th year 9月|Oyama-Afuri Jinja, September 2017 File:Oyama-afuri-jinja, shimosha, haiden.jpg|alt=下社拝殿|Lower Shrine Haiden (Worship Hall) File:Oyama-afuri-jinja, shimosha, tozanguchi.jpg|alt=下社登山口|Lower Shrine Entrance (Tozanguchi) File:Ōyama Afuri Jinja - It is a [[Beppyo shrine]], or a shrine that is particularly notable in a certain way with a significant history to it.{{Cite web|title=Learn about Oyama Afuri Shrine - Oyama Afuri Shrine|url=https://www.afuri.or.jp/en/about/|access-date=2024-03-29|language=en-US}}{{Cite web|date=2023-12-28|title=Oyama Afuri Shrine|url=https://www.afuri.or.jp/en/|access-date=2024-03-29|language=en-US}}{{Cite web|date=2013-04-07|title=Afuri Shrine on Mt. Oyama - Kanagawa|url=https://en.japantravel.com/kanagawa/afuri-shrine-on-mt-oyama/4043|access-date=2024-03-29|website=JapanTravel|language=en}} '''{{ill|Oyama Afuri Shrine|ja|大山阿夫利神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}''' (Oyama Afuri Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} located in {{ill|Isehara City|ja|伊勢原市|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Kanagawa Prefecture|ja|神奈川県|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, situated on {{ill|Oyama|ja|大山|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (also known as '''Amefuri-yama'''〈{{ill|Amefuri-yama|ja|雨降山|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}〉). It is recorded in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} from the {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} period (Enchō 5, {{ill|927|ja|927th year|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) as one of the thirteen shrines (small shrines) of the {{ill|Engishiki-shiki Naishinsha Jūsansha|ja|延喜式内社十三社|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in {{ill|Sagami Province|ja|相模国|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Under the [[Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines]], it was classified as a prefectural shrine (Ken-sha) and is currently designated as a [[Beppyo Shrine|Beppyo shrine]] by the {{ill|Jinja Honchō|ja|神社本庁|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. The shrine is composed of two parts: the main shrine (honsha), which includes the inner shrine (okusha) and the front shrine (zensha) located at the summit of Oyama, and the lower shrine (gesha) located on the mid-slope.[http://www.afuri.or.jp/about/map/]{{ill|About Oyama Afuri Shrine|ja|大山阿夫利神社について：境内のご案内|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Official site of Oyama Afuri Shrine). The lower shrine is accessible via the {{ill|Oyama Cable Car|ja|大山ケーブルカー|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} operated by {{ill|Oyama Kankō Dentetsu|ja|大山観光電鉄|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. == History == [[File:Pilgrims at the Roben waterfall, Oyama.jpg|thumb|left|245px|“Ōyama Sekison Raben-taki no Zu” by {{ill|Utagawa Kuniyoshi|ja|歌川国芳|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Art name: Ichiyūsai), painted circa 1819–1820 (Bunsei 2–3). Men praying at the waterfall of Ōyama Sekison (current Oyama Afuri Shrine).]] {{ill|Oyama|ja|大山|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} has long been revered as an object of mountain worship. Excavations at its summit have uncovered {{ill|Jomon pottery|ja|縄文土器|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} used in rituals.[http://www.afuri.or.jp/about/]{{ill|About Oyama Afuri Shrine|ja|大山阿夫利神社について|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Official site of Oyama Afuri Shrine) It is also known as “{{ill|Amefuri-yama|ja|雨降山|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}” because clouds and mist frequently gather at the summit, which are believed to bring rain, and it was revered as a rain-making deity. In addition, worship of a giant stone ({{ill|Iwa-za|ja|磐座|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) at the summit and of the twin waterfalls on the mountainside as sacred water sources is also observed.[[宝賀寿男]], “Section 3: The Early Branches of Clans in Kinai and Tōkoku – Part 2: Musashi no Kuni no Kunizukuri and the Provincial Clans of Tōkoku”, in “Studies on Ancient Clans, No. 16: The Rise and Fall of the Izumo Kingdom” (青垣出版, 2020), pp.263–264. According to tradition, Ōyama Afuri Shrine was founded during the reign of {{ill|Sujin-tennō|ja|崇神天皇|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (around the 3rd century BC, though this is considered legendary rather than historical). The {{ill|Engishiki-shiki Shinnamōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, compiled during the Engishiki period, records the shrine as “Afuri Shrine” in its 5th year ({{ill|927|ja|927th year|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) and classifies it as a minor shrine among the thirteen shrines of the {{ill|Engishiki-shiki Naishinsha Jūsansha|ja|延喜式内社十三社|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in {{ill|Sagami Province|ja|相模国|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. == Enshrined Deities == * The primary deity enshrined at the lower shrine is {{ill|Ōyamatsumi|ja|大山祇神|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Ōyamatsumi-no-kami). * The main shrine enshrines {{ill|Ōyamatsumi|ja|大山祇神|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} as its principal deity (prior to the Shinto-Buddhism separation, he was revered as {{ill|Sekison Daigongen|ja|石尊大権現|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}). * The subsidiary shrine (oku-sha) enshrines {{ill|Raijin|ja|大雷神|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Ōi-katsuchi-no-kami; known as {{ill|Ōtengu|ja|大天狗|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} during the syncretic period). * The subsidiary shrine (zen-sha) enshrines {{ill|Takaokami|ja|高龗神|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Takaokami; known as {{ill|Kotenko|ja|小天狗|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} during the syncretic period). This arrangement—enshrining Ōyamatsumi along with the subsidiary deities Raijin and Takaokami—is identical to that of the shrine in {{ill|Ehime Prefecture|ja|愛媛県|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} known as {{ill|Ōyamatsumi Shrine|ja|大山祇神社|1=Ōyamazumi Shrine|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, although these deities were enshrined only after the separation of Shinto and Buddhism in the Meiji period. During the Edo period, when Shinto and Buddhism were syncretized, the main shrine originally enshrined {{ill|Sekison Daigongen|ja|石尊大権現|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, as the sacred stone ({{ill|Reisekki|ja|霊石|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) at the summit served as his manifestation. In the subsidiary shrines, {{ill|Ōtengu|ja|大天狗|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} was enshrined in the oku-sha and {{ill|Kotenko|ja|小天狗|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in the zen-sha. == Cultural Importance == === Oyama Pilgrimage === During the Edo period the Oyama Pilgrimage was a tradition where worshippers formed groups ("{{ill|Kō (lecture)|lt=Kō|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}") to visit the shrine. This pilgrimage, coupled with the "Oyama Kaido" pathway played a role in shaping culture by inspiring rakugo stories and ukiyo e artworks. In 2008 this pilgrimage was designated as a Heritage Site due to its cultural significance. === Osamedachi Tradition === A tradition stemming from a tale about Minamoto no Yoritomo offering a sword to the shrine the Osamedachi custom involves presenting swords that can reach lengths of up to 6 meters. === Kagura Dance === Imported from Kasuga Taisha Shrine during the Meiji era the Kagura dance performed at Oyama Afuri Shrine includes dances by boys (Yamato Mai) and girls (Miko dance) spanning age groups, from elementary school students to adults. The Sendoshi Ryokan originally built to host worshippers has transformed into an inn that provides lodging and dining services. It stands as one of the temple accommodations, in Japan. As for the Oyama Noh tradition it reflects the shrines commitment to peace and harmony tracing its origins back, to the Genroku era. This tradition signifies the bond established among the leaders of Mt. Oyama through their embrace of Noh performances. == Access == === To the Lower Shrine === ; Public Transportation * From the north exit of the {{ill|Odakyu Odawara Line|ja|小田急小田原線|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} at {{ill|Isehara Station|ja|伊勢原駅|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, take Bus Route 10 operated by {{ill|Kanagawa Chūō Kōtsū|ja|神奈川中央交通西|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, alight at the final stop ("Ōyama Cable" bound), which takes approximately 25 minutes. *** Then walk about 15 minutes (approximately 600 meters) from the Ōyama Cable Car Station. ; By Car * Accessible via the {{ill|Shin-Tōmei Expressway|ja|新東名高速道路|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} at the {{ill|Isehara Ōyama Interchange|ja|伊勢原大山インターチェンジ|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, then via {{ill|Kanagawa Prefectural Road 611|ja|神奈川県道611号大山板戸線|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}; municipal parking is available (about a 15-minute walk from the parking lot to the Ōyama Cable Car Station). === To the Main Shrine === * Ascend the mountain from the lower shrine (approximately 90 minutes). ==Gallery== File:Ohyama Afuri jinja 2009.jpg|alt=大山阿夫利神社 2009|Ōyama Afuri Jinja in 2009 File:Ooyama afurijinjya.jpg|alt=大山阿夫利神社|Ooyama Afurijinjya File:Oyama Aburi Shrine 01.jpg|alt=大山阿夫利神社01|Oyama Aburi Shrine 01 File:Oyama Aburi Shrine 02.jpg|alt=大山阿夫利神社02|Oyama Aburi Shrine 02 File:Oyama afuri shrine gesha shishiyama.jpg|alt=大山阿夫利神社 月車獅子山|Oyama Afuri Shrine Gesha Shishiyama File:Oyama-Afuri jinja 201709a.jpg|alt=大山阿夫利神社 2017th year 9月|Oyama-Afuri Jinja, September 2017 File:Oyama-afuri-jinja, shimosha, haiden.jpg|alt=下社拝殿|Lower Shrine Haiden (Worship Hall) File:Oyama-afuri-jinja, shimosha, tozanguchi.jpg|alt=下社登山口|Lower Shrine Entrance (Tozanguchi) File:Ōyama Afuri Jinja - {{ill|Betsuhyō Shrine|ja|別表神社|1=Beppyo Shrine|2=ja|3=別表神社|4=simple|5=Beppyo shrine|6=zh|7=別表神社|8=mr|9=बेप्प्यो तीर्थ|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} |創建 = Tradition: During the reign of {{ill|Sujin-tennō|ja|崇神天皇|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (circa BC 97–BC 30) |例祭 = July 27 |地図 = {{Location map+|Japan Kanagawa|width=210|float=center|caption=|places= {{Location map~|Japan Kanagawa|lat_deg=35|lat_min=26|lat_sec=26|lon_deg=139|lon_min=13|lon_sec=51.8|position=top|label={{ill|Main Shrine|ja|本社|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20}} {{Location map~|Japan Kanagawa|lat_deg=35|lat_min=25|lat_sec=54.7|lon_deg=139|lon_min=14|lon_sec=16.6|position=right|label={{ill|Lower Shrine|ja|下社|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20}}|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| image=大山阿夫利神社 下社拝殿.jpg}} {{OSM Location map|coord={{coord|35.436187|N|139.234166|E}}|fullscreen-option=1|zoom=14|float=center|width=200|caption=|title=|mark-coord1={{coord|35|26|26|N|139|13|51.8|E}}|label1={{ill|Main Shrine|ja|本社|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}|label-pos1=right|mark-size1=8|mark-coord2={{coord|35|25|54.7|N|139|14|16.6|E}}|label2={{ill|Lower Shrine|ja|下社|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}|label-pos2=top|mark-size2=8}} }} {{osm box|w|161550990}} [[File:大山道.png|thumb|right|260px|{{ill|Oyama-dō|ja|大山道|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Main 8 Routes)]] {{ill|Oyama Afuri Shrine|ja|%E5%A4%A7%E5%B1%B1%E9%98%BF%E5%A4%AB%E5%88%A9%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (大山阿夫利神社) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in Isehara City, Kanagawa Prefecture, [[Japan]]. It is a [[Beppyo shrine]], or a shrine that is particularly notable in a certain way with a significant history to it.{{Cite web|title=Learn about Oyama Afuri Shrine - Oyama Afuri Shrine|url=https://www.afuri.or.jp/en/about/|access-date=2024-03-29|language=en-US}}{{Cite web|date=2023-12-28|title=Oyama Afuri Shrine|url=https://www.afuri.or.jp/en/|access-date=2024-03-29|language=en-US}}{{Cite web|date=2013-04-07|title=Afuri Shrine on Mt. Oyama - Kanagawa|url=https://en.japantravel.com/kanagawa/afuri-shrine-on-mt-oyama/4043|access-date=2024-03-29|website=JapanTravel|language=en}} '''{{ill|Oyama Afuri Shrine|ja|大山阿夫利神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}''' (Oyama Afuri Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} located in {{ill|Isehara City|ja|伊勢原市|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Kanagawa Prefecture|ja|神奈川県|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, situated on {{ill|Oyama|ja|大山|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (also known as '''Amefuri-yama'''〈{{ill|Amefuri-yama|ja|雨降山|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}〉). It is recorded in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} from the {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} period (Enchō 5, {{ill|927|ja|927th year|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) as one of the thirteen shrines (small shrines) of the {{ill|Engishiki-shiki Naishinsha Jūsansha|ja|延喜式内社十三社|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in {{ill|Sagami Province|ja|相模国|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Under the [[Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines]], it was classified as a prefectural shrine (Ken-sha) and is currently designated as a [[Beppyo Shrine|Beppyo shrine]] by the {{ill|Jinja Honchō|ja|神社本庁|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. The shrine is composed of two parts: the main shrine (honsha), which includes the inner shrine (okusha) and the front shrine (zensha) located at the summit of Oyama, and the lower shrine (gesha) located on the mid-slope.[http://www.afuri.or.jp/about/map/]{{ill|About Oyama Afuri Shrine|ja|大山阿夫利神社について：境内のご案内|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Official site of Oyama Afuri Shrine). The lower shrine is accessible via the {{ill|Oyama Cable Car|ja|大山ケーブルカー|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} operated by {{ill|Oyama Kankō Dentetsu|ja|大山観光電鉄|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. == History == [[File:Pilgrims at the Roben waterfall, Oyama.jpg|thumb|left|245px|“Ōyama Sekison Raben-taki no Zu” by {{ill|Utagawa Kuniyoshi|ja|歌川国芳|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Art name: Ichiyūsai), painted circa 1819–1820 (Bunsei 2–3). Men praying at the waterfall of Ōyama Sekison (current Oyama Afuri Shrine).]] {{ill|Oyama|ja|大山|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} has long been revered as an object of mountain worship. Excavations at its summit have uncovered {{ill|Jomon pottery|ja|縄文土器|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} used in rituals.[http://www.afuri.or.jp/about/]{{ill|About Oyama Afuri Shrine|ja|大山阿夫利神社について|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Official site of Oyama Afuri Shrine) It is also known as “{{ill|Amefuri-yama|ja|雨降山|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}” because clouds and mist frequently gather at the summit, which are believed to bring rain, and it was revered as a rain-making deity. In addition, worship of a giant stone ({{ill|Iwa-za|ja|磐座|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) at the summit and of the twin waterfalls on the mountainside as sacred water sources is also observed.[[宝賀寿男]], “Section 3: The Early Branches of Clans in Kinai and Tōkoku – Part 2: Musashi no Kuni no Kunizukuri and the Provincial Clans of Tōkoku”, in “Studies on Ancient Clans, No. 16: The Rise and Fall of the Izumo Kingdom” (青垣出版, 2020), pp.263–264. According to tradition, Ōyama Afuri Shrine was founded during the reign of {{ill|Sujin-tennō|ja|崇神天皇|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (around the 3rd century BC, though this is considered legendary rather than historical). The {{ill|Engishiki-shiki Shinnamōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, compiled during the Engishiki period, records the shrine as “Afuri Shrine” in its 5th year ({{ill|927|ja|927th year|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) and classifies it as a minor shrine among the thirteen shrines of the {{ill|Engishiki-shiki Naishinsha Jūsansha|ja|延喜式内社十三社|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in {{ill|Sagami Province|ja|相模国|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. == Enshrined Deities == * The primary deity enshrined at the lower shrine is {{ill|Ōyamatsumi|ja|大山祇神|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Ōyamatsumi-no-kami). * The main shrine enshrines {{ill|Ōyamatsumi|ja|大山祇神|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} as its principal deity (prior to the Shinto-Buddhism separation, he was revered as {{ill|Sekison Daigongen|ja|石尊大権現|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}). * The subsidiary shrine (oku-sha) enshrines {{ill|Raijin|ja|大雷神|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Ōi-katsuchi-no-kami; known as {{ill|Ōtengu|ja|大天狗|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} during the syncretic period). * The subsidiary shrine (zen-sha) enshrines {{ill|Takaokami|ja|高龗神|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Takaokami; known as {{ill|Kotenko|ja|小天狗|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} during the syncretic period). This arrangement—enshrining Ōyamatsumi along with the subsidiary deities Raijin and Takaokami—is identical to that of the shrine in {{ill|Ehime Prefecture|ja|愛媛県|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} known as {{ill|Ōyamatsumi Shrine|ja|大山祇神社|1=Ōyamazumi Shrine|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, although these deities were enshrined only after the separation of Shinto and Buddhism in the Meiji period. During the Edo period, when Shinto and Buddhism were syncretized, the main shrine originally enshrined {{ill|Sekison Daigongen|ja|石尊大権現|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, as the sacred stone ({{ill|Reisekki|ja|霊石|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) at the summit served as his manifestation. In the subsidiary shrines, {{ill|Ōtengu|ja|大天狗|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} was enshrined in the oku-sha and {{ill|Kotenko|ja|小天狗|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in the zen-sha. == Cultural Importance == === Oyama Pilgrimage === During the Edo period the Oyama Pilgrimage was a tradition where worshippers formed groups ("{{ill|Kō (lecture)|lt=Kō|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}") to visit the shrine. This pilgrimage, coupled with the "Oyama Kaido" pathway played a role in shaping culture by inspiring rakugo stories and ukiyo e artworks. In 2008 this pilgrimage was designated as a Heritage Site due to its cultural significance. === Osamedachi Tradition === A tradition stemming from a tale about Minamoto no Yoritomo offering a sword to the shrine the Osamedachi custom involves presenting swords that can reach lengths of up to 6 meters. === Kagura Dance === Imported from Kasuga Taisha Shrine during the Meiji era the Kagura dance performed at Oyama Afuri Shrine includes dances by boys (Yamato Mai) and girls (Miko dance) spanning age groups, from elementary school students to adults. The Sendoshi Ryokan originally built to host worshippers has transformed into an inn that provides lodging and dining services. It stands as one of the temple accommodations, in Japan. As for the Oyama Noh tradition it reflects the shrines commitment to peace and harmony tracing its origins back, to the Genroku era. This tradition signifies the bond established among the leaders of Mt. Oyama through their embrace of Noh performances. == Access == === To the Lower Shrine === ; Public Transportation * From the north exit of the {{ill|Odakyu Odawara Line|ja|小田急小田原線|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} at {{ill|Isehara Station|ja|伊勢原駅|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, take Bus Route 10 operated by {{ill|Kanagawa Chūō Kōtsū|ja|神奈川中央交通西|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, alight at the final stop ("Ōyama Cable" bound), which takes approximately 25 minutes. *** Then walk about 15 minutes (approximately 600 meters) from the Ōyama Cable Car Station. ; By Car * Accessible via the {{ill|Shin-Tōmei Expressway|ja|新東名高速道路|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} at the {{ill|Isehara Ōyama Interchange|ja|伊勢原大山インターチェンジ|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, then via {{ill|Kanagawa Prefectural Road 611|ja|神奈川県道611号大山板戸線|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}; municipal parking is available (about a 15-minute walk from the parking lot to the Ōyama Cable Car Station). === To the Main Shrine === * Ascend the mountain from the lower shrine (approximately 90 minutes). ==Gallery== File:Ohyama Afuri jinja 2009.jpg|alt=大山阿夫利神社 2009|Ōyama Afuri Jinja in 2009 File:Ooyama afurijinjya.jpg|alt=大山阿夫利神社|Ooyama Afurijinjya File:Oyama Aburi Shrine 01.jpg|alt=大山阿夫利神社01|Oyama Aburi Shrine 01 File:Oyama Aburi Shrine 02.jpg|alt=大山阿夫利神社02|Oyama Aburi Shrine 02 File:Oyama afuri shrine gesha shishiyama.jpg|alt=大山阿夫利神社 月車獅子山|Oyama Afuri Shrine Gesha Shishiyama File:Oyama-Afuri jinja 201709a.jpg|alt=大山阿夫利神社 2017th year 9月|Oyama-Afuri Jinja, September 2017 File:Oyama-afuri-jinja, shimosha, haiden.jpg|alt=下社拝殿|Lower Shrine Haiden (Worship Hall) File:Oyama-afuri-jinja, shimosha, tozanguchi.jpg|alt=下社登山口|Lower Shrine Entrance (Tozanguchi) File:Ōyama Afuri Jinja - It is a [[Beppyo shrine]], or a shrine that is particularly notable in a certain way with a significant history to it.{{Cite web|title=Learn about Oyama Afuri Shrine - Oyama Afuri Shrine|url=https://www.afuri.or.jp/en/about/|access-date=2024-03-29|language=en-US}}{{Cite web|date=2023-12-28|title=Oyama Afuri Shrine|url=https://www.afuri.or.jp/en/|access-date=2024-03-29|language=en-US}}{{Cite web|date=2013-04-07|title=Afuri Shrine on Mt. Oyama - Kanagawa|url=https://en.japantravel.com/kanagawa/afuri-shrine-on-mt-oyama/4043|access-date=2024-03-29|website=JapanTravel|language=en}} '''{{ill|Oyama Afuri Shrine|ja|大山阿夫利神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}''' (Oyama Afuri Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} located in {{ill|Isehara City|ja|伊勢原市|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Kanagawa Prefecture|ja|神奈川県|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, situated on {{ill|Oyama|ja|大山|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (also known as '''Amefuri-yama'''〈{{ill|Amefuri-yama|ja|雨降山|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}〉). It is recorded in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} from the {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} period (Enchō 5, {{ill|927|ja|927th year|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) as one of the thirteen shrines (small shrines) of the {{ill|Engishiki-shiki Naishinsha Jūsansha|ja|延喜式内社十三社|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in {{ill|Sagami Province|ja|相模国|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Under the [[Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines]], it was classified as a prefectural shrine (Ken-sha) and is currently designated as a [[Beppyo Shrine|Beppyo shrine]] by the {{ill|Jinja Honchō|ja|神社本庁|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. The shrine is composed of two parts: the main shrine (honsha), which includes the inner shrine (okusha) and the front shrine (zensha) located at the summit of Oyama, and the lower shrine (gesha) located on the mid-slope.[http://www.afuri.or.jp/about/map/]{{ill|About Oyama Afuri Shrine|ja|大山阿夫利神社について：境内のご案内|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Official site of Oyama Afuri Shrine). The lower shrine is accessible via the {{ill|Oyama Cable Car|ja|大山ケーブルカー|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} operated by {{ill|Oyama Kankō Dentetsu|ja|大山観光電鉄|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. == History == [[File:Pilgrims at the Roben waterfall, Oyama.jpg|thumb|left|245px|“Ōyama Sekison Raben-taki no Zu” by {{ill|Utagawa Kuniyoshi|ja|歌川国芳|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Art name: Ichiyūsai), painted circa 1819–1820 (Bunsei 2–3). Men praying at the waterfall of Ōyama Sekison (current Oyama Afuri Shrine).]] {{ill|Oyama|ja|大山|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} has long been revered as an object of mountain worship. Excavations at its summit have uncovered {{ill|Jomon pottery|ja|縄文土器|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} used in rituals.[http://www.afuri.or.jp/about/]{{ill|About Oyama Afuri Shrine|ja|大山阿夫利神社について|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Official site of Oyama Afuri Shrine) It is also known as “{{ill|Amefuri-yama|ja|雨降山|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}” because clouds and mist frequently gather at the summit, which are believed to bring rain, and it was revered as a rain-making deity. In addition, worship of a giant stone ({{ill|Iwa-za|ja|磐座|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) at the summit and of the twin waterfalls on the mountainside as sacred water sources is also observed.[[宝賀寿男]], “Section 3: The Early Branches of Clans in Kinai and Tōkoku – Part 2: Musashi no Kuni no Kunizukuri and the Provincial Clans of Tōkoku”, in “Studies on Ancient Clans, No. 16: The Rise and Fall of the Izumo Kingdom” (青垣出版, 2020), pp.263–264. According to tradition, Ōyama Afuri Shrine was founded during the reign of {{ill|Sujin-tennō|ja|崇神天皇|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (around the 3rd century BC, though this is considered legendary rather than historical). The {{ill|Engishiki-shiki Shinnamōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, compiled during the Engishiki period, records the shrine as “Afuri Shrine” in its 5th year ({{ill|927|ja|927th year|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) and classifies it as a minor shrine among the thirteen shrines of the {{ill|Engishiki-shiki Naishinsha Jūsansha|ja|延喜式内社十三社|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in {{ill|Sagami Province|ja|相模国|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. == Enshrined Deities == * The primary deity enshrined at the lower shrine is {{ill|Ōyamatsumi|ja|大山祇神|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Ōyamatsumi-no-kami). * The main shrine enshrines {{ill|Ōyamatsumi|ja|大山祇神|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} as its principal deity (prior to the Shinto-Buddhism separation, he was revered as {{ill|Sekison Daigongen|ja|石尊大権現|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}). * The subsidiary shrine (oku-sha) enshrines {{ill|Raijin|ja|大雷神|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Ōi-katsuchi-no-kami; known as {{ill|Ōtengu|ja|大天狗|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} during the syncretic period). * The subsidiary shrine (zen-sha) enshrines {{ill|Takaokami|ja|高龗神|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Takaokami; known as {{ill|Kotenko|ja|小天狗|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} during the syncretic period). This arrangement—enshrining Ōyamatsumi along with the subsidiary deities Raijin and Takaokami—is identical to that of the shrine in {{ill|Ehime Prefecture|ja|愛媛県|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} known as {{ill|Ōyamatsumi Shrine|ja|大山祇神社|1=Ōyamazumi Shrine|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, although these deities were enshrined only after the separation of Shinto and Buddhism in the Meiji period. During the Edo period, when Shinto and Buddhism were syncretized, the main shrine originally enshrined {{ill|Sekison Daigongen|ja|石尊大権現|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, as the sacred stone ({{ill|Reisekki|ja|霊石|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) at the summit served as his manifestation. In the subsidiary shrines, {{ill|Ōtengu|ja|大天狗|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} was enshrined in the oku-sha and {{ill|Kotenko|ja|小天狗|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in the zen-sha. == Cultural Importance == === Oyama Pilgrimage === During the Edo period the Oyama Pilgrimage was a tradition where worshippers formed groups ("{{ill|Kō (lecture)|lt=Kō|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}") to visit the shrine. This pilgrimage, coupled with the "Oyama Kaido" pathway played a role in shaping culture by inspiring rakugo stories and ukiyo e artworks. In 2008 this pilgrimage was designated as a Heritage Site due to its cultural significance. === Osamedachi Tradition === A tradition stemming from a tale about Minamoto no Yoritomo offering a sword to the shrine the Osamedachi custom involves presenting swords that can reach lengths of up to 6 meters. === Kagura Dance === Imported from Kasuga Taisha Shrine during the Meiji era the Kagura dance performed at Oyama Afuri Shrine includes dances by boys (Yamato Mai) and girls (Miko dance) spanning age groups, from elementary school students to adults. The Sendoshi Ryokan originally built to host worshippers has transformed into an inn that provides lodging and dining services. It stands as one of the temple accommodations, in Japan. As for the Oyama Noh tradition it reflects the shrines commitment to peace and harmony tracing its origins back, to the Genroku era. This tradition signifies the bond established among the leaders of Mt. Oyama through their embrace of Noh performances. == Access == === To the Lower Shrine === ; Public Transportation * From the north exit of the {{ill|Odakyu Odawara Line|ja|小田急小田原線|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} at {{ill|Isehara Station|ja|伊勢原駅|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, take Bus Route 10 operated by {{ill|Kanagawa Chūō Kōtsū|ja|神奈川中央交通西|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, alight at the final stop ("Ōyama Cable" bound), which takes approximately 25 minutes. *** Then walk about 15 minutes (approximately 600 meters) from the Ōyama Cable Car Station. ; By Car * Accessible via the {{ill|Shin-Tōmei Expressway|ja|新東名高速道路|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} at the {{ill|Isehara Ōyama Interchange|ja|伊勢原大山インターチェンジ|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, then via {{ill|Kanagawa Prefectural Road 611|ja|神奈川県道611号大山板戸線|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}; municipal parking is available (about a 15-minute walk from the parking lot to the Ōyama Cable Car Station). === To the Main Shrine === * Ascend the mountain from the lower shrine (approximately 90 minutes). ==Gallery== File:Ohyama Afuri jinja 2009.jpg|alt=大山阿夫利神社 2009|Ōyama Afuri Jinja in 2009 File:Ooyama afurijinjya.jpg|alt=大山阿夫利神社|Ooyama Afurijinjya File:Oyama Aburi Shrine 01.jpg|alt=大山阿夫利神社01|Oyama Aburi Shrine 01 File:Oyama Aburi Shrine 02.jpg|alt=大山阿夫利神社02|Oyama Aburi Shrine 02 File:Oyama afuri shrine gesha shishiyama.jpg|alt=大山阿夫利神社 月車獅子山|Oyama Afuri Shrine Gesha Shishiyama File:Oyama-Afuri jinja 201709a.jpg|alt=大山阿夫利神社 2017th year 9月|Oyama-Afuri Jinja, September 2017 File:Oyama-afuri-jinja, shimosha, haiden.jpg|alt=下社拝殿|Lower Shrine Haiden (Worship Hall) File:Oyama-afuri-jinja, shimosha, tozanguchi.jpg|alt=下社登山口|Lower Shrine Entrance (Tozanguchi) File:Ōyama Afuri Jinja - It is a [[Beppyo shrine]], or a shrine that is particularly notable in a certain way with a significant history to it.{{Cite web|title=Learn about Oyama Afuri Shrine - Oyama Afuri Shrine|url=https://www.afuri.or.jp/en/about/|access-date=2024-03-29|language=en-US}}{{Cite web|date=2023-12-28|title=Oyama Afuri Shrine|url=https://www.afuri.or.jp/en/|access-date=2024-03-29|language=en-US}}{{Cite web|date=2013-04-07|title=Afuri Shrine on Mt. Oyama - Kanagawa|url=https://en.japantravel.com/kanagawa/afuri-shrine-on-mt-oyama/4043|access-date=2024-03-29|website=JapanTravel|language=en}} '''{{ill|Oyama Afuri Shrine|ja|大山阿夫利神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}''' (Oyama Afuri Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} located in {{ill|Isehara City|ja|伊勢原市|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Kanagawa Prefecture|ja|神奈川県|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, situated on {{ill|Oyama|ja|大山|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (also known as '''Amefuri-yama'''〈{{ill|Amefuri-yama|ja|雨降山|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}〉). It is recorded in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} from the {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} period (Enchō 5, {{ill|927|ja|927th year|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) as one of the thirteen shrines (small shrines) of the {{ill|Engishiki-shiki Naishinsha Jūsansha|ja|延喜式内社十三社|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in {{ill|Sagami Province|ja|相模国|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Under the [[Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines]], it was classified as a prefectural shrine (Ken-sha) and is currently designated as a [[Beppyo Shrine|Beppyo shrine]] by the {{ill|Jinja Honchō|ja|神社本庁|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. The shrine is composed of two parts: the main shrine (honsha), which includes the inner shrine (okusha) and the front shrine (zensha) located at the summit of Oyama, and the lower shrine (gesha) located on the mid-slope.[http://www.afuri.or.jp/about/map/]{{ill|About Oyama Afuri Shrine|ja|大山阿夫利神社について：境内のご案内|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Official site of Oyama Afuri Shrine). The lower shrine is accessible via the {{ill|Oyama Cable Car|ja|大山ケーブルカー|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} operated by {{ill|Oyama Kankō Dentetsu|ja|大山観光電鉄|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. == History == [[File:Pilgrims at the Roben waterfall, Oyama.jpg|thumb|left|245px|“Ōyama Sekison Raben-taki no Zu” by {{ill|Utagawa Kuniyoshi|ja|歌川国芳|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Art name: Ichiyūsai), painted circa 1819–1820 (Bunsei 2–3). Men praying at the waterfall of Ōyama Sekison (current Oyama Afuri Shrine).]] {{ill|Oyama|ja|大山|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} has long been revered as an object of mountain worship. Excavations at its summit have uncovered {{ill|Jomon pottery|ja|縄文土器|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} used in rituals.[http://www.afuri.or.jp/about/]{{ill|About Oyama Afuri Shrine|ja|大山阿夫利神社について|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Official site of Oyama Afuri Shrine) It is also known as “{{ill|Amefuri-yama|ja|雨降山|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}” because clouds and mist frequently gather at the summit, which are believed to bring rain, and it was revered as a rain-making deity. In addition, worship of a giant stone ({{ill|Iwa-za|ja|磐座|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) at the summit and of the twin waterfalls on the mountainside as sacred water sources is also observed.{{ill|Toshio Hōga|ja|宝賀寿男}}, “Section 3: The Early Branches of Clans in Kinai and Tōkoku – Part 2: Musashi no Kuni no Kunizukuri and the Provincial Clans of Tōkoku”, in “Studies on Ancient Clans, No. 16: The Rise and Fall of the Izumo Kingdom” (青垣出版, 2020), pp.263–264. According to tradition, Ōyama Afuri Shrine was founded during the reign of {{ill|Sujin-tennō|ja|崇神天皇|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (around the 3rd century BC, though this is considered legendary rather than historical). The {{ill|Engishiki-shiki Shinnamōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, compiled during the Engishiki period, records the shrine as “Afuri Shrine” in its 5th year ({{ill|927|ja|927th year|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) and classifies it as a minor shrine among the thirteen shrines of the {{ill|Engishiki-shiki Naishinsha Jūsansha|ja|延喜式内社十三社|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in {{ill|Sagami Province|ja|相模国|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. == Enshrined Deities == * The primary deity enshrined at the lower shrine is {{ill|Ōyamatsumi|ja|大山祇神|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Ōyamatsumi-no-kami). * The main shrine enshrines {{ill|Ōyamatsumi|ja|大山祇神|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} as its principal deity (prior to the Shinto-Buddhism separation, he was revered as {{ill|Sekison Daigongen|ja|石尊大権現|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}). * The subsidiary shrine (oku-sha) enshrines {{ill|Raijin|ja|大雷神|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Ōi-katsuchi-no-kami; known as {{ill|Ōtengu|ja|大天狗|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} during the syncretic period). * The subsidiary shrine (zen-sha) enshrines {{ill|Takaokami|ja|高龗神|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Takaokami; known as {{ill|Kotenko|ja|小天狗|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} during the syncretic period). This arrangement—enshrining Ōyamatsumi along with the subsidiary deities Raijin and Takaokami—is identical to that of the shrine in {{ill|Ehime Prefecture|ja|愛媛県|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} known as {{ill|Ōyamatsumi Shrine|ja|大山祇神社|1=Ōyamazumi Shrine|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, although these deities were enshrined only after the separation of Shinto and Buddhism in the Meiji period. During the Edo period, when Shinto and Buddhism were syncretized, the main shrine originally enshrined {{ill|Sekison Daigongen|ja|石尊大権現|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, as the sacred stone ({{ill|Reisekki|ja|霊石|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) at the summit served as his manifestation. In the subsidiary shrines, {{ill|Ōtengu|ja|大天狗|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} was enshrined in the oku-sha and {{ill|Kotenko|ja|小天狗|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in the zen-sha. == Cultural Importance == === Oyama Pilgrimage === During the Edo period the Oyama Pilgrimage was a tradition where worshippers formed groups ("{{ill|Kō (lecture)|lt=Kō|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}") to visit the shrine. This pilgrimage, coupled with the "Oyama Kaido" pathway played a role in shaping culture by inspiring rakugo stories and ukiyo e artworks. In 2008 this pilgrimage was designated as a Heritage Site due to its cultural significance. === Osamedachi Tradition === A tradition stemming from a tale about Minamoto no Yoritomo offering a sword to the shrine the Osamedachi custom involves presenting swords that can reach lengths of up to 6 meters. === Kagura Dance === Imported from Kasuga Taisha Shrine during the Meiji era the Kagura dance performed at Oyama Afuri Shrine includes dances by boys (Yamato Mai) and girls (Miko dance) spanning age groups, from elementary school students to adults. The Sendoshi Ryokan originally built to host worshippers has transformed into an inn that provides lodging and dining services. It stands as one of the temple accommodations, in Japan. As for the Oyama Noh tradition it reflects the shrines commitment to peace and harmony tracing its origins back, to the Genroku era. This tradition signifies the bond established among the leaders of Mt. Oyama through their embrace of Noh performances. == Access == === To the Lower Shrine === ; Public Transportation * From the north exit of the {{ill|Odakyu Odawara Line|ja|小田急小田原線|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} at {{ill|Isehara Station|ja|伊勢原駅|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, take Bus Route 10 operated by {{ill|Kanagawa Chūō Kōtsū|ja|神奈川中央交通西|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, alight at the final stop ("Ōyama Cable" bound), which takes approximately 25 minutes. *** Then walk about 15 minutes (approximately 600 meters) from the Ōyama Cable Car Station. ; By Car * Accessible via the {{ill|Shin-Tōmei Expressway|ja|新東名高速道路|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} at the {{ill|Isehara Ōyama Interchange|ja|伊勢原大山インターチェンジ|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, then via {{ill|Kanagawa Prefectural Road 611|ja|神奈川県道611号大山板戸線|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}; municipal parking is available (about a 15-minute walk from the parking lot to the Ōyama Cable Car Station). === To the Main Shrine === * Ascend the mountain from the lower shrine (approximately 90 minutes). ==Gallery== File:Ohyama Afuri jinja 2009.jpg|alt=大山阿夫利神社 2009|Ōyama Afuri Jinja in 2009 File:Ooyama afurijinjya.jpg|alt=大山阿夫利神社|Ooyama Afurijinjya File:Oyama Aburi Shrine 01.jpg|alt=大山阿夫利神社01|Oyama Aburi Shrine 01 File:Oyama Aburi Shrine 02.jpg|alt=大山阿夫利神社02|Oyama Aburi Shrine 02 File:Oyama afuri shrine gesha shishiyama.jpg|alt=大山阿夫利神社 月車獅子山|Oyama Afuri Shrine Gesha Shishiyama File:Oyama-Afuri jinja 201709a.jpg|alt=大山阿夫利神社 2017th year 9月|Oyama-Afuri Jinja, September 2017 File:Oyama-afuri-jinja, shimosha, haiden.jpg|alt=下社拝殿|Lower Shrine Haiden (Worship Hall) File:Oyama-afuri-jinja, shimosha, tozanguchi.jpg|alt=下社登山口|Lower Shrine Entrance (Tozanguchi) File:Ōyama Afuri Jinja - It is a [[Beppyo shrine]], or a shrine that is particularly notable in a certain way with a significant history to it.{{Cite web|title=Learn about Oyama Afuri Shrine - Oyama Afuri Shrine|url=https://www.afuri.or.jp/en/about/|access-date=2024-03-29|language=en-US}}{{Cite web|date=2023-12-28|title=Oyama Afuri Shrine|url=https://www.afuri.or.jp/en/|access-date=2024-03-29|language=en-US}}{{Cite web|date=2013-04-07|title=Afuri Shrine on Mt. Oyama - Kanagawa|url=https://en.japantravel.com/kanagawa/afuri-shrine-on-mt-oyama/4043|access-date=2024-03-29|website=JapanTravel|language=en}} '''{{ill|Oyama Afuri Shrine|ja|大山阿夫利神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}''' (Oyama Afuri Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} located in {{ill|Isehara City|ja|伊勢原市|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Kanagawa Prefecture|ja|神奈川県|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, situated on {{ill|Oyama|ja|大山|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (also known as '''Amefuri-yama'''〈{{ill|Amefuri-yama|ja|雨降山|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}〉). It is recorded in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} from the {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} period (Enchō 5, {{ill|927|ja|927th year|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) as one of the thirteen shrines (small shrines) of the {{ill|Engishiki-shiki Naishinsha Jūsansha|ja|延喜式内社十三社|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in {{ill|Sagami Province|ja|相模国|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Under the [[Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines]], it was classified as a prefectural shrine (Ken-sha) and is currently designated as a [[Beppyo Shrine|Beppyo shrine]] by the {{ill|Jinja Honchō|ja|神社本庁|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. The shrine is composed of two parts: the main shrine (honsha), which includes the inner shrine (okusha) and the front shrine (zensha) located at the summit of Oyama, and the lower shrine (gesha) located on the mid-slope.[http://www.afuri.or.jp/about/map/]{{ill|About Oyama Afuri Shrine|ja|大山阿夫利神社について：境内のご案内|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Official site of Oyama Afuri Shrine). The lower shrine is accessible via the {{ill|Oyama Cable Car|ja|大山ケーブルカー|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} operated by {{ill|Oyama Kankō Dentetsu|ja|大山観光電鉄|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. == History == [[File:Pilgrims at the Roben waterfall, Oyama.jpg|thumb|left|245px|“Ōyama Sekison Raben-taki no Zu” by {{ill|Utagawa Kuniyoshi|ja|歌川国芳|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Art name: Ichiyūsai), painted circa 1819–1820 (Bunsei 2–3). Men praying at the waterfall of Ōyama Sekison (current Oyama Afuri Shrine).]] {{ill|Oyama|ja|大山|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} has long been revered as an object of mountain worship. Excavations at its summit have uncovered {{ill|Jomon pottery|ja|縄文土器|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} used in rituals.[http://www.afuri.or.jp/about/]{{ill|About Oyama Afuri Shrine|ja|大山阿夫利神社について|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Official site of Oyama Afuri Shrine) It is also known as “{{ill|Amefuri-yama|ja|雨降山|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}” because clouds and mist frequently gather at the summit, which are believed to bring rain, and it was revered as a rain-making deity. In addition, worship of a giant stone ({{ill|Iwa-za|ja|磐座|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) at the summit and of the twin waterfalls on the mountainside as sacred water sources is also observed.{{ill|Toshio Hōga|ja|宝賀寿男}}, “Section 3: The Early Branches of Clans in Kinai and Tōkoku – Part 2: Musashi no Kuni no Kunizukuri and the Provincial Clans of Tōkoku”, in “Studies on Ancient Clans, No. 16: The Rise and Fall of the Izumo Kingdom” (青垣出版, 2020), pp.263–264. According to tradition, Ōyama Afuri Shrine was founded during the reign of {{ill|Sujin-tennō|ja|崇神天皇|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (around the 3rd century BC, though this is considered legendary rather than historical). The {{ill|Engishiki-shiki Shinnamōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, compiled during the Engishiki period, records the shrine as “Afuri Shrine” in its 5th year ({{ill|927|ja|927th year|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) and classifies it as a minor shrine among the thirteen shrines of the {{ill|Engishiki-shiki Naishinsha Jūsansha|ja|延喜式内社十三社|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in {{ill|Sagami Province|ja|相模国|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. == Enshrined Deities == * The primary deity enshrined at the lower shrine is {{ill|Ōyamatsumi|ja|大山祇神|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Ōyamatsumi-no-kami). * The main shrine enshrines {{ill|Ōyamatsumi|ja|大山祇神|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} as its principal deity (prior to the Shinto-Buddhism separation, he was revered as {{ill|Sekison Daigongen|ja|石尊大権現|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}). * The subsidiary shrine (oku-sha) enshrines {{ill|Raijin|ja|大雷神|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Ōi-katsuchi-no-kami; known as {{ill|Ōtengu|ja|大天狗|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} during the syncretic period). * The subsidiary shrine (zen-sha) enshrines {{ill|Takaokami|ja|高龗神|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Takaokami; known as {{ill|Kotenko|ja|小天狗|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} during the syncretic period). This arrangement—enshrining Ōyamatsumi along with the subsidiary deities Raijin and Takaokami—is identical to that of the shrine in {{ill|Ehime Prefecture|ja|愛媛県|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} known as {{ill|Ōyamatsumi Shrine|ja|大山祇神社|1=Ōyamazumi Shrine|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, although these deities were enshrined only after the separation of Shinto and Buddhism in the Meiji period. During the Edo period, when Shinto and Buddhism were syncretized, the main shrine originally enshrined {{ill|Sekison Daigongen|ja|石尊大権現|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, as the sacred stone ({{ill|Reisekki|ja|霊石|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) at the summit served as his manifestation. In the subsidiary shrines, {{ill|Ōtengu|ja|大天狗|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} was enshrined in the oku-sha and {{ill|Kotenko|ja|小天狗|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in the zen-sha. == Cultural Importance == === Oyama Pilgrimage === During the Edo period the Oyama Pilgrimage was a tradition where worshippers formed groups ("{{ill|Kō (lecture)|lt=Kō|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}") to visit the shrine. This pilgrimage, coupled with the "Oyama Kaido" pathway played a role in shaping culture by inspiring rakugo stories and ukiyo e artworks. In 2008 this pilgrimage was designated as a Heritage Site due to its cultural significance. === Osamedachi Tradition === A tradition stemming from a tale about Minamoto no Yoritomo offering a sword to the shrine the Osamedachi custom involves presenting swords that can reach lengths of up to 6 meters. === Kagura Dance === Imported from Kasuga Taisha Shrine during the Meiji era the Kagura dance performed at Oyama Afuri Shrine includes dances by boys (Yamato Mai) and girls (Miko dance) spanning age groups, from elementary school students to adults. The Sendoshi Ryokan originally built to host worshippers has transformed into an inn that provides lodging and dining services. It stands as one of the temple accommodations, in Japan. As for the Oyama Noh tradition it reflects the shrines commitment to peace and harmony tracing its origins back, to the Genroku era. This tradition signifies the bond established among the leaders of Mt. Oyama through their embrace of Noh performances. == Access == === To the Lower Shrine === ; Public Transportation * From the north exit of the {{ill|Odakyu Odawara Line|ja|小田急小田原線|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} at {{ill|Isehara Station|ja|伊勢原駅|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, take Bus Route 10 operated by {{ill|Kanagawa Chūō Kōtsū|ja|神奈川中央交通西|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, alight at the final stop ("Ōyama Cable" bound), which takes approximately 25 minutes. *** Then walk about 15 minutes (approximately 600 meters) from the Ōyama Cable Car Station. ; By Car * Accessible via the {{ill|Shin-Tōmei Expressway|ja|新東名高速道路|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} at the {{ill|Isehara Ōyama Interchange|ja|伊勢原大山インターチェンジ|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, then via {{ill|Kanagawa Prefectural Road 611|ja|神奈川県道611号大山板戸線|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}; municipal parking is available (about a 15-minute walk from the parking lot to the Ōyama Cable Car Station). === To the Main Shrine === * Ascend the mountain from the lower shrine (approximately 90 minutes). ==Gallery== File:Ohyama Afuri jinja 2009.jpg|alt=大山阿夫利神社 2009|Ōyama Afuri Jinja in 2009 File:Ooyama afurijinjya.jpg|alt=大山阿夫利神社|Ooyama Afurijinjya File:Oyama Aburi Shrine 01.jpg|alt=大山阿夫利神社01|Oyama Aburi Shrine 01 File:Oyama Aburi Shrine 02.jpg|alt=大山阿夫利神社02|Oyama Aburi Shrine 02 File:Oyama afuri shrine gesha shishiyama.jpg|alt=大山阿夫利神社 月車獅子山|Oyama Afuri Shrine Gesha Shishiyama File:Oyama-Afuri jinja 201709a.jpg|alt=大山阿夫利神社 2017th year 9月|Oyama-Afuri Jinja, September 2017 File:Oyama-afuri-jinja, shimosha, haiden.jpg|alt=下社拝殿|Lower Shrine Haiden (Worship Hall) File:Oyama-afuri-jinja, shimosha, tozanguchi.jpg|alt=下社登山口|Lower Shrine Entrance (Tozanguchi) File:Ōyama Afuri Jinja -
