It is a [[Beppyo Shrine]], or a shrine that is particularly notable in a certain way with a significant history to it.{{Cite web|title=Learn about Oyama Afuri Shrine - Oyama Afuri Shrine|url=https://www.afuri.or.jp/en/about/|access-date=2024-03-29|language=en-US}}{{Cite web|date=2023-12-28|title=Oyama Afuri Shrine|url=https://www.afuri.or.jp/en/|access-date=2024-03-29|language=en-US}}{{Cite web|date=2013-04-07|title=Afuri Shrine on Mt. Oyama - Kanagawa|url=https://en.japantravel.com/kanagawa/afuri-shrine-on-mt-oyama/4043|access-date=2024-03-29|website=JapanTravel|language=en}} '''{{ill|Oyama Afuri Shrine|ja|大山阿夫利神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Oyama Afuri Shrine|1=Ōyama Afuri Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11434713}}''' (Oyama Afuri Jinja) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in [[:en:Isehara, Kanagawa|Isehara City]], [[:en:Kanagawa Prefecture|Kanagawa Prefecture]], situated on [[:en:大山|Oyama]] (also known as '''Amefuri-yama'''〈{{ill|Amefuri-yama|ja|雨降山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amefuri-yama|1=Amefuri-yama|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11659780}}〉). It is recorded in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=}} from the [[:en:Engishiki|Engishiki]] period (Enchō 5, [[:en:927|927]]) as one of the thirteen shrines (small shrines) of the {{ill|Engishiki-shiki Naishinsha Jūsansha|ja|延喜式内社十三社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki-shiki Naishinsha Jūsansha|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} in [[:en:Sagami Province|Sagami Province]]. Under the [[:en:Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines]], it was classified as a prefectural shrine (Ken-sha) and is currently designated as a [[Beppyo Shrine|Beppyo shrine]] by the [[:en:Association of Shinto Shrines|Association of Shinto Shrines]]. The shrine is composed of two parts: the main shrine (honsha), which includes the inner shrine (okusha) and the front shrine (zensha) located at the summit of Oyama, and the lower shrine (gesha) located on the mid-slope.[http://www.afuri.or.jp/about/map/]{{ill|About Oyama Afuri Shrine|ja|大山阿夫利神社について：境内のご案内|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/About Oyama Afuri Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (Official site of Oyama Afuri Shrine). The lower shrine is accessible via the {{ill|Oyama Cable Car|ja|大山ケーブルカー|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Oyama Cable Car|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大山観光電鉄大山鋼索線|1=Ōyama Cable Car|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q864604}} operated by {{ill|Oyama Kankō Dentetsu|ja|大山観光電鉄|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Oyama Kankō Dentetsu|1=Ōyama Kankō Dentetsu|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11434695}}. == History == [[File:Pilgrims at the Roben waterfall, Oyama.jpg|thumb|left|245px|“Ōyama Sekison Raben-taki no Zu” by [[:en:Utagawa Kuniyoshi|Utagawa Kuniyoshi]] (Art name: Ichiyūsai), painted circa 1819–1820 (Bunsei 2–3). Men praying at the waterfall of Ōyama Sekison (current Oyama Afuri Shrine).]] [[:en:大山|Oyama]] has long been revered as an object of mountain worship. Excavations at its summit have uncovered [[:en:Jōmon pottery|Jomon pottery]] used in rituals.[http://www.afuri.or.jp/about/]{{ill|About Oyama Afuri Shrine|ja|大山阿夫利神社について|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/About Oyama Afuri Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (Official site of Oyama Afuri Shrine) It is also known as “{{ill|Amefuri-yama|ja|雨降山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amefuri-yama|1=Amefuri-yama|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11659780}}” because clouds and mist frequently gather at the summit, which are believed to bring rain, and it was revered as a rain-making deity. In addition, worship of a giant stone ([[:en:Iwakura rock|Iwa-za]]) at the summit and of the twin waterfalls on the mountainside as sacred water sources is also observed.{{ill|Toshio Hōga|ja|宝賀寿男|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toshio Hōga|qq=}}, “Section 3: The Early Branches of Clans in Kinai and Tōkoku – Part 2: Musashi no Kuni no Kunizukuri and the Provincial Clans of Tōkoku”, in “Studies on Ancient Clans, No. 16: The Rise and Fall of the Izumo Kingdom” (青垣出版, 2020), pp.263–264. According to tradition, Ōyama Afuri Shrine was founded during the reign of [[:en:Emperor Sujin|Sujin-tennō]] (around the 3rd century BC, though this is considered legendary rather than historical). The {{ill|Engishiki-shiki Shinnamōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki-shiki Shinnamōchō|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=}}, compiled during the Engishiki period, records the shrine as “Afuri Shrine” in its 5th year ([[:en:927|927]]) and classifies it as a minor shrine among the thirteen shrines of the {{ill|Engishiki-shiki Naishinsha Jūsansha|ja|延喜式内社十三社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki-shiki Naishinsha Jūsansha|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} in [[:en:Sagami Province|Sagami Province]]. == Enshrined Deities == * The primary deity enshrined at the lower shrine is {{ill|Ōyamatsumi|ja|大山祇神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōyamatsumi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to オオヤマツミ}} (Ōyamatsumi-no-kami). * The main shrine enshrines {{ill|Ōyamatsumi|ja|大山祇神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōyamatsumi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to オオヤマツミ}} as its principal deity (prior to the Shinto-Buddhism separation, he was revered as {{ill|Sekison Daigongen|ja|石尊大権現|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sekison Daigongen|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 石尊権現|1=Sekison Gongen|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q55528104}}). * The subsidiary shrine (oku-sha) enshrines {{ill|Raijin|ja|大雷神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Raijin|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (Ōi-katsuchi-no-kami; known as {{ill|Ōtengu|ja|大天狗|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōtengu|1=daitengu|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q10934709}} during the syncretic period). * The subsidiary shrine (zen-sha) enshrines {{ill|Takaokami|ja|高龗神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takaokami|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 淤加美神|1=Kuraokami|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q644201}} (Takaokami; known as {{ill|Kotenko|ja|小天狗|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kotenko|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 烏天狗|1=karasu tengu|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q863869}} during the syncretic period). This arrangement—enshrining Ōyamatsumi along with the subsidiary deities Raijin and Takaokami—is identical to that of the shrine in [[:en:Ehime Prefecture|Ehime Prefecture]] known as [[:en:Ōyamazumi Shrine|Ōyamazumi Shrine]], although these deities were enshrined only after the separation of Shinto and Buddhism in the Meiji period. During the Edo period, when Shinto and Buddhism were syncretized, the main shrine originally enshrined {{ill|Sekison Daigongen|ja|石尊大権現|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sekison Daigongen|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 石尊権現|1=Sekison Gongen|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q55528104}}, as the sacred stone ({{ill|Reisekki|ja|霊石|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Reisekki|1=Reisekki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q23998630}}) at the summit served as his manifestation. In the subsidiary shrines, {{ill|Ōtengu|ja|大天狗|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōtengu|1=daitengu|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q10934709}} was enshrined in the oku-sha and {{ill|Kotenko|ja|小天狗|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kotenko|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 烏天狗|1=karasu tengu|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q863869}} in the zen-sha. == Cultural Importance == === Oyama Pilgrimage === During the Edo period the Oyama Pilgrimage was a tradition where worshippers formed groups ("{{ill|Kō (lecture)|lt=Kō|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kō (lecture)|qq=}}") to visit the shrine. This pilgrimage, coupled with the "Oyama Kaido" pathway played a role in shaping culture by inspiring rakugo stories and ukiyo e artworks. In 2008 this pilgrimage was designated as a Heritage Site due to its cultural significance. === Osamedachi Tradition === A tradition stemming from a tale about Minamoto no Yoritomo offering a sword to the shrine the Osamedachi custom involves presenting swords that can reach lengths of up to 6 meters. === Kagura Dance === Imported from Kasuga Taisha Shrine during the Meiji era the Kagura dance performed at Oyama Afuri Shrine includes dances by boys (Yamato Mai) and girls (Miko dance) spanning age groups, from elementary school students to adults. The Sendoshi Ryokan originally built to host worshippers has transformed into an inn that provides lodging and dining services. It stands as one of the temple accommodations, in Japan. As for the Oyama Noh tradition it reflects the shrines commitment to peace and harmony tracing its origins back, to the Genroku era. This tradition signifies the bond established among the leaders of Mt. Oyama through their embrace of Noh performances. == Access == === To the Lower Shrine === ; Public Transportation * From the north exit of the [[:en:Odakyū Odawara Line|Odakyu Odawara Line]] at 神奈川中央交通|1=Kanagawa Chuo Kotsu|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q10854960}}, alight at the final stop ("Ōyama Cable" bound), which takes approximately 25 minutes. *** Then walk about 15 Interchange|ja|伊勢原大山インターチェンジ|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Isehara Ōyama Interchange|1=Isehara oyama interchange|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11378953}}, then via {{ill|Kanagawa It is a [[Beppyo Shrine]], or a shrine that is particularly notable in a certain way with a significant history to it.{{Cite web|title=Learn about Oyama Afuri Shrine - Oyama Afuri Shrine|url=https://www.afuri.or.jp/en/about/|access-date=2024-03-29|language=en-US}}{{Cite web|date=2023-12-28|title=Oyama Afuri Shrine|url=https://www.afuri.or.jp/en/|access-date=2024-03-29|language=en-US}}{{Cite web|date=2013-04-07|title=Afuri Shrine on Mt. Oyama - Kanagawa|url=https://en.japantravel.com/kanagawa/afuri-shrine-on-mt-oyama/4043|access-date=2024-03-29|website=JapanTravel|language=en}} '''{{ill|Oyama Afuri Shrine|ja|大山阿夫利神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Oyama Afuri Shrine|1=Ōyama Afuri Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11434713}}''' (Oyama Afuri Jinja) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in [[:en:Isehara, Kanagawa|Isehara City]], [[:en:Kanagawa Prefecture|Kanagawa Prefecture]], situated on [[:en:大山|Oyama]] (also known as '''Amefuri-yama'''〈{{ill|Amefuri-yama|ja|雨降山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amefuri-yama|1=Amefuri-yama|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11659780}}〉). It is recorded in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=}} from the [[:en:Engishiki|Engishiki]] period (Enchō 5, [[:en:927|927]]) as one of the thirteen shrines (small shrines) of the {{ill|Engishiki-shiki Naishinsha Jūsansha|ja|延喜式内社十三社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki-shiki Naishinsha Jūsansha|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} in [[:en:Sagami Province|Sagami Province]]. Under the [[:en:Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines]], it was classified as a prefectural shrine (Ken-sha) and is currently designated as a [[Beppyo Shrine|Beppyo shrine]] by the [[:en:Association of Shinto Shrines|Association of Shinto Shrines]]. The shrine is composed of two parts: the main shrine (honsha), which includes the inner shrine (okusha) and the front shrine (zensha) located at the summit of Oyama, and the lower shrine (gesha) located on the mid-slope.[http://www.afuri.or.jp/about/map/]{{ill|About Oyama Afuri Shrine|ja|大山阿夫利神社について：境内のご案内|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/About Oyama Afuri Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (Official site of Oyama Afuri Shrine). The lower shrine is accessible via the {{ill|Oyama Cable Car|ja|大山ケーブルカー|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Oyama Cable Car|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大山観光電鉄大山鋼索線|1=Ōyama Cable Car|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q864604}} operated by {{ill|Oyama Kankō Dentetsu|ja|大山観光電鉄|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Oyama Kankō Dentetsu|1=Ōyama Kankō Dentetsu|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11434695}}. == History == [[File:Pilgrims at the Roben waterfall, Oyama.jpg|thumb|left|245px|“Ōyama Sekison Raben-taki no Zu” by [[:en:Utagawa Kuniyoshi|Utagawa Kuniyoshi]] (Art name: Ichiyūsai), painted circa 1819–1820 (Bunsei 2–3). Men praying at the waterfall of Ōyama Sekison (current Oyama Afuri Shrine).]] [[:en:大山|Oyama]] has long been revered as an object of mountain worship. Excavations at its summit have uncovered [[:en:Jōmon pottery|Jomon pottery]] used in rituals.[http://www.afuri.or.jp/about/]{{ill|About Oyama Afuri Shrine|ja|大山阿夫利神社について|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/About Oyama Afuri Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (Official site of Oyama Afuri Shrine) It is also known as “{{ill|Amefuri-yama|ja|雨降山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amefuri-yama|1=Amefuri-yama|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11659780}}” because clouds and mist frequently gather at the summit, which are believed to bring rain, and it was revered as a rain-making deity. In addition, worship of a giant stone ([[:en:Iwakura rock|Iwa-za]]) at the summit and of the twin waterfalls on the mountainside as sacred water sources is also observed.{{ill|Toshio Hōga|ja|宝賀寿男|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toshio Hōga|qq=}}, “Section 3: The Early Branches of Clans in Kinai and Tōkoku – Part 2: Musashi no Kuni no Kunizukuri and the Provincial Clans of Tōkoku”, in “Studies on Ancient Clans, No. 16: The Rise and Fall of the Izumo Kingdom” (青垣出版, 2020), pp.263–264. According to tradition, Ōyama Afuri Shrine was founded during the reign of [[:en:Emperor Sujin|Sujin-tennō]] (around the 3rd century BC, though this is considered legendary rather than historical). The {{ill|Engishiki-shiki Shinnamōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki-shiki Shinnamōchō|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=}}, compiled during the Engishiki period, records the shrine as “Afuri Shrine” in its 5th year ([[:en:927|927]]) and classifies it as a minor shrine among the thirteen shrines of the {{ill|Engishiki-shiki Naishinsha Jūsansha|ja|延喜式内社十三社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki-shiki Naishinsha Jūsansha|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} in [[:en:Sagami Province|Sagami Province]]. == Enshrined Deities == * The primary deity enshrined at the lower shrine is {{ill|Ōyamatsumi|ja|大山祇神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōyamatsumi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to オオヤマツミ}} (Ōyamatsumi-no-kami). * The main shrine enshrines {{ill|Ōyamatsumi|ja|大山祇神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōyamatsumi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to オオヤマツミ}} as its principal deity (prior to the Shinto-Buddhism separation, he was revered as {{ill|Sekison Daigongen|ja|石尊大権現|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sekison Daigongen|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 石尊権現|1=Sekison Gongen|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q55528104}}). * The subsidiary shrine (oku-sha) enshrines {{ill|Raijin|ja|大雷神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Raijin|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (Ōi-katsuchi-no-kami; known as {{ill|Ōtengu|ja|大天狗|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōtengu|1=daitengu|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q10934709}} during the syncretic period). * The subsidiary shrine (zen-sha) enshrines {{ill|Takaokami|ja|高龗神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takaokami|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 淤加美神|1=Kuraokami|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q644201}} (Takaokami; known as {{ill|Kotenko|ja|小天狗|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kotenko|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 烏天狗|1=karasu tengu|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q863869}} during the syncretic period). This arrangement—enshrining Ōyamatsumi along with the subsidiary deities Raijin and Takaokami—is identical to that of the shrine in [[:en:Ehime Prefecture|Ehime Prefecture]] known as [[:en:Ōyamazumi Shrine|Ōyamazumi Shrine]], although these deities were enshrined only after the separation of Shinto and Buddhism in the Meiji period. During the Edo period, when Shinto and Buddhism were syncretized, the main shrine originally enshrined {{ill|Sekison Daigongen|ja|石尊大権現|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sekison Daigongen|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 石尊権現|1=Sekison Gongen|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q55528104}}, as the sacred stone ({{ill|Reisekki|ja|霊石|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Reisekki|1=Reisekki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q23998630}}) at the summit served as his manifestation. In the subsidiary shrines, {{ill|Ōtengu|ja|大天狗|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōtengu|1=daitengu|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q10934709}} was enshrined in the oku-sha and {{ill|Kotenko|ja|小天狗|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kotenko|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 烏天狗|1=karasu tengu|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q863869}} in the zen-sha. == Cultural Importance == === Oyama Pilgrimage === During the Edo period the Oyama Pilgrimage was a tradition where worshippers formed groups ("{{ill|Kō (lecture)|lt=Kō|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kō (lecture)|qq=}}") to visit the shrine. This pilgrimage, coupled with the "Oyama Kaido" pathway played a role in shaping culture by inspiring rakugo stories and ukiyo e artworks. In 2008 this pilgrimage was designated as a Heritage Site due to its cultural significance. === Osamedachi Tradition === A tradition stemming from a tale about Minamoto no Yoritomo offering a sword to the shrine the Osamedachi custom involves presenting swords that can reach lengths of up to 6 meters. === Kagura Dance === Imported from Kasuga Taisha Shrine during the Meiji era the Kagura dance performed at Oyama Afuri Shrine includes dances by boys (Yamato Mai) and girls (Miko dance) spanning age groups, from elementary school students to adults. The Sendoshi Ryokan originally built to host worshippers has transformed into an inn that provides lodging and dining services. It stands as one of the temple accommodations, in Japan. As for the Oyama Noh tradition it reflects the shrines commitment to peace and harmony tracing its origins back, to the Genroku era. This tradition signifies the bond established among the leaders of Mt. Oyama through their embrace of Noh performances. == Access == === To the Lower Shrine === ; Public Transportation * From the north exit of the [[:en:Odakyū Odawara Line|Odakyu Odawara Line]] at It is a [[Beppyo Shrine]], or a shrine that is particularly notable in a certain way with a significant history to it.{{Cite web|title=Learn about Oyama Afuri Shrine - Oyama Afuri Shrine|url=https://www.afuri.or.jp/en/about/|access-date=2024-03-29|language=en-US}}{{Cite web|date=2023-12-28|title=Oyama Afuri Shrine|url=https://www.afuri.or.jp/en/|access-date=2024-03-29|language=en-US}}{{Cite web|date=2013-04-07|title=Afuri Shrine on Mt. Oyama - Kanagawa|url=https://en.japantravel.com/kanagawa/afuri-shrine-on-mt-oyama/4043|access-date=2024-03-29|website=JapanTravel|language=en}} '''{{ill|Oyama Afuri Shrine|ja|大山阿夫利神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Oyama Afuri Shrine|1=Ōyama Afuri Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11434713}}''' (Oyama Afuri Jinja) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in [[:en:Isehara, Kanagawa|Isehara City]], [[:en:Kanagawa Prefecture|Kanagawa Prefecture]], situated on [[:en:大山|Oyama]] (also known as '''Amefuri-yama'''〈{{ill|Amefuri-yama|ja|雨降山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amefuri-yama|1=Amefuri-yama|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11659780}}〉). It is recorded in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=}} from the [[:en:Engishiki|Engishiki]] period (Enchō 5, [[:en:927|927]]) as one of the thirteen shrines (small shrines) of the {{ill|Engishiki-shiki Naishinsha Jūsansha|ja|延喜式内社十三社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki-shiki Naishinsha Jūsansha|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} in [[:en:Sagami Province|Sagami Province]]. Under the [[:en:Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines]], it was classified as a prefectural shrine (Ken-sha) and is currently designated as a [[Beppyo Shrine|Beppyo shrine]] by the [[:en:Association of Shinto Shrines|Association of Shinto Shrines]]. The shrine is composed of two parts: the main shrine (honsha), which includes the inner shrine (okusha) and the front shrine (zensha) located at the summit of Oyama, and the lower shrine (gesha) located on the mid-slope.[http://www.afuri.or.jp/about/map/]{{ill|About Oyama Afuri Shrine|ja|大山阿夫利神社について：境内のご案内|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/About Oyama Afuri Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (Official site of Oyama Afuri Shrine). The lower shrine is accessible via the {{ill|Oyama Cable Car|ja|大山ケーブルカー|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Oyama Cable Car|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大山観光電鉄大山鋼索線|1=Ōyama Cable Car|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q864604}} operated by {{ill|Oyama Kankō Dentetsu|ja|大山観光電鉄|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Oyama Kankō Dentetsu|1=Ōyama Kankō Dentetsu|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11434695}}. == History == [[File:Pilgrims at the Roben waterfall, Oyama.jpg|thumb|left|245px|“Ōyama Sekison Raben-taki no Zu” by [[:en:Utagawa Kuniyoshi|Utagawa Kuniyoshi]] (Art name: Ichiyūsai), painted circa 1819–1820 (Bunsei 2–3). Men praying at the waterfall of Ōyama Sekison (current Oyama Afuri Shrine).]] [[:en:大山|Oyama]] has long been revered as an object of mountain worship. Excavations at its summit have uncovered [[:en:Jōmon pottery|Jomon pottery]] used in rituals.[http://www.afuri.or.jp/about/]{{ill|About Oyama Afuri Shrine|ja|大山阿夫利神社について|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/About Oyama Afuri Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (Official site of Oyama Afuri Shrine) It is also known as “{{ill|Amefuri-yama|ja|雨降山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amefuri-yama|1=Amefuri-yama|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11659780}}” because clouds and mist frequently gather at the summit, which are believed to bring rain, and it was revered as a rain-making deity. In addition, worship of a giant stone ([[:en:Iwakura rock|Iwa-za]]) at the summit and of the twin waterfalls on the mountainside as sacred water sources is also observed.{{ill|Toshio Hōga|ja|宝賀寿男|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toshio Hōga|qq=}}, “Section 3: The Early Branches of Clans in Kinai and Tōkoku – Part 2: Musashi no Kuni no Kunizukuri and the Provincial Clans of Tōkoku”, in “Studies on Ancient Clans, No. 16: The Rise and Fall of the Izumo Kingdom” (青垣出版, 2020), pp.263–264. According to tradition, Ōyama Afuri Shrine was founded during the reign of [[:en:Emperor Sujin|Sujin-tennō]] (around the 3rd century BC, though this is considered legendary rather than historical). The {{ill|Engishiki-shiki Shinnamōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki-shiki Shinnamōchō|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=}}, compiled during the Engishiki period, records the shrine as “Afuri Shrine” in its 5th year ([[:en:927|927]]) and classifies it as a minor shrine among the thirteen shrines of the {{ill|Engishiki-shiki Naishinsha Jūsansha|ja|延喜式内社十三社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki-shiki Naishinsha Jūsansha|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} in [[:en:Sagami Province|Sagami Province]]. == Enshrined Deities == * The primary deity enshrined at the lower shrine is {{ill|Ōyamatsumi|ja|大山祇神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōyamatsumi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to オオヤマツミ}} (Ōyamatsumi-no-kami). * The main shrine enshrines {{ill|Ōyamatsumi|ja|大山祇神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōyamatsumi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to オオヤマツミ}} as its principal deity (prior to the Shinto-Buddhism separation, he was revered as {{ill|Sekison Daigongen|ja|石尊大権現|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sekison Daigongen|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 石尊権現|1=Sekison Gongen|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q55528104}}). * The subsidiary shrine (oku-sha) enshrines {{ill|Raijin|ja|大雷神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Raijin|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (Ōi-katsuchi-no-kami; known as {{ill|Ōtengu|ja|大天狗|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōtengu|1=daitengu|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q10934709}} during the syncretic period). * The subsidiary shrine (zen-sha) enshrines {{ill|Takaokami|ja|高龗神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takaokami|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 淤加美神|1=Kuraokami|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q644201}} (Takaokami; known as {{ill|Kotenko|ja|小天狗|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kotenko|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 烏天狗|1=karasu tengu|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q863869}} during the syncretic period). This arrangement—enshrining Ōyamatsumi along with the subsidiary deities Raijin and Takaokami—is identical to that of the shrine in [[:en:Ehime Prefecture|Ehime Prefecture]] known as [[:en:Ōyamazumi Shrine|Ōyamazumi Shrine]], although these deities were enshrined only after the separation of Shinto and Buddhism in the Meiji period. During the Edo period, when Shinto and Buddhism were syncretized, the main shrine originally enshrined {{ill|Sekison Daigongen|ja|石尊大権現|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sekison Daigongen|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 石尊権現|1=Sekison Gongen|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q55528104}}, as the sacred stone ({{ill|Reisekki|ja|霊石|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Reisekki|1=Reisekki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q23998630}}) at the summit served as his manifestation. In the subsidiary shrines, {{ill|Ōtengu|ja|大天狗|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōtengu|1=daitengu|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q10934709}} was enshrined in the oku-sha and {{ill|Kotenko|ja|小天狗|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kotenko|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 烏天狗|1=karasu tengu|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q863869}} in the zen-sha. == Cultural Importance == === Oyama Pilgrimage === During the Edo period the Oyama Pilgrimage was a tradition where worshippers formed groups ("{{ill|Kō (lecture)|lt=Kō|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kō (lecture)|qq=}}") to visit the shrine. This pilgrimage, coupled with the "Oyama Kaido" pathway played a role in shaping culture by inspiring rakugo stories and ukiyo e artworks. In 2008 this pilgrimage was designated as a Heritage Site due to its cultural significance. === Osamedachi Tradition === A tradition stemming from a tale about Minamoto no Yoritomo offering a sword to the shrine the Osamedachi custom involves presenting swords that can reach lengths of up to 6 meters. === Kagura Dance === Imported from Kasuga Taisha Shrine during the Meiji era the Kagura dance performed at Oyama Afuri Shrine includes dances by boys (Yamato Mai) and girls (Miko dance) spanning age groups, from elementary school students to adults. The Sendoshi Ryokan originally built to host worshippers has transformed into an inn that provides lodging and dining services. It stands as one of the temple accommodations, in Japan. As for the Oyama Noh tradition it reflects the shrines commitment to peace and harmony tracing its origins back, to the Genroku era. This tradition signifies the bond established among the leaders of Mt. Oyama through their embrace of Noh performances. == Access == === To the Lower Shrine === ; Public Transportation * From the north exit of the [[:en:Odakyū Odawara Line|Odakyu Odawara Line]] at It is a [[Beppyo Shrine]], or a shrine that is particularly notable in a certain way with a significant history to it.{{Cite web|title=Learn about Oyama Afuri Shrine - Oyama Afuri Shrine|url=https://www.afuri.or.jp/en/about/|access-date=2024-03-29|language=en-US}}{{Cite web|date=2023-12-28|title=Oyama Afuri Shrine|url=https://www.afuri.or.jp/en/|access-date=2024-03-29|language=en-US}}{{Cite web|date=2013-04-07|title=Afuri Shrine on Mt. Oyama - Kanagawa|url=https://en.japantravel.com/kanagawa/afuri-shrine-on-mt-oyama/4043|access-date=2024-03-29|website=JapanTravel|language=en}} '''{{ill|Oyama Afuri Shrine|ja|大山阿夫利神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Oyama Afuri Shrine|1=Ōyama Afuri Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11434713}}''' (Oyama Afuri Jinja) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in [[:en:Isehara, Kanagawa|Isehara City]], [[:en:Kanagawa Prefecture|Kanagawa Prefecture]], situated on [[:en:大山|Oyama]] (also known as '''Amefuri-yama'''〈{{ill|Amefuri-yama|ja|雨降山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amefuri-yama|1=Amefuri-yama|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11659780}}〉). It is recorded in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=}} from the [[:en:Engishiki|Engishiki]] period (Enchō 5, [[:en:927|927]]) as one of the thirteen shrines (small shrines) of the {{ill|Engishiki-shiki Naishinsha Jūsansha|ja|延喜式内社十三社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki-shiki Naishinsha Jūsansha|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} in [[:en:Sagami Province|Sagami Province]]. Under the [[:en:Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines]], it was classified as a prefectural shrine (Ken-sha) and is currently designated as a [[Beppyo Shrine|Beppyo shrine]] by the [[:en:Association of Shinto Shrines|Association of Shinto Shrines]]. The shrine is composed of two parts: the main shrine (honsha), which includes the inner shrine (okusha) and the front shrine (zensha) located at the summit of Oyama, and the lower shrine (gesha) located on the mid-slope.[http://www.afuri.or.jp/about/map/]{{ill|About Oyama Afuri Shrine|ja|大山阿夫利神社について：境内のご案内|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/About Oyama Afuri Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (Official site of Oyama Afuri Shrine). The lower shrine is accessible via the {{ill|Oyama Cable Car|ja|大山ケーブルカー|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Oyama Cable Car|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大山観光電鉄大山鋼索線|1=Ōyama Cable Car|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q864604}} operated by {{ill|Oyama Kankō Dentetsu|ja|大山観光電鉄|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Oyama Kankō Dentetsu|1=Ōyama Kankō Dentetsu|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11434695}}. == History == [[File:Pilgrims at the Roben waterfall, Oyama.jpg|thumb|left|245px|“Ōyama Sekison Raben-taki no Zu” by [[:en:Utagawa Kuniyoshi|Utagawa Kuniyoshi]] (Art name: Ichiyūsai), painted circa 1819–1820 (Bunsei 2–3). Men praying at the waterfall of Ōyama Sekison (current Oyama Afuri Shrine).]] [[:en:大山|Oyama]] has long been revered as an object of mountain worship. Excavations at its summit have uncovered [[:en:Jōmon pottery|Jomon pottery]] used in rituals.[http://www.afuri.or.jp/about/]{{ill|About Oyama Afuri Shrine|ja|大山阿夫利神社について|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/About Oyama Afuri Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (Official site of Oyama Afuri Shrine) It is also known as “{{ill|Amefuri-yama|ja|雨降山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amefuri-yama|1=Amefuri-yama|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11659780}}” because clouds and mist frequently gather at the summit, which are believed to bring rain, and it was revered as a rain-making deity. In addition, worship of a giant stone ([[:en:Iwakura rock|Iwa-za]]) at the summit and of the twin waterfalls on the mountainside as sacred water sources is also observed.{{ill|Toshio Hōga|ja|宝賀寿男|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toshio Hōga|qq=}}, “Section 3: The Early Branches of Clans in Kinai and Tōkoku – Part 2: Musashi no Kuni no Kunizukuri and the Provincial Clans of Tōkoku”, in “Studies on Ancient Clans, No. 16: The Rise and Fall of the Izumo Kingdom” (青垣出版, 2020), pp.263–264. According to tradition, Ōyama Afuri Shrine was founded during the reign of [[:en:Emperor Sujin|Sujin-tennō]] (around the 3rd century BC, though this is considered legendary rather than historical). The {{ill|Engishiki-shiki Shinnamōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki-shiki Shinnamōchō|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=}}, compiled during the Engishiki period, records the shrine as “Afuri Shrine” in its 5th year ([[:en:927|927]]) and classifies it as a minor shrine among the thirteen shrines of the {{ill|Engishiki-shiki Naishinsha Jūsansha|ja|延喜式内社十三社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki-shiki Naishinsha Jūsansha|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} in [[:en:Sagami Province|Sagami Province]]. == Enshrined Deities == * The primary deity enshrined at the lower shrine is {{ill|Ōyamatsumi|ja|大山祇神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōyamatsumi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to オオヤマツミ}} (Ōyamatsumi-no-kami). * The main shrine enshrines {{ill|Ōyamatsumi|ja|大山祇神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōyamatsumi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to オオヤマツミ}} as its principal deity (prior to the Shinto-Buddhism separation, he was revered as {{ill|Sekison Daigongen|ja|石尊大権現|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sekison Daigongen|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 石尊権現|1=Sekison Gongen|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q55528104}}). * The subsidiary shrine (oku-sha) enshrines {{ill|Raijin|ja|大雷神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Raijin|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (Ōi-katsuchi-no-kami; known as {{ill|Ōtengu|ja|大天狗|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōtengu|1=daitengu|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q10934709}} during the syncretic period). * The subsidiary shrine (zen-sha) enshrines {{ill|Takaokami|ja|高龗神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takaokami|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 淤加美神|1=Kuraokami|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q644201}} (Takaokami; known as {{ill|Kotenko|ja|小天狗|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kotenko|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 烏天狗|1=karasu tengu|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q863869}} during the syncretic period). This arrangement—enshrining Ōyamatsumi along with the subsidiary deities Raijin and Takaokami—is identical to that of the shrine in [[:en:Ehime Prefecture|Ehime Prefecture]] known as [[:en:Ōyamazumi Shrine|Ōyamazumi Shrine]], although these deities were enshrined only after the separation of Shinto and Buddhism in the Meiji period. During the Edo period, when Shinto and Buddhism were syncretized, the main shrine originally enshrined {{ill|Sekison Daigongen|ja|石尊大権現|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sekison Daigongen|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 石尊権現|1=Sekison Gongen|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q55528104}}, as the sacred stone ({{ill|Reisekki|ja|霊石|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Reisekki|1=Reisekki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q23998630}}) at the summit served as his manifestation. In the subsidiary shrines, {{ill|Ōtengu|ja|大天狗|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōtengu|1=daitengu|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q10934709}} was enshrined in the oku-sha and {{ill|Kotenko|ja|小天狗|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kotenko|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 烏天狗|1=karasu tengu|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q863869}} in the zen-sha. == Cultural Importance == === Oyama Pilgrimage === During the Edo period the Oyama Pilgrimage was a tradition where worshippers formed groups ("{{ill|Kō (lecture)|lt=Kō|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kō (lecture)|qq=}}") to visit the shrine. This pilgrimage, coupled with the "Oyama Kaido" pathway played a role in shaping culture by inspiring rakugo stories and ukiyo e artworks. In 2008 this pilgrimage was designated as a Heritage Site due to its cultural significance. === Osamedachi Tradition === A tradition stemming from a tale about Minamoto no Yoritomo offering a sword to the shrine the Osamedachi custom involves presenting swords that can reach lengths of up to 6 meters. === Kagura Dance === Imported from Kasuga Taisha Shrine during the Meiji era the Kagura dance performed at Oyama Afuri Shrine includes dances by boys (Yamato Mai) and girls (Miko dance) spanning age groups, from elementary school students to adults. The Sendoshi Ryokan originally built to host worshippers has transformed into an inn that provides lodging and dining services. It stands as one of the temple accommodations, in Japan. As for the Oyama Noh tradition it reflects the shrines commitment to peace and harmony tracing its origins back, to the Genroku era. This tradition signifies the bond established among the leaders of Mt. Oyama through their embrace of Noh performances. == Access == === To the Lower Shrine === ; Public Transportation * From the north exit of the [[:en:Odakyū Odawara Line|Odakyu Odawara Line]] at [[:en:Isehara Station|Isehara Station]], take Bus Route 10 operated by {{ill|Kanagawa Chūō Kōtsū|ja|神奈川中央交通西|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kanagawa Chūō Kōtsū|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 神奈川中央交通|1=Kanagawa Chuo Kotsu|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q10854960}}, alight at the final stop ("Ōyama Cable" bound), which takes approximately 25 minutes. *** Then walk about 15 minutes (approximately 600 meters) from the Ōyama Cable Car Station. ; By Car * Accessible via the [[:en:Shin-Tōmei Expressway|Shin-Tōmei Expressway]] at the {{ill|Isehara Ōyama Interchange|ja|伊勢原大山インターチェンジ|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Isehara Ōyama Interchange|1=Isehara oyama interchange|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11378953}}, then via {{ill|Kanagawa Prefectural Road 611|ja|神奈川県道611号大山板戸線|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kanagawa Prefectural Road 611|1=Kanagawa Prefectural Road Route 611|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11589328}}; municipal parking is available (about a 15-minute walk from the parking lot to the Ōyama Cable Car Station). === To the Main Shrine === * Ascend the mountain from the lower shrine (approximately 90 [[:en:Beppyo shrine|Beppyo Shrine]] |創建 = Tradition: During the reign of [[:en:Emperor Sujin|Sujin-tennō]] (circa BC 97–BC 30) |例祭 = July 27 |地図 = {{Location map+|Japan Kanagawa|width=210|float=center|caption=|places= {{Location map~|Japan Kanagawa|lat_deg=35|lat_min=26|lat_sec=26|lon_deg=139|lon_min=13|lon_sec=51.8|position=top|label=[[:en:Corporate headquarters|Main Shrine]]|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20}} {{Location map~|Japan Kanagawa|lat_deg=35|lat_min=25|lat_sec=54.7|lon_deg=139|lon_min=14|lon_sec=16.6|position=right|label={{ill|Lower Shrine|ja|下社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Lower Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20}}|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| image=大山阿夫利神社 下社拝殿.jpg}} {{OSM Location map|coord={{coord|35.436187|N|139.234166|E}}|fullscreen-option=1|zoom=14|float=center|width=200|caption=|title=|mark-coord1={{coord|35|26|26|N|139|13|51.8|E}}|label1=[[:en:Corporate headquarters|Main Shrine]]|label-pos1=right|mark-size1=8|mark-coord2={{coord|35|25|54.7|N|139|14|16.6|E}}|label2={{ill|Lower Shrine|ja|下社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Lower Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}|label-pos2=top|mark-size2=8}} |prefecture = {{ill|Isehara|WD=Q734520}} |coordinates = {{Coord|35.420861|N|139.256861|E|region:JP_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} |deity = {{ill|Sekison Gongen|WD=Q55528104}}; {{ill|Ōyamatsumi|WD=Q386563}} }} {{osm box|w|161550990}} [[File:大山道.png|thumb|right|260px|{{ill|Oyama-dō|ja|大山道|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Oyama-dō|1=Ōyamadō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11434707}} (Main 8 Routes)]] {{ill|Oyama Afuri Shrine|ja|%E5%A4%A7%E5%B1%B1%E9%98%BF%E5%A4%AB%E5%88%A9%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE|1=Ōyama Afuri Shrine|2=ja|3=大山阿夫利神社|WD=Q11434713|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Oyama Afuri Shrine|qq=}} (大山阿夫利神社) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in Isehara City, Kanagawa Prefecture, [[:en:Japan|Japan]]. It is a [[Beppyo Shrine]], or a shrine that is particularly notable in a certain way with a significant history to it.{{Cite web|title=Learn about Oyama Afuri Shrine - Oyama Afuri Shrine|url=https://www.afuri.or.jp/en/about/|access-date=2024-03-29|language=en-US}}{{Cite web|date=2023-12-28|title=Oyama Afuri Shrine|url=https://www.afuri.or.jp/en/|access-date=2024-03-29|language=en-US}}{{Cite web|date=2013-04-07|title=Afuri Shrine on Mt. Oyama - Kanagawa|url=https://en.japantravel.com/kanagawa/afuri-shrine-on-mt-oyama/4043|access-date=2024-03-29|website=JapanTravel|language=en}} '''{{ill|Oyama Afuri Shrine|ja|大山阿夫利神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Oyama Afuri Shrine|1=Ōyama Afuri Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11434713}}''' (Oyama Afuri Jinja) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in [[:en:Isehara, Kanagawa|Isehara City]], [[:en:Kanagawa Prefecture|Kanagawa Prefecture]], situated on [[:en:大山|Oyama]] (also known as '''Amefuri-yama'''〈{{ill|Amefuri-yama|ja|雨降山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amefuri-yama|1=Amefuri-yama|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11659780}}〉). It is recorded in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=}} from the [[:en:Engishiki|Engishiki]] period (Enchō 5, [[:en:927|927]]) as one of the thirteen shrines (small shrines) of the {{ill|Engishiki-shiki Naishinsha Jūsansha|ja|延喜式内社十三社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki-shiki Naishinsha Jūsansha|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} in [[:en:Sagami Province|Sagami Province]]. Under the [[:en:Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines]], it was classified as a prefectural shrine (Ken-sha) and is currently designated as a [[Beppyo Shrine|Beppyo shrine]] by the [[:en:Association of Shinto Shrines|Association of Shinto Shrines]]. The shrine is composed of two parts: the main shrine (honsha), which includes the inner shrine (okusha) and the front shrine (zensha) located at the summit of Oyama, and the lower shrine (gesha) located on the mid-slope.[http://www.afuri.or.jp/about/map/]{{ill|About Oyama Afuri Shrine|ja|大山阿夫利神社について：境内のご案内|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/About Oyama Afuri Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (Official site of Oyama Afuri Shrine). The lower shrine is accessible via the {{ill|Oyama Cable Car|ja|大山ケーブルカー|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Oyama Cable Car|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大山観光電鉄大山鋼索線|1=Ōyama Cable Car|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q864604}} operated by {{ill|Oyama Kankō Dentetsu|ja|大山観光電鉄|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Oyama Kankō Dentetsu|1=Ōyama Kankō Dentetsu|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11434695}}. == History == [[File:Pilgrims at the Roben waterfall, Oyama.jpg|thumb|left|245px|“Ōyama Sekison Raben-taki no Zu” by [[:en:Utagawa Kuniyoshi|Utagawa Kuniyoshi]] (Art name: Ichiyūsai), painted circa 1819–1820 (Bunsei 2–3). Men praying at the waterfall of Ōyama Sekison (current Oyama Afuri Shrine).]] [[:en:大山|Oyama]] has long been revered as an object of mountain worship. Excavations at its summit have uncovered [[:en:Jōmon pottery|Jomon pottery]] used in rituals.[http://www.afuri.or.jp/about/]{{ill|About Oyama Afuri Shrine|ja|大山阿夫利神社について|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/About Oyama Afuri Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (Official site of Oyama Afuri Shrine) It is also known as “{{ill|Amefuri-yama|ja|雨降山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amefuri-yama|1=Amefuri-yama|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11659780}}” because clouds and mist frequently gather at the summit, which are believed to bring rain, and it was revered as a rain-making deity. In addition, worship of a giant stone ([[:en:Iwakura rock|Iwa-za]]) at the summit and of the twin waterfalls on the mountainside as sacred water sources is also observed.{{ill|Toshio Hōga|ja|宝賀寿男|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toshio Hōga|qq=}}, “Section 3: The Early Branches of Clans in Kinai and Tōkoku – Part 2: Musashi no Kuni no Kunizukuri and the Provincial Clans of Tōkoku”, in “Studies on Ancient Clans, No. 16: The Rise and Fall of the Izumo Kingdom” (青垣出版, 2020), pp.263–264. According to tradition, Ōyama Afuri Shrine was founded during the reign of [[:en:Emperor Sujin|Sujin-tennō]] (around the 3rd century BC, though this is considered legendary rather than historical). The {{ill|Engishiki-shiki Shinnamōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki-shiki Shinnamōchō|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=}}, compiled during the Engishiki period, records the shrine as “Afuri Shrine” in its 5th year ([[:en:927|927]]) and classifies it as a minor shrine among the thirteen shrines of the {{ill|Engishiki-shiki Naishinsha Jūsansha|ja|延喜式内社十三社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki-shiki Naishinsha Jūsansha|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} in [[:en:Sagami Province|Sagami Province]]. == Enshrined Deities == * The primary deity enshrined at the lower shrine is {{ill|Ōyamatsumi|ja|大山祇神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōyamatsumi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to オオヤマツミ}} (Ōyamatsumi-no-kami). * The main shrine enshrines {{ill|Ōyamatsumi|ja|大山祇神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōyamatsumi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to オオヤマツミ}} as its principal deity (prior to the Shinto-Buddhism separation, he was revered as {{ill|Sekison Daigongen|ja|石尊大権現|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sekison Daigongen|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 石尊権現|1=Sekison Gongen|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q55528104}}). * The subsidiary shrine (oku-sha) enshrines {{ill|Raijin|ja|大雷神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Raijin|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (Ōi-katsuchi-no-kami; known as {{ill|Ōtengu|ja|大天狗|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōtengu|1=daitengu|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q10934709}} during the syncretic period). * The subsidiary shrine (zen-sha) enshrines {{ill|Takaokami|ja|高龗神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takaokami|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 淤加美神|1=Kuraokami|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q644201}} (Takaokami; known as {{ill|Kotenko|ja|小天狗|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kotenko|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 烏天狗|1=karasu tengu|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q863869}} during the syncretic period). This arrangement—enshrining Ōyamatsumi along with the subsidiary deities Raijin and Takaokami—is identical to that of the shrine in [[:en:Ehime Prefecture|Ehime Prefecture]] known as [[:en:Ōyamazumi Shrine|Ōyamazumi Shrine]], although these deities were enshrined only after the separation of Shinto and Buddhism in the Meiji period. During the Edo period, when Shinto and Buddhism were syncretized, the main shrine originally enshrined {{ill|Sekison Daigongen|ja|石尊大権現|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sekison Daigongen|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 石尊権現|1=Sekison Gongen|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q55528104}}, as the sacred stone ({{ill|Reisekki|ja|霊石|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Reisekki|1=Reisekki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q23998630}}) at the summit served as his manifestation. In the subsidiary shrines, {{ill|Ōtengu|ja|大天狗|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōtengu|1=daitengu|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q10934709}} was enshrined in the oku-sha and {{ill|Kotenko|ja|小天狗|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kotenko|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 烏天狗|1=karasu tengu|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q863869}} in the zen-sha. == Cultural Importance == === Oyama Pilgrimage === During the Edo period the Oyama Pilgrimage was a tradition where worshippers formed groups ("{{ill|Kō (lecture)|lt=Kō|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kō (lecture)|qq=}}") to visit the shrine. This pilgrimage, coupled with the "Oyama Kaido" pathway played a role in shaping culture by inspiring rakugo stories and ukiyo e artworks. In 2008 this pilgrimage was designated as a Heritage Site due to its cultural significance. === Osamedachi Tradition === A tradition stemming from a tale about Minamoto no Yoritomo offering a sword to the shrine the Osamedachi custom involves presenting swords that can reach lengths of up to 6 meters. === Kagura Dance === Imported from Kasuga Taisha Shrine during the Meiji era the Kagura dance performed at Oyama Afuri Shrine includes dances by boys (Yamato Mai) and girls (Miko dance) spanning age groups, from elementary school students to adults. The Sendoshi Ryokan originally built to host worshippers has transformed into an inn that provides lodging and dining services. It stands as one of the temple accommodations, in Japan. As for the Oyama Noh tradition it reflects the shrines commitment to peace and harmony tracing its origins back, to the Genroku era. This tradition signifies the bond established among the leaders of Mt. Oyama through their embrace of Noh performances. == Access == === To the Lower Shrine === ; Public Transportation * From the north exit of the [[:en:Odakyū Odawara Line|Odakyu Odawara Line]] at [[:en:Isehara Station|Isehara Station]], take Bus Route 10 operated by {{ill|Kanagawa Chūō Kōtsū|ja|神奈川中央交通西|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kanagawa Chūō Kōtsū|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 神奈川中央交通|1=Kanagawa Chuo Kotsu|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q10854960}}, alight at the final stop ("Ōyama Cable" bound), which takes approximately 25 minutes. *** Then walk about 15 minutes (approximately 600 meters) from the Ōyama Cable Car Station. ; By Car * Accessible via the [[:en:Shin-Tōmei Expressway|Shin-Tōmei Expressway]] at the {{ill|Isehara Ōyama Interchange|ja|伊勢原大山インターチェンジ|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Isehara Ōyama Interchange|1=Isehara oyama interchange|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11378953}}, then via {{ill|Kanagawa Prefectural Road 611|ja|神奈川県道611号大山板戸線|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kanagawa Prefectural Road 611|1=Kanagawa Prefectural Road Route 611|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11589328}}; municipal parking is available (about a 15-minute walk from the parking lot to the Ōyama Cable Car Station). === To the Main Shrine === * Ascend the mountain from the lower shrine (approximately 90 It is a [[Beppyo Shrine]], or a shrine that is particularly notable in a certain way with a significant history to it.{{Cite web|title=Learn about Oyama Afuri Shrine - Oyama Afuri Shrine|url=https://www.afuri.or.jp/en/about/|access-date=2024-03-29|language=en-US}}{{Cite web|date=2023-12-28|title=Oyama Afuri Shrine|url=https://www.afuri.or.jp/en/|access-date=2024-03-29|language=en-US}}{{Cite web|date=2013-04-07|title=Afuri Shrine on Mt. Oyama - Kanagawa|url=https://en.japantravel.com/kanagawa/afuri-shrine-on-mt-oyama/4043|access-date=2024-03-29|website=JapanTravel|language=en}} '''{{ill|Oyama Afuri Shrine|ja|大山阿夫利神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Oyama Afuri Shrine|1=Ōyama Afuri Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11434713}}''' (Oyama Afuri Jinja) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in [[:en:Isehara, Kanagawa|Isehara City]], [[:en:Kanagawa Prefecture|Kanagawa Prefecture]], situated on [[:en:大山|Oyama]] (also known as '''Amefuri-yama'''〈{{ill|Amefuri-yama|ja|雨降山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amefuri-yama|1=Amefuri-yama|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11659780}}〉). It is recorded in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=}} from the [[:en:Engishiki|Engishiki]] period (Enchō 5, [[:en:927|927]]) as one of the thirteen shrines (small shrines) of the {{ill|Engishiki-shiki Naishinsha Jūsansha|ja|延喜式内社十三社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki-shiki Naishinsha Jūsansha|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} in [[:en:Sagami Province|Sagami Province]]. Under the [[:en:Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines]], it was classified as a prefectural shrine (Ken-sha) and is currently designated as a [[Beppyo Shrine|Beppyo shrine]] by the [[:en:Association of Shinto Shrines|Association of Shinto Shrines]]. The shrine is composed of two parts: the main shrine (honsha), which includes the inner shrine (okusha) and the front shrine (zensha) located at the summit of Oyama, and the lower shrine (gesha) located on the mid-slope.[http://www.afuri.or.jp/about/map/]{{ill|About Oyama Afuri Shrine|ja|大山阿夫利神社について：境内のご案内|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/About Oyama Afuri Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (Official site of Oyama Afuri Shrine). The lower shrine is accessible via the {{ill|Oyama Cable Car|ja|大山ケーブルカー|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Oyama Cable Car|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大山観光電鉄大山鋼索線|1=Ōyama Cable Car|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q864604}} operated by {{ill|Oyama Kankō Dentetsu|ja|大山観光電鉄|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Oyama Kankō Dentetsu|1=Ōyama Kankō Dentetsu|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11434695}}. == History == [[File:Pilgrims at the Roben waterfall, Oyama.jpg|thumb|left|245px|“Ōyama Sekison Raben-taki no Zu” by [[:en:Utagawa Kuniyoshi|Utagawa Kuniyoshi]] (Art name: Ichiyūsai), painted circa 1819–1820 (Bunsei 2–3). Men praying at the waterfall of Ōyama Sekison (current Oyama Afuri Shrine).]] [[:en:大山|Oyama]] has long been revered as an object of mountain worship. Excavations at its summit have uncovered [[:en:Jōmon pottery|Jomon pottery]] used in rituals.[http://www.afuri.or.jp/about/]{{ill|About Oyama Afuri Shrine|ja|大山阿夫利神社について|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/About Oyama Afuri Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (Official site of Oyama Afuri Shrine) It is also known as “{{ill|Amefuri-yama|ja|雨降山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amefuri-yama|1=Amefuri-yama|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11659780}}” because clouds and mist frequently gather at the summit, which are believed to bring rain, and it was revered as a rain-making deity. In addition, worship of a giant stone ([[:en:Iwakura rock|Iwa-za]]) at the summit and of the twin waterfalls on the mountainside as sacred water sources is also observed.{{ill|Toshio Hōga|ja|宝賀寿男|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toshio Hōga|qq=}}, “Section 3: The Early Branches of Clans in Kinai and Tōkoku – Part 2: Musashi no Kuni no Kunizukuri and the Provincial Clans of Tōkoku”, in “Studies on Ancient Clans, No. 16: The Rise and Fall of the Izumo Kingdom” (青垣出版, 2020), pp.263–264. According to tradition, Ōyama Afuri Shrine was founded during the reign of [[:en:Emperor Sujin|Sujin-tennō]] (around the 3rd century BC, though this is considered legendary rather than historical). The {{ill|Engishiki-shiki Shinnamōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki-shiki Shinnamōchō|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=}}, compiled during the Engishiki period, records the shrine as “Afuri Shrine” in its 5th year ([[:en:927|927]]) and classifies it as a minor shrine among the thirteen shrines of the {{ill|Engishiki-shiki Naishinsha Jūsansha|ja|延喜式内社十三社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki-shiki Naishinsha Jūsansha|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} in [[:en:Sagami Province|Sagami Province]]. == Enshrined Deities == * The primary deity enshrined at the lower shrine is {{ill|Ōyamatsumi|ja|大山祇神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōyamatsumi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to オオヤマツミ}} (Ōyamatsumi-no-kami). * The main shrine enshrines {{ill|Ōyamatsumi|ja|大山祇神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōyamatsumi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to オオヤマツミ}} as its principal deity (prior to the Shinto-Buddhism separation, he was revered as {{ill|Sekison Daigongen|ja|石尊大権現|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sekison Daigongen|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 石尊権現|1=Sekison Gongen|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q55528104}}). * The subsidiary shrine (oku-sha) enshrines {{ill|Raijin|ja|大雷神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Raijin|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (Ōi-katsuchi-no-kami; known as {{ill|Ōtengu|ja|大天狗|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōtengu|1=daitengu|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q10934709}} during the syncretic period). * The subsidiary shrine (zen-sha) enshrines {{ill|Takaokami|ja|高龗神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takaokami|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 淤加美神|1=Kuraokami|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q644201}} (Takaokami; known as {{ill|Kotenko|ja|小天狗|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kotenko|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 烏天狗|1=karasu tengu|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q863869}} during the syncretic period). This arrangement—enshrining Ōyamatsumi along with the subsidiary deities Raijin and Takaokami—is identical to that of the shrine in [[:en:Ehime Prefecture|Ehime Prefecture]] known as [[:en:Ōyamazumi Shrine|Ōyamazumi Shrine]], although these deities were enshrined only after the separation of Shinto and Buddhism in the Meiji period. During the Edo period, when Shinto and Buddhism were syncretized, the main shrine originally enshrined {{ill|Sekison Daigongen|ja|石尊大権現|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sekison Daigongen|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 石尊権現|1=Sekison Gongen|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q55528104}}, as the sacred stone ({{ill|Reisekki|ja|霊石|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Reisekki|1=Reisekki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q23998630}}) at the summit served as his manifestation. In the subsidiary shrines, {{ill|Ōtengu|ja|大天狗|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōtengu|1=daitengu|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q10934709}} was enshrined in the oku-sha and {{ill|Kotenko|ja|小天狗|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kotenko|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 烏天狗|1=karasu tengu|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q863869}} in the zen-sha. == Cultural Importance == === Oyama Pilgrimage === During the Edo period the Oyama Pilgrimage was a tradition where worshippers formed groups ("{{ill|Kō (lecture)|lt=Kō|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kō (lecture)|qq=}}") to visit the shrine. This pilgrimage, coupled with the "Oyama Kaido" pathway played a role in shaping culture by inspiring rakugo stories and ukiyo e artworks. In 2008 this pilgrimage was designated as a Heritage Site due to its cultural significance. === Osamedachi Tradition === A tradition stemming from a tale about Minamoto no Yoritomo offering a sword to the shrine the Osamedachi custom involves presenting swords that can reach lengths of up to 6 meters. === Kagura Dance === Imported from Kasuga Taisha Shrine during the Meiji era the Kagura dance performed at Oyama Afuri Shrine includes dances by boys (Yamato Mai) and girls (Miko dance) spanning age groups, from elementary school students to adults. The Sendoshi Ryokan originally built to host worshippers has transformed into an inn that provides lodging and dining services. It stands as one of the temple accommodations, in Japan. As for the Oyama Noh tradition it reflects the shrines commitment to peace and harmony tracing its origins back, to the Genroku era. This tradition signifies the bond established among the leaders of Mt. Oyama through their embrace of Noh performances. == Access == === To the Lower Shrine === ; Public Transportation * From the north exit of the [[:en:Odakyū Odawara Line|Odakyu Odawara Line]] at 神奈川中央交通|1=Kanagawa Chuo Kotsu|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q10854960}}, alight at the final stop ("Ōyama Cable" bound), which takes approximately 25 minutes. *** Then walk about 15 It is a [[Beppyo Shrine]], or a shrine that is particularly notable in a certain way with a significant history to it.{{Cite web|title=Learn about Oyama Afuri Shrine - Oyama Afuri Shrine|url=https://www.afuri.or.jp/en/about/|access-date=2024-03-29|language=en-US}}{{Cite web|date=2023-12-28|title=Oyama Afuri Shrine|url=https://www.afuri.or.jp/en/|access-date=2024-03-29|language=en-US}}{{Cite web|date=2013-04-07|title=Afuri Shrine on Mt. Oyama - Kanagawa|url=https://en.japantravel.com/kanagawa/afuri-shrine-on-mt-oyama/4043|access-date=2024-03-29|website=JapanTravel|language=en}} '''{{ill|Oyama Afuri Shrine|ja|大山阿夫利神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Oyama Afuri Shrine|1=Ōyama Afuri Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11434713}}''' (Oyama Afuri Jinja) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in [[:en:Isehara, Kanagawa|Isehara City]], [[:en:Kanagawa Prefecture|Kanagawa Prefecture]], situated on [[:en:大山|Oyama]] (also known as '''Amefuri-yama'''〈{{ill|Amefuri-yama|ja|雨降山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amefuri-yama|1=Amefuri-yama|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11659780}}〉). It is recorded in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=}} from the [[:en:Engishiki|Engishiki]] period (Enchō 5, [[:en:927|927]]) as one of the thirteen shrines (small shrines) of the {{ill|Engishiki-shiki Naishinsha Jūsansha|ja|延喜式内社十三社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki-shiki Naishinsha Jūsansha|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} in [[:en:Sagami Province|Sagami Province]]. Under the [[:en:Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines]], it was classified as a prefectural shrine (Ken-sha) and is currently designated as a [[Beppyo Shrine|Beppyo shrine]] by the [[:en:Association of Shinto Shrines|Association of Shinto Shrines]]. The shrine is composed of two parts: the main shrine (honsha), which includes the inner shrine (okusha) and the front shrine (zensha) located at the summit of Oyama, and the lower shrine (gesha) located on the mid-slope.[http://www.afuri.or.jp/about/map/]{{ill|About Oyama Afuri Shrine|ja|大山阿夫利神社について：境内のご案内|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/About Oyama Afuri Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (Official site of Oyama Afuri Shrine). The lower shrine is accessible via the {{ill|Oyama Cable Car|ja|大山ケーブルカー|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Oyama Cable Car|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大山観光電鉄大山鋼索線|1=Ōyama Cable Car|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q864604}} operated by {{ill|Oyama Kankō Dentetsu|ja|大山観光電鉄|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Oyama Kankō Dentetsu|1=Ōyama Kankō Dentetsu|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11434695}}. == History == [[File:Pilgrims at the Roben waterfall, Oyama.jpg|thumb|left|245px|“Ōyama Sekison Raben-taki no Zu” by [[:en:Utagawa Kuniyoshi|Utagawa Kuniyoshi]] (Art name: Ichiyūsai), painted circa 1819–1820 (Bunsei 2–3). Men praying at the waterfall of Ōyama Sekison (current Oyama Afuri Shrine).]] [[:en:大山|Oyama]] has long been revered as an object of mountain worship. Excavations at its summit have uncovered [[:en:Jōmon pottery|Jomon pottery]] used in rituals.[http://www.afuri.or.jp/about/]{{ill|About Oyama Afuri Shrine|ja|大山阿夫利神社について|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/About Oyama Afuri Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (Official site of Oyama Afuri Shrine) It is also known as “{{ill|Amefuri-yama|ja|雨降山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amefuri-yama|1=Amefuri-yama|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11659780}}” because clouds and mist frequently gather at the summit, which are believed to bring rain, and it was revered as a rain-making deity. In addition, worship of a giant stone ([[:en:Iwakura rock|Iwa-za]]) at the summit and of the twin waterfalls on the mountainside as sacred water sources is also observed.{{ill|Toshio Hōga|ja|宝賀寿男|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toshio Hōga|qq=}}, “Section 3: The Early Branches of Clans in Kinai and Tōkoku – Part 2: Musashi no Kuni no Kunizukuri and the Provincial Clans of Tōkoku”, in “Studies on Ancient Clans, No. 16: The Rise and Fall of the Izumo Kingdom” (青垣出版, 2020), pp.263–264. According to tradition, Ōyama Afuri Shrine was founded during the reign of [[:en:Emperor Sujin|Sujin-tennō]] (around the 3rd century BC, though this is considered legendary rather than historical). The {{ill|Engishiki-shiki Shinnamōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki-shiki Shinnamōchō|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=}}, compiled during the Engishiki period, records the shrine as “Afuri Shrine” in its 5th year ([[:en:927|927]]) and classifies it as a minor shrine among the thirteen shrines of the {{ill|Engishiki-shiki Naishinsha Jūsansha|ja|延喜式内社十三社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki-shiki Naishinsha Jūsansha|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} in [[:en:Sagami Province|Sagami Province]]. == Enshrined Deities == * The primary deity enshrined at the lower shrine is {{ill|Ōyamatsumi|ja|大山祇神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōyamatsumi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to オオヤマツミ}} (Ōyamatsumi-no-kami). * The main shrine enshrines {{ill|Ōyamatsumi|ja|大山祇神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōyamatsumi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to オオヤマツミ}} as its principal deity (prior to the Shinto-Buddhism separation, he was revered as {{ill|Sekison Daigongen|ja|石尊大権現|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sekison Daigongen|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 石尊権現|1=Sekison Gongen|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q55528104}}). * The subsidiary shrine (oku-sha) enshrines {{ill|Raijin|ja|大雷神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Raijin|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (Ōi-katsuchi-no-kami; known as {{ill|Ōtengu|ja|大天狗|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōtengu|1=daitengu|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q10934709}} during the syncretic period). * The subsidiary shrine (zen-sha) enshrines {{ill|Takaokami|ja|高龗神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takaokami|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 淤加美神|1=Kuraokami|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q644201}} (Takaokami; known as {{ill|Kotenko|ja|小天狗|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kotenko|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 烏天狗|1=karasu tengu|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q863869}} during the syncretic period). This arrangement—enshrining Ōyamatsumi along with the subsidiary deities Raijin and Takaokami—is identical to that of the shrine in [[:en:Ehime Prefecture|Ehime Prefecture]] known as [[:en:Ōyamazumi Shrine|Ōyamazumi Shrine]], although these deities were enshrined only after the separation of Shinto and Buddhism in the Meiji period. During the Edo period, when Shinto and Buddhism were syncretized, the main shrine originally enshrined {{ill|Sekison Daigongen|ja|石尊大権現|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sekison Daigongen|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 石尊権現|1=Sekison Gongen|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q55528104}}, as the sacred stone ({{ill|Reisekki|ja|霊石|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Reisekki|1=Reisekki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q23998630}}) at the summit served as his manifestation. In the subsidiary shrines, {{ill|Ōtengu|ja|大天狗|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōtengu|1=daitengu|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q10934709}} was enshrined in the oku-sha and {{ill|Kotenko|ja|小天狗|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kotenko|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 烏天狗|1=karasu tengu|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q863869}} in the zen-sha. == Cultural Importance == === Oyama Pilgrimage === During the Edo period the Oyama Pilgrimage was a tradition where worshippers formed groups ("{{ill|Kō (lecture)|lt=Kō|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kō (lecture)|qq=}}") to visit the shrine. This pilgrimage, coupled with the "Oyama Kaido" pathway played a role in shaping culture by inspiring rakugo stories and ukiyo e artworks. In 2008 this pilgrimage was designated as a Heritage Site due to its cultural significance. === Osamedachi Tradition === A tradition stemming from a tale about Minamoto no Yoritomo offering a sword to the shrine the Osamedachi custom involves presenting swords that can reach lengths of up to 6 meters. === Kagura Dance === Imported from Kasuga Taisha Shrine during the Meiji era the Kagura dance performed at Oyama Afuri Shrine includes dances by boys (Yamato Mai) and girls (Miko dance) spanning age groups, from elementary school students to adults. The Sendoshi Ryokan originally built to host worshippers has transformed into an inn that provides lodging and dining services. It stands as one of the temple accommodations, in Japan. As for the Oyama Noh tradition it reflects the shrines commitment to peace and harmony tracing its origins back, to the Genroku era. This tradition signifies the bond established among the leaders of Mt. Oyama through their embrace of Noh performances. == Access == === To the Lower Shrine === ; Public Transportation * From the north exit of the [[:en:Odakyū Odawara Line|Odakyu Odawara Line]] at [[:en:Isehara Station|Isehara Station]], take Bus Route 10 operated by {{ill|Kanagawa Chūō Kōtsū|ja|神奈川中央交通西|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kanagawa Chūō Kōtsū|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 神奈川中央交通|1=Kanagawa Chuo Kotsu|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q10854960}}, alight at the final stop ("Ōyama Cable" bound), which takes approximately 25 minutes. *** Then walk about 15 minutes (approximately 600 meters) from the Ōyama Cable Car Station. ; By Car * Accessible via the [[:en:Shin-Tōmei Expressway|Shin-Tōmei Expressway]] at the {{ill|Isehara Ōyama Interchange|ja|伊勢原大山インターチェンジ|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Isehara Ōyama Interchange|1=Isehara oyama interchange|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11378953}}, then via {{ill|Kanagawa municipal parking is available (about a 15-minute walk from the parking lot to the Ōyama Cable Car Station). === To the Main Shrine === * Ascend the mountain from the lower shrine (approximately 90
